score_notes.cs_foundations: Requires CS 111/201/202/208/251/252/254/257 including computability and complexity theory, but no confirmed operating-systems or compilers requirement [CA-S4].
score_notes.math_foundations: Only MATH 111 is required; linear algebra (MATH 232) and STAT 120 are advisory recommendations for graduate-bound students [CA-S4].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: Verified AI offerings are CS 320 ML, CS 322 NLP, CS 321 (not run 2025-26), CS 327 Robotics (not run 2024-25); no intro-AI, deep-learning, or computer-vision course confirmed [CA-S4][CA-S9].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: Depth beyond CS 320/322 depends on CS 294/394 Directed Research rather than a course sequence [CA-S4].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: DGAH 220 Creative Coding and Generative AI is catalog-eligible but did not run in 2025-26; no LLM, agents, or AI-safety course found [CA-S4].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: The 72-credit major leaves substantial room in a 33-major, 39-minor college, and CS 294/394 Directed Research runs every term [CA-S1][CA-S4].
score_notes.course_availability: CS 320 and CS 322 ran in both 2024-25 and 2025-26, but CS 321, CS 311, and CS 327 each skipped a year [CA-S4][CA-S9].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: Paid CS research at $580/week with a published application cycle, plus a Summer Science Fellowship restricted to first- and second-years offering two summers of support [CA-S10][CA-S11].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: Fourteen named CS faculty supervise CS 294/394 every term with no graduate students competing, and summer projects list 1-2 students per named professor [CA-S4][CA-S15].
score_notes.project_based_learning: CS 400 comps is a required faculty-specified team project with 21 consecutive archived years, but no makerspace or hardware lab was found [CA-S4][CA-S22].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: No robotics degree or minor; 1 undergrad robotics course. No research labs, 1 competition team.
score_notes.computing_resources: Seven Olin Hall labs with two research-dedicated rooms and Linux via x2go; GPU hardware is implied only by a 2025 NVIDIA GPU research project, with no cluster page found [CA-S14][CA-S15].
score_notes.industry_preparation: 77% of the Class of 2025 was employed with Microsoft, Epic Systems, MEDITECH, and Walmart Global Tech among top employers, but no CS-specific placement or salary data is published [CA-S33].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: Ranked 6th nationally at 18% doctoral attainment for 2013-2022 doctorates and 6th by NSF S&E yield ratio (14.7, 768 recipients 2010-20) [CA-S29][CA-S30].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: No graduate programs exist, so no accelerated master's pathway is possible [CA-S3][CA-S4].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: CS is the most popular major with 147 declarations across two classes, and the college ranks 3rd among 556 baccalaureate colleges in doctoral production [CA-S7][CA-S32].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: Three independent accounts converge on collaborative, non-competitive intensity, while also reporting real workload strain and probable grade deflation on the 10-week term [CA-S8][CA-S34][CA-S35].
score_notes.student_agency: Directed research every term plus off-campus research funding through Kolenkow-Reitz for work with non-Carleton faculty [CA-S4][CA-S12].
score_notes.community_within_scale: About 2,086 students with four departmental CS student groups and departmental newsletters/mailing lists as explicit on-ramps [CA-S1][CA-S23].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: Four officially listed CS groups including a Hack4Impact 501(c)(3) chapter recruiting with "no prior experience required," but no active hackathon or robotics team verified [CA-S23][CA-S24][CA-S26].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: Listed activities span jazz band, symphony, musical theater, film society, and Model UN, but the source is an aggregator and participation data is unpublished [CA-S38].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: Greek participation is 0% and social life runs on townhouse gatherings, club sports, and traditions like Rottblatt and Sproncert, though the student paper calls it "a grassroots effort" [CA-S35][CA-S36].
score_notes.campus_engagement: Fully residential small-town campus with named all-college traditions and in-town Campus Go service limited to non-entertainment trips [CA-S17][CA-S36].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: An 80,000 sq ft rec center with a 200-meter indoor track, 5,300 sq ft fitness center, four courts, two pools, and a 30-ft climbing wall, entered by OneCard [CA-S39][CA-S40][CA-S41].
score_notes.daily_life: Scheduled daily bus service to MSP and Mall of America at $15-$35 each way plus Zipcar on campus, offset by Minnesota winters [CA-S16][CA-S44].

why_us_ammunition: Carleton's CS major is unusually systems-and-theory complete for a college with no engineering school: required core spans Data Structures, Mathematics of CS, Computer Systems, Programming Languages, Algorithms, Computability & Complexity, and Software Design [CARL-S4].

Robotics and AI exist as real coursework, not just interest groups: CS 327 Introduction to Robotics is offered as a junior seminar, alongside CS 320 Machine Learning, CS 321 Making Decisions with AI, CS 322 Natural Language Processing, CS 344 Human-Computer Interaction and CS 361 Artificial Life & Digital Evolution [CARL-S4][CARL-S5].

Every CS major finishes with a team capstone — CS 399 Senior Seminar plus CS 400 Integrative Exercise, where small student teams design and build a faculty-specified project — which maps directly onto an FRC-style team-build background [CARL-S4].

Faculty-directed research is a formal course: CS 294/394 Directed Research in Computer Science has students work on a faculty member's research project with the long-run goal of "dissemination to a scholarly community beyond Carleton" [CARL-S5].

For a student who wants a licensed engineering path, Carleton runs a 3-2 engineering program with published CS-major course schedules, so 'no engineering school' has an institutional answer [CARL-S7].

robotics_curriculum_detail.score_basis: Carleton College has no engineering department or robotics program; robotics exists only inside the Computer Science department. Exactly one robotics course is published: CS 327 Introduction to Robotics, a junior seminar covering kinematics, sensors and perception, path planning, and control with mobile-robot deployment, offered Spring 2026 with CS 200/201, MATH 134/232, and CS 202/236 prerequisites [CARL-R1]. CS 220 Art, Interactivity, and Microcontrollers (cross-listed ARTS 220) is a microcontroller/interactive-construction course rather than a robotics course, and the non-seminar version is not offered in 2025-26 [CARL-R1]. CS 321 Making Decisions with Artificial Intelligence uses a search-and-rescue robot only as an example application and is not offered in 2025-26 [CARL-R1]. The catalog page states explicitly that there is no robotics degree or program and no computer engineering program; students interested in hardware are pointed to physics electronics courses [CARL-R1]. One to two robotics courses offered on rotation = 2.

admissions.admit_rate_note_note: CMU's CDS does not publish an in-state vs out-of-state admit split.
admissions.major_admit_context: CMU admits by college and by program, and the spread is enormous. In CMU's own publication, the School of Computer Science 'now turns away almost 95 percent of those who apply': in the cited year 6,756 students applied to SCS and only 350 were admitted, 'a rate of less than 5.2 percent. ... Compare that to the 19 percent acceptance rate for CMU's other seven undergraduate programs' [CMU-S5]. Testing requirements also differ by college for the most recently published cycle: SCS requires the SAT or ACT, the College of Fine Arts is test-optional, and the College of Engineering, Dietrich, Heinz Information Systems, Mellon College of Science and Tepper are 'test flexible' — applicants must submit some standardized evidence (SAT, ACT, IB, AP, Cambridge A-Level or French Baccalaureate) [CMU-S4]. The College of Engineering admits directly to a department/major unless the applicant selects undecided [CMU-S6]. Early Decision is materially easier: 553 admits from 2,680 ED applicants (20.6%) versus 11.07% overall [CMU-S1]. Robotics at the undergraduate level is a minor rather than a major — the Robotics Institute offers 'masters programs and an undergraduate minor for Carnegie Mellon students' [CMU-S8].
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 Early Action = No, and CMU states plainly: 'Carnegie Mellon does not offer early action.'
admissions.pct_submitting_sat_note: 1,182 enrolled first-years submitted SAT scores (65.5%); 327 submitted ACT (18.1%).
admissions.gpa_note: CDS C12 average high school GPA 3.89, reported for 99.7% of enrolled first-years; CDS C10 shows 82.5% in the top tenth of their high school class.
admissions.test_policy_note: CDS C8 marks SAT/ACT 'Consider if Submitted' for the Fall 2027 cycle, which reads as test-optional. However CMU's own testing pages describe a by-college policy for Fall 2026 — SAT/ACT required for the School of Computer Science, test-optional for the College of Fine Arts, and 'test flexible' for Engineering, Dietrich, Heinz Information Systems, MCS and Tepper. CMU has not published a Fall-2027-specific statement, so an SCS applicant should assume a test requirement until CMU posts the 2027 policy.

why_us_ammunition: The Robotics Institute 'was established in 1979 to conduct basic and applied research in robotics technologies' and founded 'the world's first Robotics PhD program' in 1989 — the deepest institutional robotics lineage available to cite [CMU-S8].

RI facilities span roughly 100,000 sq ft on the Pittsburgh campus plus another 100,000 sq ft at the National Robotics Engineering Center in Lawrenceville, so an applicant can point to specific research infrastructure [CMU-S8].
Undergraduates engage robotics through an RI undergraduate minor rather than a major — an honest, well-informed applicant should frame robotics as a minor layered on an SCS or CIT major [CMU-S8].
The College of Engineering admits directly to a department, so a Why-Us essay can and should argue for a specific department rather than the university in general [CMU-S6].

CMU's own reporting that SCS 'turns away almost 95 percent' of applicants versus roughly 19 percent for its other undergraduate programs is useful for explaining a considered college choice within CMU [CMU-S5].

admissions.admit_rate_note_reason: Cornell publishes no in-state/out-of-state admit-rate split in CDS Section C (it does mark state residency as 'Considered' in C7).
admissions.major_admit_context: Cornell applicants "apply directly to one of our undergraduate colleges and schools" rather than to the university at large [CORNELL-S2], and the college-specific supplemental essays differ sharply — Duffield Engineering asks two 200-word essays including "engineering is the application of math, science, and technology to solve complex problems. Why do you want to study engineering?", while Arts & Sciences asks a single 650-word intellectual-passion essay [CORNELL-S3][CORNELL-S4]. Despite this college-by-college process, the CDS reports only one university-wide funnel (72,523 / 6,077) and one ED funnel (10,057 / 1,889), so the effective ED bar for the College of Engineering is not published as a separate rate — applicants must treat the ED CoE bar as unpublished rather than assume it matches the 18.78% university-wide ED rate [CORNELL-S1].
admissions.ed2_note: Cornell offers no ED II; CDS C21 shows a single ED round (closing Nov 1, notification mid-December) [CORNELL-S1].
admissions.ea_note: Cornell does not offer Early Action; CDS C22 = No [CORNELL-S1].
admissions.gpa_note_reason: Cornell leaves CDS C11/C12 (GPA distribution and average HS GPA) blank. It does report class rank: 84% of rank-submitting enrollees were in the top tenth of their class (12.2% submitted rank) [CORNELL-S1].

why_us_ammunition: Robotics@Cornell is a cross-college umbrella spanning "autonomy, design, perception, control, learning, planning, multi robot systems, and human-robot interaction," and it publishes dedicated undergraduate resources including a robotics minor and project-team information — an applicant can name the minor by name [CORNELL-S5].

The Cornell Bowers CS department's robotics research area works with "aerial robots, home robots, assistive robots, autonomous cars, humanoids, legged robots, and modular robots," which lets an applicant tie a specific FRC/robotics background to a specific subarea [CORNELL-S6].

Named labs give concrete essay anchors: the EmPRISE Lab describes itself as "a full-stack robotics lab leveraging tools from sensing, perception, planning, learning, and control," with work in human-robot interaction, haptic perception, manipulation and tactile sensing [CORNELL-S7].

Duffield's ECE research groups include the Laboratory for Intelligent Systems and Controls (learning, control and computational intelligence for autonomous systems) and the Collective Embodied Intelligence Lab (large robot collectives inspired by social insects) — useful for a swarm/multi-robot pitch [CORNELL-S9].

Because you apply to one college, the Duffield prompts ('Why do you want to study engineering?' / 'Why Duffield?') reward naming the exact lab, minor, or cross-listed course sequence rather than generic Cornell praise [CORNELL-S3].

why_us_ammunition: Bass Connections year-long interdisciplinary project teams are open to all current Duke undergraduates, typically run 9-12 months with 5-15 undergraduate and graduate students plus at least two faculty leaders, meet weekly, and carry ~12 hours/week and academic credit — a concrete vehicle for an AI/robotics applicant to name a specific team and theme [DUKE-S5][DUKE-S8].

Pratt's undergraduate research pipeline is explicit and early: experiential learning begins in the first semester, faculty labs post undergraduate openings in the Muser system across three recruiting rounds per year, first- and second-year students can take an EGR independent study as a free elective, and the Pratt Research Fellows Program supports three semesters of immersive research [DUKE-S4].

Duke Robotics sits in Pratt: undergraduate courses in robotics and autonomy are offered through Mechanical Engineering & Materials Science, and many students take robotics projects as their senior design capstone or as independent study with robotics faculty [DUKE-S7].

Duke's surgical-robotics ecosystem (the NSF-funded Traineeship in the Advancement of Surgical Technologies) shows a research direction an applicant interested in AI plus medical robotics can point to as a long-term goal [DUKE-S7].

Because Duke publishes no separate Trinity vs. Pratt admit rate and the 'Why Duke' essay explicitly asks how you will engage with Trinity or Pratt, naming the specific school and a named lab/team is the highest-leverage move available [DUKE-S1][DUKE-S3].

admissions.admit_rate_note: CDS 2024-25 (Fall 2024) C1: 73,557 first-year applicants, 17,804 admitted, 7,513 enrolled = 24.20% [UF-S1]. UF publishes a residency breakdown and it is remarkably residency-neutral: in-state 39,022 applied / 9,294 admitted = 23.8%; OUT-OF-STATE 29,376 applied / 6,834 admitted = 23.3%; international 5,159 / 1,676 = 32.5% [UF-S1]. So unlike UT Austin (top-6% auto-admit crowd-out) or UW (2% non-resident DTM-CS), UF admits out-of-state applicants at essentially the same rate as Floridians — 29,376 OOS applications is a large, seriously-reviewed pool. UF also has no waiting-list policy per C2 ('Do you have a policy of placing students on a waiting list? No') [UF-S1], although the deadlines page does mention Waitlist and PaCE/Pathways outcomes for Regular Decision [UF-S2] — flag as CONFLICTING between the 2024-25 CDS and the current deadlines page; the current admissions page is the better guide for the Fall 2027 cycle.
admissions.major_admit_context: UF DOES NOT ADMIT BY MAJOR — this directly CORRECTS the brief. UF Admissions states verbatim: 'The University of Florida does not admit by major, so Early Decision is binding regardless of outcome through the College of the Arts audition process' [UF-S3]. Applicants are admitted to the university, and access to competitive majors is controlled AFTER matriculation by CRITICAL TRACKING, a published per-semester progression standard. The brief's 2.5 / 2.8 figures are correct but they are critical-tracking thresholds, not admission thresholds, and the direction is confirmed: CS is the more forgiving path and ME is HARDER. Verified thresholds: (a) CS in the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences requires a 2.5 GPA across all critical-tracking courses (checked from semester 4 onward) plus a 2.0 UF GPA every semester, tracking MAC 1147/2311, MAC 2312, MAC 2313, PHY 2053/2048 series, COP 3502C/3504C, COP 3503C, COT 3100, COP 3530, COP 4600 [UF-S6]. (b) CS in the Herbert Wertheim College of Engineering requires a 2.5 GPA across a group of SIX critical-tracking courses (MAC 2311, MAC 2312, MAC 2313, COP 3502C, PHY 2048, PHY 2049), each completed with a minimum grade of C within TWO ATTEMPTS, on a 1/1/2/1/all-six semester schedule, plus 2.0 UF GPA [UF-S7]. (c) MECHANICAL ENGINEERING requires a 2.8 GPA across a group of EIGHT critical-tracking courses (CHM 2045/2095, EML 2023, MAC 2311, MAC 2312, MAC 2313, MAP 2302, PHY 2048, PHY 2049), each with a minimum grade of C within two attempts, two courses per semester across semesters 1-4, plus 2.0 UF GPA [UF-S8]. ME additionally enforces departmental probation: 'An aerospace or mechanical engineering student whose cumulative, upper-division or department grade point average falls below a 2.0 or who does not meet critical tracking requirements will be placed on academic probation,' with a maximum of two probation terms and possible dismissal from the department [UF-S8]. STRATEGIC CONSEQUENCE: at UF the admissions bar is university-level and OOS-neutral, but the ME major carries a 2.8 tracking GPA and a two-attempts-per-course rule that is unforgiving of a weak first-year calculus/physics run — the real risk at UF is post-admission, and a robotics applicant choosing ME should plan first-year course load accordingly. Note also the ED consequence of not admitting by major: because there is no major-contingent outcome, UF's binding ED gives no major-access advantage, only a timing/odds advantage.
admissions.gpa_note: CDS 2024-25 C12: average high school GPA 3.92, with 94.00% of enrolled first-years reporting GPA; C11 distribution 53% at 4.0, 41% at 3.75-3.99, 6% at 3.50-3.74 and effectively ZERO below 3.50 [UF-S1] — the most top-compressed GPA distribution in this batch. Class rank (C10): 84% top tenth, 98% top quarter, 100% top half, 85% submitting rank [UF-S1]. Test detail from C9: 80% submitted SAT (n=5,908), 40% submitted ACT (n=2,952) — the highest submission rates in this batch, consistent with UF requiring tests; SAT composite 25/50/75 = 1330/1400/1470, EBRW 660/700/730, Math 660/700/750; ACT composite 29/31/33, ACT Math 26/29/32, ACT English 28/32/35 [UF-S1]. Score-range detail: 51.52% of enrolled scored 1400-1600 [UF-S1]. Application fee $30, waivable for financial need [UF-S1].
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: TEST REQUIRED. 'All applicants must submit test scores from the SAT, ACT and/or CLT' [UF-S4]. UF SUPERSCORES, and ACT Science is no longer required or counted [UF-S4]. Score deadline for EA/RD admits is May 1; transcripts July 1 [UF-S2]. UF also requires 16 academic units (4 English, 4 Math, 3 Natural Science, 3 Social Science, 2 sequential foreign language), a minimum C average in the academic core, and STARS (formerly SSAR — self-reported courses and grades entered in the Gator Portal) rather than an initial official transcript [UF-S4]. Along with UT Austin, UF is the reason a strong SAT retains full value in this applicant's portfolio.
admissions.c7_factors_note: CDS 2024-25 C7 [UF-S1]. Also marked: geographical residence = considered, state residency = considered, alumni relation = not_considered, religious affiliation = not_considered. UF is one of only two schools in this batch (with TAMU) marking BOTH extracurricular activities AND talent/ability as VERY IMPORTANT while marking RECOMMENDATIONS as NOT CONSIDERED — so at UF the applicant's own activity record and short answers carry the entire non-academic case, and there is no point chasing extra letters. Note the internal tension: UF requires test scores [UF-S4] but marks them only 'Important' in C7, below rigor/GPA/extracurriculars/talent.

interview.mechanism: No admissions interview for general admission (CDS marks Interview 'Not Considered' [UF-S1]). The only audition/interview-like process is the College of the Arts audition referenced in UF's Early Decision policy, which is irrelevant to an engineering/CS applicant [UF-S3].

first_frc_scholarship.note: NOT VERIFIABLE in this session. No FIRST/FRC-specific award appears on any UF admissions or College of Engineering page reviewed, and the FIRST provider list is behind the portal login [UF-S10]. Relevant published context instead: UF's ED deposit/confirmation timeline is Jan 8 for ED admits versus May 1 for EA/RD [UF-S2] and the $200 enrollment deposit applies [UF-S2] — i.e. binding ED at UF requires committing before comparing aid offers, which is the material trade-off for an out-of-state family. Do not assume Florida Bright Futures applies; it is a Florida-resident program.

decision_dates.restrictions: UF NOW HAS BINDING EARLY DECISION and it is CONFIRMED for the 2026-27 cycle (Fall 2027 entry) — the brief's flag is correct. Mechanics: ED application due Oct 15, supporting materials Oct 22, decision released DEC 11, 2026, and ED admits must confirm by JAN 8, 2027. ED is single-choice and binding, with the Common App ED agreement signed by student, parent/guardian AND school counselor. ED outcomes are limited to Admit / Defer (the applicant is RELEASED from the binding agreement when deferred) / Deny (no further review in the same cycle). Release requests are considered case-by-case at freshman@ufl.edu; change-of-plan requests (switching out of ED) must be submitted by Dec 10 at 5:00 pm EST [UF-S3][UF-S2]. Non-binding EARLY ACTION: apply Nov 1, materials Nov 8, decision Jan 22, 2027. REGULAR: apply Jan 15, materials Jan 22, decision MAR 19, 2027 (RD outcomes may include Waitlist or a Pathways/PaCE offer rather than a direct admit). EA and RD admits confirm by MAY 1 with a $200 deposit; test scores due May 1; final transcripts July 1 [UF-S2]. Because UF does not admit by major, ED at UF buys odds and certainty, NOT major access — and it forecloses aid comparison [UF-S3].

why_us_ammunition: Center for Intelligent Machines and Robotics (CIMAR) — UF's named robotics center, housed in the Department of Mechanical & Aerospace Engineering [UF-S9].

AFOSR Center of Excellence in Assured Autonomy in Contested Environments — an Air Force Office of Scientific Research Center of Excellence at UF MAE, i.e. federally funded autonomy research an undergraduate can point to concretely [UF-S9].

UF MAE's declared strategic initiatives explicitly lead with 'Autonomy & AI' (alongside Computational Engineering, Energy, Health, National Security, Sustainability, Security), plus the Warren B. Nelms Institute for the Connected World and an Institute for Computational Engineering [UF-S9].

The ME curriculum itself advertises advanced coursework in robotics, solid mechanics, thermal/fluid systems, dynamics and controls, and biomechanics, and the first six semesters are shared with aerospace engineering so a dual ME/AE degree needs only one extra semester [UF-S8].

Show critical-tracking literacy: naming the 2.8 eight-course ME tracking GPA (or the 2.5 six-course CS-in-Engineering standard) and the two-attempts-per-course rule demonstrates the applicant understands that UF's real selection happens in the first two years, not at admission [UF-S8][UF-S7].

decision_dates.restrictions: UF NOW HAS BINDING EARLY DECISION and it is CONFIRMED for the 2026-27 cycle (Fall 2027 entry) — the brief's flag is correct. Mechanics: ED application due Oct 15, supporting materials Oct 22, decision released DEC 11, 2026, and ED admits must confirm by JAN 8, 2027. ED is single-choice and binding, with the Common App ED agreement signed by student, parent/guardian AND school counselor. ED outcomes are limited to Admit / Defer (the applicant is RELEASED from the binding agreement when deferred) / Deny (no further review in the same cycle). Release requests are considered case-by-case at freshman@ufl.edu; change-of-plan requests (switching out of ED) must be submitted by Dec 10 at 5:00 pm EST [UF-S3][UF-S2]. Non-binding EARLY ACTION: apply Nov 1, materials Nov 8, decision Jan 22, 2027. REGULAR: apply Jan 15, materials Jan 22, decision MAR 19, 2027 (RD outcomes may include Waitlist or a Pathways/PaCE offer rather than a direct admit). EA and RD admits confirm by MAY 1 with a $200 deposit; test scores due May 1; final transcripts July 1 [UF-S2]. Because UF does not admit by major, ED at UF buys odds and certainty, NOT major access — and it forecloses aid comparison [UF-S3].

interview.mechanism: No admissions interview for general admission (CDS marks Interview 'Not Considered' [UF-S1]). The only audition/interview-like process is the College of the Arts audition referenced in UF's Early Decision policy, which is irrelevant to an engineering/CS applicant [UF-S3].

_raw.test_policy_2027_cycle: TEST REQUIRED. 'All applicants must submit test scores from the SAT, ACT and/or CLT' [UF-S4]. UF SUPERSCORES, and ACT Science is no longer required or counted [UF-S4]. Score deadline for EA/RD admits is May 1; transcripts July 1 [UF-S2]. UF also requires 16 academic units (4 English, 4 Math, 3 Natural Science, 3 Social Science, 2 sequential foreign language), a minimum C average in the academic core, and STARS (formerly SSAR — self-reported courses and grades entered in the Gator Portal) rather than an initial official transcript [UF-S4]. Along with UT Austin, UF is the reason a strong SAT retains full value in this applicant's portfolio.

supplemental_essays.prompt: Common App personal essay — required. 'Complete the Personal Essay question. The essay helps our admissions staff get to know you better. Use this space to tell us something about yourself that we wouldn't learn elsewhere in your application.'

UF does NOT publish the prompt texts or word limits on its official admissions pages; the prompts appear only inside the Common App UF supplement. The brief's '7 short answers historically' could NOT be confirmed from any official UF source in this session — treat the count and word limits as UNVERIFIED and check the live Common App supplement when it opens Aug 1, 2026.
Honors Program additional essay question — required only for Honors applicants; indicated on the Common App. ED applicants may also apply to the University Honors Program.

admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2025: 66,881 applicants, 8,921 admitted, 4,071 enrolled = 13.34% [GT-S1]. In-state (Georgia) 3,691/12,527 = 29.5%; out-of-state 4,513/44,596 = 10.1%; international 716/9,758 = 7.3% [GT-S1] (INFERRED - division of CDS C1 counts). Georgia Tech's own published Fall 2025 profile rounds these to 30% Georgia / 9% non-Georgia [GT-S10][GT-S11]; the Fall 2026 profile shows 67,985 applications, 8,715 admits, 28% Georgia / 9% non-Georgia, class goal 4,100 [GT-S9]. For a North Carolina resident the operative number is the ~9-10% non-resident rate, not the 13.3% headline.
admissions.major_admit_context: Georgia Tech admits by major, and the college you name on the Common App materially changes your odds. Institute-published profiles show only intended-area-of-study mix rather than per-college admit rates: 42% Engineering, 15% Computing, 22% Sciences, 7% Business, 8% Liberal Arts, 6% Design for the Fall 2026 admitted class [GT-S9] (Fall 2025: 44% Engineering, 16% Computing) [GT-S10]. The College of Computing states only that 'Competition remains high, with an admission rate for Computing that is lower than Georgia Tech's already low overall admission rate,' while disclosing that the Fall 2025 cycle drew 66,895 total applications including 13,711 for CS and Computational Media combined, that 1,547 first-year students were offered admission to CS or CM, and that CS alone accounted for 92.7% of College applicants [GT-S8]. That implies a CS+CM admit rate of roughly 11.3% (INFERRED - 1,547/13,711) [GT-S8], i.e. computing sits below the Institute-wide 13.3% [GT-S1]. The widely repeated figures of 8.5% for the College of Computing versus 13.1% for the College of Engineering could NOT be verified from any Georgia Tech source fetched on 2026-08-16 - treat them as unsourced. The second, larger constraint is mobility after admission: change of major into CS was suspended, and as of April 15, 2025 the College of Computing 'updated their change of major process based on semester of matriculation,' with separate rules for students who matriculated in summer 2024 or afterward; the department 'is now prepared to begin accepting Change of Major applications again on a limited basis, which includes students who would like to add Computer Science as a second major' [GT-S7][GT-S8]. Practical consequence: apply directly to the major you want (Computer Science, or a specific engineering major such as Mechanical Engineering); do not plan on entering through another major and switching. Note also that Georgia Tech's CDS marks 'state residency' as Very Important in the review [GT-S1], which is the single biggest structural headwind for a North Carolina applicant.
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: Georgia Tech does not offer Early Decision (CDS C21 = No) [GT-S1].
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 confirms a non-restrictive Early Action plan (closing 11/1, notification 1/31) but publishes no EA applicant/admit counts, and no Georgia Tech page fetched on 2026-08-16 published an EA2 admit rate [GT-S1][GT-S3]. The frequently cited 8.1% EA2 rate could not be verified from an official source.
admissions.test_detail_note: Fall 2025 enrolled: SAT submitted by 78% (3,181 students), ACT by 33% (1,348). SAT composite 25th/50th/75th = 1370/1460/1530; ACT 31/33/35 [GT-S1].
admissions.gpa_note: 95.85% of enrolled first-year students reported a weighted GPA of 4.0 or higher; average high school GPA 4.17 with 95.31% submitting GPA [GT-S1]. Class rank: 88.69% in the top tenth, 97.93% in the top quarter, though only 40.43% of enrollees submitted rank [GT-S1].
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: REQUIRED. CDS C8 for the 2025-2026 edition states SAT/ACT are 'Required to be considered for admission' for Fall 2027 [GT-S1], and the admissions site states 'All first-year applicants must submit results from at least one SAT and/or ACT in order to be considered for admission' [GT-S4]. Self-reported scores are accepted and recommended (Common App testing section or the post-submission portal form); scores on transcripts or sent by email/fax/mail are not used. ACT writing and the SAT optional essay are not required. Highest section scores are combined (English/Math/Reading for ACT; EBRW/Math for SAT). CLT scores may be self-reported but do not substitute for SAT/ACT [GT-S4]. Latest acceptable test date per CDS C8E: 23 January [GT-S1].
admissions.c7_note: Also from CDS C7: state residency Very Important; geographical residence Considered; alumni relation and religious affiliation Not Considered [GT-S1].

why_us_ammunition: Institute for Robotics and Intelligent Machines (IRIM) is Georgia Tech's cross-campus robotics institute whose mission is 'to ignite collaborations across Georgia Tech and beyond to imagine, design, and deploy robotic systems that enhance human capabilities to sense, think, and act' - a natural hook for a FIRST/robotics applicant [GT-S12].

Scale and selectivity of the computing pipeline is itself a talking point: 13,711 applications for CS and Computational Media in one cycle, with CS accounting for 92.7% of College of Computing applicants and 1,547 admits [GT-S8] - showing you understand what you are applying into strengthens a 'why this major' answer.

Georgia Tech's admitted-class mix (42% Engineering, 15% Computing in Fall 2026) means interdisciplinary robotics arguments that connect Mechanical Engineering and Computing land well with a reader [GT-S9].

Because change of major into CS is only reopening 'on a limited basis' [GT-S7], an essay that commits credibly to one named major (and explains why that specific curriculum) reads as informed rather than opportunistic.

State residency is Very Important in Georgia Tech's own review [GT-S1]; a non-Georgia applicant needs the essays and activity record to carry more weight, so lead with concrete robotics artifacts (build, code, competition outcomes) rather than generic enthusiasm.

score_notes.cs_foundations: Data structures (CS 331), algorithms (CS 430), discrete structures (CS 330), databases (CS 425) and software engineering (CS 487) are all required, but computer systems (CS 350/351) is elective-only and no theory-of-computation course appears in the degree [IIT-S1].
score_notes.math_foundations: 23 required math credits including MATH 251 Multivariate and Vector Calculus, MATH 332 Linear Algebra, and MATH 474 + MATH 476 probability and statistics [IIT-S1].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: CV (CS 512), deep learning (CS 577), NLP (CS 585), PGMs (CS 583), RL inside CS 580/CS 581, robotics (CS 582), IoT/edge (ECE 442) are all approved courses in the degree [IIT-S1][IIT-S2].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: Only one AI depth course (3 cr) plus 9 elective credits are required beyond CS 480/481/422; depth is opt-in rather than built in [IIT-S1].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: No dedicated generative-AI, LLM, or AI-agents course exists; transformers and deep generative models appear only as topics inside CS 577 [IIT-S2].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: 127 credits with a mandatory 15-credit outside minor, 21 humanities/social-science credits, 11 science credits and 6 IPRO credits leaves no unallocated free electives [IIT-S1].
score_notes.course_availability: Catalog eligibility is clear, but no term class schedule was reachable, so offering frequency and seat caps for CS 512/577/582/585 are unverified [IIT-S1][IIT-S2].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: SURE pays $550/week for 10 weeks plus free housing for CS/applied-math undergraduates but is competitive and U.S.-citizen/permanent-resident only, and the normal path to a lab is direct faculty email [IIT-S11][IIT-S41].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: 17:1 ratio and a small Ph.D. population (434 across the university) reduce competition, but no evidence of formal mentorship structures, listed undergraduate lab members, or undergraduate co-authorship was found [IIT-S20][IIT-S50].
score_notes.project_based_learning: Two required IPRO experiences (6 credits) on sponsor-facing cross-major teams, plus a staffed makerspace open for personal projects [IIT-S35][IIT-S14].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: ECE undergraduate track; 4 undergrad robotics courses. 6 labs, Autonomous Systems @ Illinois.
score_notes.computing_resources: The Ocient Computational Center is described as the CS department's compute backbone for AI and HPC, but no GPU inventory or undergraduate access policy is published [IIT-S19].
score_notes.industry_preparation: The Elevate Promise guarantees at least two experiential placements and offers tuition-free additional coursework if no job offer arrives within six months of graduation [IIT-S7][IIT-S8].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: Undergraduates can take up to a full slate of 500-level AI courses [IIT-S1], but there is no honors thesis, no published undergraduate publication record, and no published MS/PhD placement list [IIT-S34].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: Established Co-Terminal (AMP-CT) path: 60 credits + 3.0 GPA to apply, up to 9 shared credit hours, bachelor's + master's in as few as five years, undergraduate status and aid eligibility retained [IIT-S9][IIT-S47].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: Students across four independent threads consistently describe a "studious," academically focused campus, while also calling campus life quiet and city-dependent [IIT-S26][IIT-S27][IIT-S28][IIT-S60].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: No gated major, no capped seats, and graduate AI courses open by prerequisite mean there is no structural scarcity to compete over [IIT-S1][IIT-S2].
score_notes.student_agency: Students report it is "fairly easy to set up" a new club [IIT-S28] and the makerspace is open for "your own personal endeavor" [IIT-S14], but the 127-credit degree has zero free electives [IIT-S1].
score_notes.community_within_scale: Two-year residency requirement with dedicated first/second-year halls builds cohorts [IIT-S32], and students describe "tons of small circles" [IIT-S28], but ~20% of total enrollment is fully online and the graduate population exceeds the undergraduate one [IIT-S20][IIT-S62].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: ACM runs an annual Mock ICPC and a spring hackathon [IIT-S30] and Illinois Tech Robotics was officially profiled in April 2025 [IIT-S38], but the AI Student Association shows no activity evidence since its 2022 page date [IIT-S29].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: 150-plus organizations including a student-run radio station and esports [IIT-S33], plus Union Board concerts, an eight-lane campus bowling alley and a campus disc golf course [IIT-S61] — directory breadth verified, participation not.
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: Greek life is small (245 members, ~8% of bachelor's students) yet multiple students still say the scene is thin without it — "Campus life is dead unless you join a frat" and "around 4/10" [IIT-S22][IIT-S59][IIT-S26].
score_notes.campus_engagement: Students repeatedly describe weekends as time to "head into downtown Chicago," with one official student panel saying "our campus simply revolves around downtown Chicago" [IIT-S61][IIT-S26].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: Keating opens at 10:00 a.m. on weekdays, athletes have exclusive 6–10 a.m. access per a student report, and the main court closes for varsity practices and games [IIT-S24][IIT-S25].
score_notes.daily_life: Universal Ventra U-Pass, an on-campus Green Line station, Red Line and Metra within walking distance, and both airports reachable by train [IIT-S52][IIT-S53][IIT-S54].

admissions.cds_year_note: Illinois Tech's most recent published Common Data Set is the 2023-2024 edition; no 2024-2025 or 2025-2026 CDS was found on 2026-08-16 (the CDS index page returns HTTP 403 to programmatic fetches) [IIT-S1][IIT-S2]. All CDS-derived numbers below are therefore two cycles old - the oldest data in this batch.
admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2023 (CDS 2023-2024): 8,912 applicants, 4,939 admitted, 534 enrolled = 55.4% [IIT-S1]. In-state 2,233/3,676 = 60.7%; out-of-state 1,430/2,321 = 61.6%; international 1,188/2,726 = 43.6% [IIT-S1] (INFERRED - division of CDS C1 counts). Out-of-state applicants are admitted at essentially the same rate as Illinois residents, so residency is not a factor for a North Carolina applicant. Note the small entering class (534) relative to applications - yield is low and merit aid is the main lever.
admissions.major_admit_context: Illinois Tech admits directly to the major, and each program sets its own bar. The admissions office publishes recommended-GPA guidance by track rather than admit rates: the STEM track (all School of Engineering, Applied Science, and Health programs except Industrial Technology and Management, all School of Computing programs except IT and Management/Computer Information Systems, plus Finance, Biology, Chemistry, Physics and Food Science) has a recommended GPA range of 3.5-4.0+ with an average GPA of 4.12 among 2023 admits, while the Discover+/Tech+/Innovation and Society/Architecture track sits at 3.4-4.0+ with a 4.0 average [IIT-S5]. Review is holistic and explicitly weighs course level 'including math for more selective majors,' honors/AP/IB performance, the personal statement and activities [IIT-S4]. Applicants who miss their first-choice major are handled through an alternate-major process: for engineering and computing programs 'Illinois Tech typically requires a B or higher in math and science courses,' and reconsideration for a first-choice major in the School of Engineering, Applied Science, and Health or the School of Computing is possible with an updated mid-year or final transcript showing 'a B or higher in pre-calculus, calculus, or physics'; an ALEKS math placement score of 80 or above also figures in placement, and Architecture is called out as 'one of Illinois Tech's most selective academic programs' with a transfer-pathway fallback [IIT-S7]. No per-major admit rates are published. Practical consequence: name the exact major you want, keep pre-calculus/calculus/physics grades at B or higher, and know that reconsideration is a documented process rather than a favor - and that a 'Discover+' style admit is a real alternate outcome rather than a rejection.
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: CDS 2023-2024: 69 Early Decision applications, 47 admitted = 68.1% (INFERRED - division of CDS C21 counts) [IIT-S1]. ED volume is tiny, so the rate is noisy; the value of ED here is signaling and scholarship timing rather than a large statistical edge.
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 records Early Action closing 11/15 with notification 1/3 but publishes no EA applicant/admit counts [IIT-S1].
admissions.test_detail_note: Fall 2023 enrolled (CDS 2023-2024): SAT submitted by 45% (239 students), ACT by 11% (57). SAT composite 25th/50th/75th = 1190/1300/1400; ACT 25/28/31 [IIT-S1]. Lowest test band in this batch - a strong score is a differentiator for merit aid here.
admissions.gpa_note: CDS 2023-2024: 37.6% of enrolled first-year students reported a 4.0 GPA; average high school GPA 4.20 with 86.4% submitting [IIT-S1]. Class rank: 39% top tenth, 77% top quarter, 26% submitting rank [IIT-S1]. Admissions separately publishes recommended GPA ranges of 3.5-4.0+ for STEM majors and a 4.12 average for 2023 STEM admits [IIT-S5].
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: NOT REQUIRED (test-optional/test-blind by choice): 'Illinois Tech does not require standardized tests for undergraduate applicants,' a policy that 'applies to all first-year, transfer, and international applicants and all institutional scholarship considerations.' Students may submit scores or a letter of recommendation for consideration, but neither is required, and 'All students will be considered for institutional scholarships regardless.' Submitted official scores are superscored (SAT code 1318, ACT code 1040) [IIT-S4]. The page does not tie the policy to a specific entry year, so confirm for Fall 2027.
admissions.c7_note: From CDS 2023-2024 C7: only rigor of secondary school record and academic GPA are Very Important; everything else is Considered or Not Considered, and level of applicant's interest, first generation, alumni relation, geographical residence, state residency and religious affiliation are all Not Considered [IIT-S1]. Because this grid is two cycles old, treat it as directional.

why_us_ammunition: Illinois Tech runs a named FIRST pipeline - a $5,000/year, renewable, stackable robotics scholarship open to any major and triggered by your FRC/FTC Activities entry [IIT-S6] - the single most concrete robotics-to-institution link in this batch.

Chicago co-op and internship access is institutionalized through Elevate Experiences, whose employer directory lists 'organizations... who have actively recruited at Illinois Tech in the past year through career fairs, on-campus events, and more,' with postings flowing through Handshake [IIT-S8].
Small entering class (534 first-year enrollees) against 8,912 applications [IIT-S1] supports a 'small-cohort, high-access' argument - name specific labs or faculty rather than generic scale.

Direct-to-major admission with published, achievable academic guidance (STEM track recommended GPA 3.5-4.0+, average admit GPA 4.12) [IIT-S5] means your application can be targeted at one program from day one, with a documented reconsideration path if you are placed in an alternate major [IIT-S7].

The test-optional-by-policy stance covering 'all institutional scholarship considerations' [IIT-S4] means a robotics-heavy record and specific personal statement carry the scholarship weight - exactly where your profile is strongest.

robotics_curriculum_detail.score_basis: Undergraduate robotics teaching is real but thin relative to the research footprint. MMAE 440 Introduction to Robotics (kinematics/inverse kinematics, trajectory planning, dynamics, position control) is the one undergraduate course titled robotics [IIT-R1]. The ECE undergraduate track 'Artificial Intelligence, Robotics and Automation' adds ECE 438 Control Systems, ECE 481 Image Processing, and ECE 497 Special Problems on Robotics and Automation, and permits 500-level courses with advisor approval [IIT-R5]. The Minor in Electromechanical Design and Manufacturing is described as addressing industrial automation and robotics but publishes no course list on the fetched pages [IIT-R4]; the Minor in Electromechanical Systems is power-electronics focused, not robotics [IIT-R3]. Robotics depth sits mostly in graduate courses (MMAE 539 Robotic Motion Planning, MMAE 540 Robotics, MMAE 551 Experimental Mechatronics) and an MS in Autonomous Systems and Robotics [IIT-R2][IIT-R9]; undergraduate access to those requires permission, which is not documented as routine. That places this at 3-4 robotics courses = 3.

undergrad_courses.title: Special Problems on Robotics and Automation

robotics_curriculum_detail.minor_or_concentration: ECE undergraduate track 'Artificial Intelligence, Robotics and Automation' [IIT-R5]; Minor in Electromechanical Design and Manufacturing (5 courses, 17-20 credits; described as industrial automation and robotics, course list not published on fetched pages) [IIT-R4]
robotics_curriculum_detail.capstone: n.a. (no robotics-specific capstone documented on fetched pages; MMAE senior design and IPRO interprofessional projects exist but robotics linkage not confirmed)

robotics_access_detail.score_basis: ANCHOR CORRECTED UPWARD: Illinois Tech has substantially more robotics research than the anchor suggested. The Autonomous Systems @ Illinois Tech group publishes 6 faculty, 6 labs, and 20+ undergraduate and graduate students (NavLab UAV navigation, Autonomous Control Systems Lab for connected vehicles and robots, Wave Lab soft robots, Robotics Lab, Control Systems Lab, Space Weather Lab) [IIT-R7][IIT-R6]. The Robotics Lab@IIT (Prof. Matthew Spenko) runs externally funded work on electrostatic gecko-like adhesives for climbing/perching/manipulation (ONR, NASA), soft robots from boundary-constrained granular swarms (NSF EFRI), navigation integrity for self-driving cars, ubiquitous-robot urban policy (NSF NRI 2.0), and was an XPRIZE Rainforest finalist [IIT-R8]. The Nonsmooth Robotics Lab (Nelson Rosa) works on legged locomotion and biped robots [IIT-R10]. Held at 3 rather than 4 because this is a faculty group rather than a chartered robotics institute, it is fewer than 10 documented robotics labs, and no active robotics competition team could be confirmed on fetched pages.

score_notes.cs_foundations: 17 required core credits (Gateway, 601.220 Intermediate Programming, 601.226 Data Structures, 601.229 Computer System Fundamentals, 601.433 Intro Algorithms) at C+ or higher, plus a required discrete-math/theory option [JHU-S1].
score_notes.math_foundations: Only 16 math credits are required and linear algebra plus Calculus III are listed as recommended*, not required, even though they are hard prerequisites for 601.475 Machine Learning [JHU-S1][JHU-S2].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: The catalog lists 400-level undergraduate courses spanning AI, ML, learning theory, deep learning, RL, vision, NLP, robotics, causal inference, HCI and AI safety [JHU-S2].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: Every graduate AI course numbered 601.6xx has a 400-level undergraduate twin, so undergraduates reach graduate content directly (e.g., 601.482/682 Deep Learning) [JHU-S2].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: Named 400-level courses include Artificial Agents (601.470), NLP: Self-Supervised Models (601.471), AI Safety Alignment & Governance (601.469), Embodied AI with Web-Scale Video Data (601.460) and Generative Vision (601.483) [JHU-S2].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: Of 120 credits, about 64 are required in-field (40 CS + 16 math + 8 science) and only 12 upper-level CS credits are mandated, leaving large elective room [JHU-S1].
score_notes.course_availability: The Spring 2026 schedule confirms 601.464, 601.474 and 601.475 ran with meeting times, but no fetched page documents the rotation of newer electives such as 601.470 Artificial Agents [JHU-S5].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: Official participation claims range from 65% to over 90%, but an official HOUR deck states 80% of undergraduate researchers are entirely uncompensated volunteers [JHU-S13][JHU-S15][JHU-S38].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: The 9:1 student-faculty ratio and 22 new DSAI faculty hired in August 2025 expand capacity, but HOUR's own guidance is cold-email outreach with 3-4 follow-ups [JHU-S25][JHU-S8][JHU-S38].
score_notes.project_based_learning: Only one CSCI-TEAM course (3-4 credits) is required and it "may overlap with other requirements"; there is no single named senior capstone [JHU-S1].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: Robotics Minor; 13 undergrad robotics courses. 17 labs, LCSR, 1 competition team.
score_notes.computing_resources: Rockfish offers 45,072 cores and 32 A100/L40S GPU nodes, but accounts activate only after a PI with an approved allocation adds the user [JHU-S32][JHU-S33].
score_notes.industry_preparation: University-wide 91% are employed full-time or in graduate school within six months, but no CS-specific placement or salary data is published [JHU-S16][JHU-S1].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: 38% of graduates continue to graduate/professional school and the Senior Honors Thesis (601.519/520) unlocks extra research credit toward the major [JHU-S16][JHU-S1].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: Concurrent BS/MSE students receive a Dean's Master's Fellowship covering half of full-time tuition after four years at JHU, plus two double-counted courses under WSE policy [JHU-S17][JHU-S18].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: HopHacks runs every semester and its September 12-14, 2025 edition drew nearly 300 participants from 57 universities with a record 102 projects [JHU-S21].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: No current multi-source student evidence on competitiveness or pressure was collected, and the brief forbids inferring it from structure.
score_notes.student_agency: A CS major can declare via an SIS request plus an advisor-approved four-year plan, and can substitute a 600-level course for a 400-level one in the robotics minor without an exception form [JHU-S1][JHU-S3].
score_notes.community_within_scale: 5,679 full-time undergraduates with a mandatory two-year on-campus residency requirement and 93% of first-years in college housing [JHU-S25][JHU-S26].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: The CS department lists nine student groups including HopAI (the AI society), a Data Science Club, ACM with a Systems Programming subgroup, Cyberbirds, Game Dev Society and WiCS [JHU-S20].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: About 80% of students are involved in one or more student organization, but no full student-activities directory was fetched to verify breadth [JHU-S27].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: 25% of men and 21% of women join Greek organizations per the 2025-26 CDS, and the two-year residency requirement keeps underclass housing outside Greek control [JHU-S25][JHU-S26].
score_notes.campus_engagement: 93% of first-year students live on campus but only 46% of all undergraduates do, so most juniors and seniors live in surrounding neighborhoods [JHU-S25].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: The O'Connor Center is free to all Homewood students and includes a six-lane pool, climbing wall and bouldering cave, indoor track and three weight rooms, though it closes 3-4 weeks a year for maintenance [JHU-S29][JHU-S31].
score_notes.daily_life: A single contiguous Homewood campus with a two-year residency requirement, on-campus rec center at the North Gate, and off-campus housing within walking distance [JHU-S43][JHU-S28].

supplemental_essays.prompt: "At Johns Hopkins, community is built through dialogue, collaboration, and a willingness to engage across differences. Whether on campus or in the broader world, community depends on bridge builders who can listen to differing perspectives, challenge their own assumptions, or work together toward shared goals. Drawing on your own experiences, what have you learned about engaging across differences and how has it shaped the way you think about building bridges, enhancing community, and working with others?"

why_us_ammunition: The Laboratory for Computational Sensing and Robotics (LCSR) describes itself as "one of the most technologically advanced robotics research centers worldwide... an international leader in the areas of medical robotics, autonomous systems, and bio-inspiration" — the single strongest anchor for a robotics applicant's Hopkins essay [JHU-S4].

LCSR is deliberately cross-divisional, joining Whiting School engineers with researchers from the School of Medicine, Bloomberg School of Public Health, Krieger School of Arts & Sciences, the Applied Physics Laboratory and Kennedy Krieger Institute — a genuine 'only at Hopkins' structural fact [JHU-S4].

Named sub-labs let you be specific: PULSE (photoacoustic/ultrasound imaging with robots), HAMR (haptics and medical robotics), CIRL (computational interaction and robotics), LIMBS (locomotion in mechanical and biological systems), and MUSiiC (interventional ultrasound) [JHU-S5].

LCSR's faculty roster spans CS, mechanical engineering, ECE and clinical departments (e.g., Russell Taylor in computer-integrated interventional medicine; Axel Krieger's IMERSE lab on autonomous surgical robots; Iulian Iordachita's AMIRo lab on smart surgical tools) — useful for naming a specific mentor fit [JHU-S7][JHU-S8].

Because the 2026-27 supplement is a single 350-word community/bridge-building prompt rather than a 'why Hopkins' essay, robotics specifics should be woven into a collaboration narrative (e.g., FRC team dynamics) rather than listed as a program wish list [JHU-S3].

admissions.cds_note: Kettering University publishes no public Common Data Set — its library guides point only to an internal my.kettering.edu location. Every CDS-derived field below is therefore null, and the values that do exist come from Kettering's own admissions, scholarship and robotics pages.
admissions.overall_admit_rate_note: Not published on kettering.edu and no public CDS exists. Would need to be pulled from IPEDS directly.
admissions.major_admit_context: Kettering has no published major-level admission gate; review is squarely academic-record-based. Kettering states: 'Our application review centers on your preparedness for success at Kettering and includes consideration of your overall GPA, grade pattern, and selection of courses throughout high school' and 'Kettering does not have a fixed formula for admission' [KETT-S1]. Required high school coursework is unusually specific — two years of algebra, one year of geometry, a semester of trigonometry or equivalent, two years of lab science including chemistry or physics, and three years of English, with calculus/pre-calculus, CAD or engineering design, and computer science recommended [KETT-S1]. The distinctive structure is the co-op model and the A-section/B-section calendar rather than competitive major admission: orientation and move-in run on separate A-section (summer) and B-section (fall) tracks [KETT-S6]. For an FRC applicant the real 'major context' is financial and cultural — Kettering reports 'Awarding over $5.5 million in robotics scholarships since 1999' and hosts the Kettering University Robotics Center [KETT-S3].
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: Kettering publishes no Early Decision plan and no plan-level admit statistics.
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: Kettering has an Early Action priority date (November 15) but publishes no EA application or admit counts.
admissions.sat_mid50_note: No public CDS and no admitted-student score profile published on kettering.edu.
admissions.gpa_note: No numeric GPA profile is published. Kettering says only that it 'does not have a fixed formula for admission, however, we do seek students who exhibit a strong record of achievement', with review centered on overall GPA, grade pattern and course selection.
admissions.test_policy_note: Kettering's apply page lists 'standardized test results (optional)' among the materials, and Kettering states 'Kettering University is test-optional for all students. Students may submit SAT/ACT score(s) if they feel it will benefit their standing in the admissions review process. Students who choose not to submit standardized testing scores will not be negatively impacted during the review process.' Neither statement is stamped to a specific cycle, so Fall 2027 applicability is inferred.
admissions.c7_note: No public Common Data Set, so no C7 factor ratings exist for Kettering.
admissions.demonstrated_interest_note: Cannot be derived — no C7. Note that Kettering's robotics scholarship application does ask 'How did you first learn about Kettering University?', which is an interest-adjacent question inside the scholarship (not admission) process.

interview.mechanism: No admissions interview is required or published. Kettering invites applicants to 'get in touch with us at 810-762-9500 ext. 7865 if you would like to discuss your application with one of our admissions counselors', which is informational rather than evaluative. A spoken interview with a TESOL-trained instructor is required only for international applicants using the Duolingo English Test.

why_us_ammunition: Kettering reports 'Awarding over $5.5 million in robotics scholarships since 1999' — the most FRC-aligned funding history of any school in this set [KETT-S3].

The Kettering University Robotics Center is an active, externally funded hub: it received a $20,000 GM Community Impact Grant and Kettering received a $155,000 DENSO Foundation grant to expand an industrial robotic cell [KETT-S8][KETT-S9].

The alumni association funds the FRC pipeline itself, awarding $27,500 and $30,000 in sponsorships to high school robotics teams across FIRST, VEX and FTC — an applicant can position themselves as already part of that ecosystem [KETT-S10].
All first-year students receive a Kettering scholarship — 'yes, 100%' — alongside co-op earnings, which lets an applicant discuss affordability concretely [KETT-S4].
The co-op calendar (A-section and B-section tracks with alternating work terms) is the structural reason to choose Kettering and should anchor any Why-Us essay [KETT-S6].

robotics_curriculum_detail.score_basis: BS Engineering offers a 52-credit Robotic Systems concentration and a separate 52-credit Mechatronic Systems concentration, each with a fully published course list [KETT-R1][KETT-R2]. Robotics-specific and directly supporting courses include CE-442 Mobile Robotics, IME-408 Industrial Robotics, CE-452 AI for Autonomous Driving, CE-454 Computer Vision for Autonomous Driving, IME-412 Applied Control Systems Design, CE-426 Real-Time Embedded Systems, MECH-311 Mechatronics Systems Design and MECH-430/431 Dynamic Systems with Controls - covering mechanics, controls, and perception. Held at 4 rather than 5 because there is no dedicated robotics degree and the capstone (ENGR-490 Senior Multidisciplinary Engineering Design Project) is a general engineering design capstone, not a robotics capstone.

robotics_access_detail.score_basis: Kettering publishes 16 research facilities, of which several are robotics/autonomy relevant: Autonomous Driving and AI Laboratory, Autonomous and Connected Mobility (ACM) Lab, Mobile Systems and Vehicle Controls Lab, Intelligent Transportation Laboratory, Human Interfaces Ergonomics Laboratory, Research Engineering and Collaborative Haptics Lab, and the Kettering University GM Mobility Research Center [KETT-R3]. That is 'several robotics labs' plus active teams, not an institute and not 10+ documented robotics labs. Importantly, the Kettering Robotics Center is outreach infrastructure - it is the FIRST at Kettering / FIRST Community Center and publishes no faculty or lab roster [KETT-R4][KETT-R5]. Competition presence is real: the KUdos VEX U team (launched 2023, competed at the VEX World Championship) [KETT-R6], plus hosting duties for local FIRST teams [KETT-R5].

admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2025: 67,101 applicants, 30,218 admitted, 6,559 enrolled = 45.0% [UMD-S1]. In-state 8,075/18,487 = 43.7%; out-of-state 22,143/48,614 = 45.6% [UMD-S1] (INFERRED - division of CDS C1 counts). This is COUNTERINTUITIVE - UMD's reported out-of-state admit rate (45.6%) is slightly HIGHER than its in-state rate (43.7%) in the 2025-2026 CDS, the reverse of every other public in this batch; no UMD narrative page fetched on 2026-08-16 explains or contradicts it, so treat the residency gap as effectively neutral rather than favorable and re-check next year's CDS. Waitlist: 247 offered, 0 accepted a place [UMD-S1].
admissions.major_admit_context: UMD separates admission to the university from admission to the major through Limited Enrollment Programs (LEPs). The LEP list includes both majors a robotics applicant cares about - Computer Science and Engineering - alongside Biochemistry, Biological Sciences, Business, Chemistry, Criminology, Immersive Media Design, Neuroscience and Psychology [UMD-S5]. The mechanics: 'Prospective students should indicate their preferred major when completing their online application... However, your preferred major does not affect your admissibility to the university. Admitted students who selected an LEP as their major are reviewed by the specific program to determine admission to that major,' and 'While the majority of students are admitted to their preferred major, some LEP applicants may not be.' Students admitted to UMD but not to the LEP are placed in Letters & Sciences to meet gateway requirements, while non-LEP applicants 'are admitted directly to the major indicated on their application'; all major decisions arrive in the admission decision letter [UMD-S5][UMD-S3]. LEP review is also test-optional [UMD-S7]. If you land in Letters & Sciences, the CS gateway for students starting Fall 2024 or later is concrete and demanding: CMSC131 or CMSC133 with a minimum B-, CMSC132 with a minimum B-, MATH140 with a minimum B-, and a minimum 3.0 GPA across all institutions, with the final grade posted by the application deadline; starting at CMSC131/133 means 'a minimum of 7 semesters/terms to complete the major' [UMD-S6]. No public per-major admit rate or internal-transfer slot count (the often-quoted '~100 CS slots per year') appears on any UMD page fetched on 2026-08-16 - that figure is unverified. Practical consequence: naming CS or Engineering costs nothing at the university level (preferred major does not affect admissibility) but the major decision is a second, program-level gate, and the fallback path through Letters & Sciences is a real risk with a 3.0/B- floor.

why_us_ammunition: The Maryland Robotics Center is the strongest single hook: 'an interdisciplinary research center in the Institute for Systems Research within the A. James Clark School of Engineering,' with '47 Faculty members from 8 different departments' and '26 State-of-the-art labs and facilities including 3 multi-user MRC labs, 20 affiliated research labs, and 3 affiliated facilities,' spanning autonomous systems, bio-inspired, cognitive, extreme, human-robot interaction, medical, miniature and multirobot systems [UMD-S8].

MRC's named MATRIX Lab is pitched as 'Advancing Smarter, More Affordable Autonomy' and the center offers an undergraduate robotics minor alongside graduate options [UMD-S8] - a concrete undergraduate-accessible credential to name.

The Institute for Systems Research is 'a permanent, interdisciplinary research unit' that began as 'one of the National Science Foundation's original Engineering Research Centers in 1985' and now hosts 'more than 60 faculty and other researchers from 13 departments in five colleges' working on autonomous and distributed systems [UMD-S9].

There is a Clark School FIRST scholarship pathway specifically for FRC/FTC alumni requiring a 500-word essay on how FIRST shaped your career goals [UMD-S10] - your robotics record maps directly onto an institutional award, even if the cycle dates need confirming.

UMD's own framing rewards specificity: the required 300-word question asks for 'your reasons for wishing to enroll at UMD' [UMD-S4], and LEP review is a program-level read [UMD-S5], so naming MRC/ISR labs and the robotics minor does double duty.

score_notes.cs_foundations: Required core spans EECS 203, 280, 281, 370, 376 plus a probability/statistics requirement, with C-or-better grades and identical CS requirements in LSA and Engineering [UM-S7][UM-S2].
score_notes.math_foundations: Two approved math courses from MATH 115/116/214/215/216 plus a probability/statistics requirement; EECS 442 additionally requires linear algebra or ROB 101 [UM-S7][UM-S11].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: Named undergraduate courses cover intro AI (EECS 492), ML (445), ML principles (453), CV (442), NLP (487), conversational AI (449), applied ML (448), data mining (476), and autonomous robotics (467) [UM-S11].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: Depth exists via EECS 453, 467, graduate EECS 545 and CSE 595 (open at senior standing), but only 15 credits of upper-level CS electives are required [UM-S11][UM-S7].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: EECS 449 Conversational AI is the only named emerging-AI course verified; RL, generative AI, and AI safety appear only via EECS 498 Special Topics [UM-S11].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: Two colleges offer identical CS requirements at 120 vs 128 credits, CS-Eng has named AI/security/game-dev tracks, and MDP spans 11 schools [UM-S2][UM-S5][UM-S16].
score_notes.course_availability: Only the bulletin was verified, not a live term schedule, so offering frequency for EECS 449/453/448 is unconfirmed [UM-S11].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: UROP matches "more than 1,300" students with "over 800" faculty with a first- and second-year focus, and MDP admits first-year undergraduates to ~40 partnered teams and 9 faculty research projects [UM-S12][UM-S18][UM-S16][UM-S17].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: UROP's 800-faculty structured matching and MDP teams of 5-7 students provide mentorship without cold-emailing, though the Michigan AI Lab page publishes no undergraduate on-ramp [UM-S12][UM-S16][UM-S10].
score_notes.project_based_learning: Capstone required in every route (EECS 443/MDE, senior thesis, ROB 450), EECS 467 is a design experience, ROB 103 starts hands-on in year one, and MDP runs ~40 industry teams [UM-S7][UM-S5][UM-S8][UM-S11][UM-S16].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: B.S.E. in Robotics (Robotics BSE) (no ABET); 30 undergrad robotics courses. 20 labs, University of Michigan Robotics, 7 competition teams.
score_notes.computing_resources: Great Lakes offers ~13,000 cores plus GPU nodes, is "available to all researchers on campus," and class Slurm accounts are available on request [UM-S21].
score_notes.industry_preparation: Current CS salary and placement figures sit in an interactive dashboard not present on the fetched pages, and the only verified CS median is $85,000 from 2015 [UM-S28][UM-S30].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: A senior thesis can satisfy the CS-Eng capstone, CSE 595 is open at senior standing, and SUGS is a formal 30-credit pathway with 97 robotics PhD students on campus [UM-S5][UM-S11][UM-S19][UM-S34].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: SUGS allows 9 double-counted credits (more than Georgia Tech's 6) over 2-3 terms, but requires a 3.6 cumulative GPA plus B+ in EECS 281, EECS 270/370, and four 300+ EECS courses [UM-S19][UM-S20].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: 1,300 UROP students, ~40 MDP teams, 221 robotics majors, and a purpose-built 134,000 sq ft robotics building opened in 2021 [UM-S12][UM-S16][UM-S34][UM-S9].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: The sharpest documented pressure is structural: CS must be selected* before declaration in both colleges, and LSA enforces a two-attempt repeat limit on prerequisites [UM-S2][UM-S7].
score_notes.student_agency: MDP spans 11 schools and admits first-years, UROP serves all fields, and ROB 101 substitutes for a CS course prerequisite — but declaring CS itself is gated [UM-S16][UM-S18][UM-S11][UM-S2].
score_notes.community_within_scale: Against 32,802 undergraduates, 96% of first-years live in campus housing, MDP teams are 5-7 students, and Robotics is a 221-student major [UM-S26][UM-S16][UM-S34].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: MHacks is currently running ("MHacks 2026," $40,000 in prizes) with a Sept 2025 post citing 700+ hackers, but no other technical club was verified on a fetched page [UM-S31][UM-S32].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: No student-organization directory was fetched; only RecSports facilities and adventure programs were verified [UM-S27].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: Greek participation is a precisely documented 18.03% (5,913 of 32,802) across 55 chapters, and with only 25% of undergraduates in campus housing most social life is off-campus and non-Greek by default [UM-S25][UM-S26].
score_notes.campus_engagement: 96% of first-year students live in campus housing, dropping to 25% for all undergraduates — a residential first year followed by an Ann Arbor-centered upper-class life [UM-S26].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: RecSports operates a newly renovated Intramural Sports Building, the North Campus Recreation Building, a 36,000 sq ft Sports Coliseum, and the new Hadley Family Recreation and Well-Being Center, the largest recreational facility on campus — though pools and climbing were not listed on the fetched page [UM-S27].
score_notes.daily_life: Ann Arbor walkability, transit, dining, housing guarantee, and safety data were not verified from fetched sources.

admissions.admit_rate_note_note: Michigan's CDS does not publish in-state vs out-of-state application or admit counts, even though CDS C7 marks state residency as 'Considered'.
admissions.major_admit_context: Michigan's binding constraint is the Computer Science major, not the college. U-M's CSE department states: 'Due to capacity constraints, students who are admitted to the University of Michigan in Fall 2023 or later must first be selected for the Computer Science (CS) major before they can declare the major. This selection policy ... is the same for students in both the College of Engineering and the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts (LSA). The selection policy applies only to the CS major and does NOT apply to students seeking to major in the Computer Engineering (CE) or Data Science (DS) programs' [UMICH-S6]. Incoming students request CS 'advance selection' on the Common Application itself, and transfer students cannot switch into CS once on campus [UMICH-S6][UMICH-S7]. Robotics is the opposite story: the Robotics BSE has no capacity cap — students declare after at least one term with a 2.0 GPA [UMICH-S8]. So a robotics-focused applicant should target Robotics BSE (open declaration) and treat CS as the gated option requiring the advance-selection request on the application.
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: Early Decision is brand new — U-M describes it as 'New for 2025-2026 Application Cycle ... new option to apply Early Decision (binding decision)'. The Fall 2025 CDS therefore reports no ED plan and no ED counts. No ED admit rate exists yet.
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 confirms a non-binding, non-restrictive Early Action plan closing November 1 with notification January 31, but U-M does not report EA application or admit counts.
admissions.sat_mid50_note: Fall 2025 CDS C9: 25th 1370 / 50th 1470 / 75th 1530, from 4,503 enrolled submitters.
admissions.pct_submitting_sat_note: 55% of enrolled first-years submitted SAT scores; 18% submitted ACT scores.
admissions.gpa_note: CDS C12 average high school GPA 3.9, reported for 97.8% of enrolled first-years; CDS C11 shows 38.8% of enrolled first-years with a 4.0 GPA. CDS C7 marks class rank 'Not Considered'.
admissions.test_policy_note: This one is genuinely ambiguous and worth verifying. CDS C8 marks SAT/ACT 'Recommended' for the Fall 2027 cycle (not 'test-optional'), and CDS C7 rates test scores 'Important' — a stronger weighting than most peers. Meanwhile U-M's admissions and LSA pages say test-optional only 'for the 2026 application cycle'. There is no published Fall 2027 test-policy statement, so the practical read is test-optional-but-recommended, with scores carrying real weight when submitted.

interview.mechanism: By invitation and program-specific. U-M's CDS C7 note reads: 'Some applicants to Music, Theatre and Dance and some applicants to the College of Engineering may be interviewed. A portfolio is required and considered for admission for Art, Architecture and the Ross Business School.' The top-level C7 grid still marks Interview 'Not Considered', so a College of Engineering interview should be treated as possible but neither required nor requestable.

first_frc_scholarship.note: No FIRST/FRC-specific scholarship is published on umich.edu. The College of Engineering states that its merit scholarships are awarded automatically with no separate application, which leaves no mechanism for an activity-specific FIRST award.

why_us_ammunition: The Robotics BSE launched in Fall 2022 as 'a first among top 10 engineering schools', and the robotics department reports 175+ current robotics majors — a concrete, citable program identity [UMICH-S8].

The Ford Motor Company Robotics Building, completed in 2021, is a $75 million, 134,000-square-foot facility and Ford's first robotics and mobility lab on a university campus, with roughly 100 Ford researchers on its fourth floor [UMICH-S9].
Facility specifics an applicant can name: a three-story fly zone for drone testing and a Mars Yard for rough-terrain robot testing inside the Ford Robotics Building [UMICH-S9].
Robotics BSE has open declaration — after at least one term with a 2.0 GPA — which lets an applicant honestly say they can start robotics coursework without competing for a capped seat [UMICH-S8].
If CS matters to the applicant, U-M requires requesting CS advance selection on the Common Application itself; naming that awareness signals genuine research into how U-M works [UMICH-S6][UMICH-S7].
