admissions.admit_rate_note: CDS 2024-25 (Fall 2024) C1: 14,105 first-year applicants (6,920 M + 7,022 W + 124 another gender + 39 unknown), 7,844 admitted (3,541 + 4,217 + 71 + 15), 1,114 enrolled = 55.61% [DBN-S1]. No residency breakdown is published in the CDS, and none is needed: UM-Dearborn's CDS C7 marks BOTH state residency AND geographical residence as NOT CONSIDERED [DBN-S1], making it the most residency-neutral school in this batch. Note the very low yield (1,114 enrolled from 7,844 admits) — Dearborn is a commuter-heavy campus, which is the honest context for both the admit rate and the housing/experience question.
admissions.major_admit_context: UM-Dearborn has NO major-level admissions gate for engineering — admission is university-wide and formula-driven on GPA, and the College of Engineering and Computer Science (CECS) majors, including the dedicated Robotics Engineering BSE, are entered directly. The published rule is a genuine guarantee: a high school GPA of 3.00 AND ABOVE = GUARANTEED ADMISSION (subject to conduct requirements); 2.75-2.99 is 'potentially admissible' and assessed on academic preparation and grade trends, and may require an essay and/or letters of recommendation; below 2.75 is 'likely not admissible' as a first-year student and is routed to a community-college pathway. GED equivalency requires a total of 660 with at least 165 in each area [DBN-S2]. This is the only school in this batch offering a published, mechanical admissions guarantee, and it is the reason Dearborn functions as the portfolio's anchor 'likely' — the odds engine should NOT downgrade it for major gating, because there is none. Distinctive academic point: Dearborn awards a dedicated ABET-accredited Robotics Engineering BSE (not a robotics concentration inside ME or ECE), teaching robotics, electrical and computer engineering, systems engineering and mechanical engineering with 'lots of opportunities for hands-on learning in your classes and in our pair of robotics engineering labs' [DBN-S4]. Michigan residents should also note the separate Michigan Assured Admission pathway [DBN-S7]; it does not apply to a North Carolina applicant.
admissions.gpa_note: CDS 2024-25 C12: average high school GPA 3.64, with 100.00% of enrolled first-years reporting GPA; C11 distribution 18.76% at 4.0, 26.48% at 3.75-3.99, 20.56% at 3.50-3.74, 15.17% at 3.25-3.49, 14.90% at 3.00-3.24, 4.13% at 2.50-2.99 and 0% below 2.50 [DBN-S1] — the widest GPA spread in this batch, consistent with the 3.0 guarantee. Class rank is not reported. Test detail from C9: SAT composite 25/50/75 = 990/1120/1250, EBRW 500/560/620, SAT Math 490/550/630; ACT composite 24/26/29, ACT Math 20/25/28, ACT English 23/26/34, ACT Reading 24/28/31. UM-Dearborn LEAVES THE 'percent submitting SAT/ACT' CELLS BLANK, so pct_submitting_sat is null rather than estimated [DBN-S1]. Interpretation for a strong applicant: an FRC-caliber SAT sits far above the 75th percentile here (1250), which is exactly why Dearborn is the merit-scholarship and safety play rather than a stretch.
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: TEST-OPTIONAL. UM-Dearborn's first-year application pages describe a test-optional process, with the Personal Statement required only for applicants below a 3.0 GPA and for test-optional applicants below 3.0 [DBN-S2][DBN-S3]; CDS C7 marks standardized test scores as merely 'Considered' while academic GPA is the sole 'Very Important' factor [DBN-S1]. Money caveat that argues for submitting anyway: CECS states 'All scholarships consider earned grades; ACT scores are also considered for freshmen scholarships' [DBN-S5]. (INFERRED for Fall 2027 — the pages reflect the currently open cycle; Dearborn has not posted a Fall 2027-specific testing statement.)
admissions.c7_factors_note: CDS 2024-25 C7 [DBN-S1]. This is the most extreme C7 grid in the entire dataset: ACADEMIC GPA IS THE ONLY 'VERY IMPORTANT' FACTOR; rigor and test scores are 'Considered'; and EVERY OTHER FACTOR — class rank, essay, recommendations, interview, extracurriculars, talent/ability, character, first generation, alumni relation, geographical residence, state residency, religious affiliation, volunteer work, work experience and level of applicant's interest — is marked NOT CONSIDERED. Under C6 'Other (explain)' Dearborn writes 'At UM-Dearborn, all incoming students have some type of require[d]...' (truncated in the published form) [DBN-S1]. STRATEGIC CONSEQUENCE: an FRC robotics record earns the applicant nothing at Dearborn admissions — it earns money and program placement instead. Zero essay effort should be spent here; effort belongs in the scholarship and co-op channels.

interview.mechanism: No admissions interview; CDS marks Interview 'Not Considered' [DBN-S1]. A Personal Statement is required only for applicants below a 3.0 GPA (and for test-optional applicants below 3.0) [DBN-S2][DBN-S3].

first_frc_scholarship.application_mechanism: automatic for CECS awards (no separate application)
first_frc_scholarship.note: NOT VERIFIABLE in this session. No FIRST/FRC-specific award is named on the CECS scholarships page or the first-year admissions pages reviewed, and the FIRST provider list is behind the portal login [DBN-S8]. The UM-Dearborn first-year scholarship page is Cloudflare-protected and could not be retrieved, so no institutional merit-award amounts are asserted. What IS documented on the CECS page: 'New students are automatically considered for awards. No additional application is required to be considered for CECS scholarships'; 'All scholarships consider earned grades; ACT scores are also considered for freshmen scholarships'; recipients 'need to enroll full time in an approved CECS degree program'; continuing students apply annually via Scholarship Universe; named awards include The Brick Program Endowed Scholarship I & II and CECS Student Scholarship I & II, each a '$1,000 annual tuition award, available for a maximum of four (4) terms', usable in Fall and Winter terms only; and as of retrieval 'All scholarships for 2025-2026 have been awarded. Additional information about next year's awards will be available in Spring 2026' [DBN-S5]. Separately, the Go Blue Guarantee program page exists for Dearborn [DBN-S6] but is a Michigan-resident tuition-free program and should NOT be assumed to apply to a North Carolina applicant — verify before modeling cost. NOTE: the $1,000/term CECS awards are small; if Dearborn is meant to be the affordability anchor, the real lever is the university merit award, which must be confirmed with admissions directly.

decision_dates.deposit_deadline: 2027-05-01 recommended (2027-08-26 final)
decision_dates.restrictions: NO Early Decision and NO Early Action — pure ROLLING admission, and the application is FREE. Published cycle structure: application opens AUG 1; decisions begin releasing OCT 15; FAFSA priority DEC 1; recommended application deadline APR 1 with a final deadline of AUG 15; Decision Day recommended MAY 1 with a final date of AUG 26 [DBN-S2][DBN-S3]. Because admission is guaranteed at 3.00+ GPA and the application is free with no essay for a 3.0+ applicant, the correct play is to submit in August and bank a guaranteed offer before any other decision arrives — this is the portfolio's psychological and financial floor. Dates shown are for the currently open cycle (INFERRED — prior-cycle dates; Fall 2027 dates not yet posted).

supplemental_essays.prompt: Personal Statement — REQUIRED ONLY for applicants with a high school GPA below 3.0, and for test-optional applicants below 3.0. Applicants at or above a 3.0 GPA are guaranteed admission and are NOT required to submit a personal statement. Applicants in the 2.75-2.99 band may additionally be asked for letters of recommendation.
No why-us or supplemental essay exists. CDS C7 marks Application Essay as NOT CONSIDERED [DBN-S1], so for a 3.0+ applicant Dearborn requires zero writing.

why_us_ammunition: A DEDICATED, ABET-accredited Robotics Engineering BSE — not a track or a minor. The program integrates robotics, electrical and computer engineering, systems engineering and mechanical engineering and is taught with 'lots of opportunities for hands-on learning in your classes and in our pair of robotics engineering labs at UM-Dearborn' [DBN-S4]. Among the seven schools in this batch, only Dearborn awards the robotics degree itself.

Detroit-metro automotive and mobility adjacency is the campus's structural advantage for a robotics/mechatronics student seeking co-op and internship placement. CAUTION: the specific co-op employer lists and program mechanics are NOT documented on the pages retrieved in this session (the robotics BSE page does not mention co-op or internships at all [DBN-S4]), so this bullet must be verified on the CECS co-op page before it goes into an essay — do not name employers on the strength of reputation alone.

CECS scholarships require no separate application ('New students are automatically considered for awards') and consider ACT scores for freshmen — so a strong-testing FRC applicant converts test performance into money without extra paperwork [DBN-S5].

The admissions formula itself is strategically usable: GPA is the ONLY 'Very Important' factor and a 3.00 GPA is a published guarantee [DBN-S1][DBN-S2], which makes Dearborn the one school where the applicant's outcome is knowable in advance — the correct role for it in the portfolio is a guaranteed August offer, not a persuasion exercise.
Verify the Go Blue Guarantee terms for non-Michigan residents before treating Dearborn as the low-cost option [DBN-S6]; the confirmed CECS awards are only $1,000/year for up to four terms [DBN-S5].

robotics_curriculum_detail.score_basis: Dedicated ABET-accredited BSE in Robotics Engineering (125 credits), one of the earliest such undergraduate degrees in the US, with a two-semester robotics capstone (ECE 4987/4988 Robotics Engineering Design I and II) [UMD-R1][UMD-R2]. Robotics course sequence spans manipulation (ECE 3641 Robotic Manipulation), mobility (ECE 4641 Mobile Robots), perception (ECE 4881 Introduction to Robot Vision), industrial robotics (IMSE 381, IMSE 489 Robotics Systems Simulation), mechatronics (ME 472) and vehicle/energy systems (ECE 237) [UMD-R1][UMD-R10]. A separate 9-credit Mechatronics and Robotics undergraduate certificate is open to other majors [UMD-R7][UMD-R8], and a 4+1 BSE/MSE Robotics Engineering path exists [UMD-R9].

robotics_access_detail.score_basis: The Institute for Advanced Vehicle Systems (IAVS) is a documented research institute with a Driving Simulator Lab (autonomous driving, HMI, human factors, eye tracking, Detroit road network model) [UMD-R5], satisfying the 'institute' condition for a 4. Documented robotics labs include the Robotics Engineering Laboratory (4 stations, hosts ECE 3641/4641/4881 and capstone), the Robotic Motion Intelligence (RMI) Lab, the Bio-Inspired Machine Intelligence Lab [UMD-R3], the IMSE robotics lab (two Fanuc LR Mate 200iD arms, Fanuc M1iA, vision sensors, conveyors, Roboguide) [UMD-R4], and the Manufacturing Systems Engineering Lab [UMD-R6]. Lab access requires safety training plus a faculty-submitted request [UMD-R6]. Not a 5: no named undergraduate research program with published participation, and no dedicated robotics competition team was found - the documented teams are Formula SAE and Formula SAE Electric [UMD-R11].

score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: The degree forces one subject from each of five distinct areas — data-, model-, decision-, computation- and human-centric [MIT-S1].

score_notes.faculty_mentorship: More than half of MIT faculty serve as UROP mentors and SuperUROP pairs juniors/seniors with a faculty supervisor for a year plus 6.UAR [MIT-S36], [MIT-S15].
score_notes.project_based_learning: Every 6-4 student must complete an Application CI-M project course (6.4200[J], 6.4210, or 6.8611) plus a second CI-M [MIT-S1].

score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: SuperUROP is explicitly aimed at "publication-worthy results" with grad-level facility access, and the 6-P4 MEng requires a master's thesis [MIT-S15], [MIT-S24].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: 6-4 students are explicitly eligible for the MEng, with a dedicated 6-P4 MNG in AI and Decision Making including an Artificial Intelligence concentration and a thesis [MIT-S48], [MIT-S24].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: 4,561 undergraduates alongside 7,255 graduate students, 500+ student organizations, and a for-credit January IAP included in tuition [MIT-S37], [MIT-S54], [MIT-S14].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: Structural pressure relief is documented (fall P/NR, spring ABC/NR, 48 units of lifetime Flex P/NR) and there is no internal major competition; no student-source culture evidence was gathered [MIT-S20], [MIT-S21].
score_notes.student_agency: No declared major until sophomore year, cross-registration at Harvard/Wellesley/MassArt at no added tuition, and UROP open to any registered undergraduate [MIT-S16], [MIT-S31], [MIT-S11].

admissions.major_admit_context: MIT runs a single Institute-wide admission review: applicants are not admitted to a school, department, or major, and the CDS reports one funnel (29,281 / 1,334) with no departmental breakdown [MIT-S1]. MIT's own stats page likewise reports only Institute-level Early Action and Regular Action counts (EA 12,052 applicants / 721 admitted; RA 17,229 applicants / 603 admitted, plus 175 admitted from the 7,486 deferred) with no major-level rates [MIT-S2]. Consequently intended field of study does not change the admissions bar, and the essay set asks about interests rather than about a chosen department [MIT-S3].
admissions.ed_note: MIT offers no Early Decision — CDS C21 Early Decision = No. MIT's early round is non-binding, non-restrictive Early Action [MIT-S1].
admissions.gpa_note_reason: MIT reports average HS GPA as "N/Av" in the CDS; MIT does not publish an average GPA [MIT-S1].
admissions.c7_note: MIT is the only school in this batch where Character/Personal Qualities is the sole 'Very Important' factor — GPA, rigor, test scores, essays, recommendations, interview, activities and talent are all rated one tier lower at 'Important' [MIT-S1].

why_us_ammunition: UROP is the flagship, and the numbers are official: begun in 1969, UROP supports nearly 6,000 projects yearly; 93% of the Class of 2025 did at least one UROP; 3,200+ undergraduates participated and 73% of first-year students (Class of 2028) did a UROP in AY2025, with $16.86M allocated to paid UROPs and 58% of MIT faculty serving as mentors [MIT-S6].

UROPs are available "in every MIT department, as well as centers and labs throughout the Institute," for pay or credit, over a summer, a term, or longer — so a first-year robotics applicant can credibly describe starting research immediately [MIT-S6][MIT-S7].

CSAIL is a named, scaled destination: "the largest research laboratory at MIT," hosting over 1,700 members, 130+ distinguished researchers, ~1,200 graduate students, 119 postdocs, 60 research groups and 900+ active projects [MIT-S8].

2.007 (Design and Manufacturing I) is the direct FRC analogue: students spend the spring semester "learning the principles of mechanical design and applying those principles in the lab to build a robot from a kit of servos, circuit boards, and sheet metal," culminating in an annual robot competition whose theme changes each year [MIT-S10][MIT-S11].

The essay set rewards this specificity: MIT explicitly asks what problems you would tackle with an MIT education and with whom, which is an invitation to name a lab (CSAIL group), a mechanism (UROP), and a course (2.007) [MIT-S3][MIT-S6][MIT-S8].

Strategically, MIT is the one school here with no binding early option (non-binding, non-restrictive EA at 5.98%), test scores required, no demonstrated-interest tracking, and Character/Personal Qualities as the only 'Very Important' factor — so the file should be built around substance and character rather than early-round commitment [MIT-S1][MIT-S2].

name: North Carolina State University

alternative_route: B.S. Computer Engineering, AI and Machine Learning Concentration (ECE) — includes ECE 411 Intro to ML and ECE 425/525 Neural Networks and Deep Learning

notable_ai_institute: Data Science and AI Academy (AI Academy launched spring 2020, spanning all 12 colleges); Laboratory for Analytic Sciences on Centennial Campus (undergraduate involvement unverified)
notable_undergraduate_research_program: CSC 299 (first/second-year research) + CSC Undergraduate Research Lightning Talks; Office of Undergraduate Research Project Supply Grants
fourplusone_name: Accelerated Bachelor's/Master's (ABM) — Master of Computer Science, M.S. Computer Science, or M.S. Computer Networking
housing_guarantee: UNVERIFIED (housing site did not state a first-year guarantee)
greek_participation: CONFLICTING official figures — "more than 15%" (FSL Snapshot, updated Summer 2026), "more than 12%" (FSL FAQ), 12.03% (Spring 2023 official grade report); 52 chapters, 3,800+ members, Greek Village houses 767
sports_influence: UNVERIFIED (ACC member; no evidence gathered on social dominance)

score_notes.cs_foundations: Required core includes CSC 226 discrete math, CSC 316 data structures/algorithms, CSC 333 automata and computability, CSC 246 OS, CSC 230 C/tools and a 4-credit CSC 326 software engineering — a complete theory+systems spine, ABET-accredited [NCSU-S1][NCSU-S2].
score_notes.math_foundations: Three-semester calculus (MA 141/241/242), MA 305 linear algebra and ST 370 probability/statistics are all required; optimization is elective only [NCSU-S1].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: CSC 411 AI and CSC 422 ML are required and CSC 201/301 come early, but no undergraduate CSC course for computer vision, NLP, RL or deep learning was found on the concentration's elective lists [NCSU-S1].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: 21 hours of AI coursework with 15 hours of AI-directed electives, but the graduate versions (e.g., CSC 522) are open only to CSC Honors or ABM students [NCSU-S1][NCSU-S15].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: CSC 455 Social Computing and Decentralized AI and CSC 484 Building Game AI are catalog electives and DSA micro-courses cover applied ML, but no LLM/generative-AI/agents course was verified [NCSU-S1][NCSU-S9].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: The 121-hour AI concentration leaves only about 3 hours of truly free electives after chemistry, physics, calculus and the CS core [NCSU-S1][NCSU-S6].
score_notes.course_availability: CSC 411 and CSC 422 are required and therefore scheduled every year, but CSC 490/491/499 are majors-only and CSC 492 requires 6 prior CSC restricted-elective hours [NCSU-S1][NCSU-S18].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: CSC 299 exists specifically for first- and second-year undergraduate research and the department runs faculty Lightning Talks the first Friday of each semester, though OUR funding caps at $500 supplies + $1,000 of work [NCSU-S13][NCSU-S11].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: Named faculty coordinators for each elective track and honors program plus a recurring department-run mentor-matching event [NCSU-S15][NCSU-S14][NCSU-S13].
score_notes.project_based_learning: CSC 492 Senior Design is a required team-built software system with written and oral reports, run through the Senior Design Center with industrial sponsors [NCSU-S3][NCSU-S18].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: Joint NC State / UNC Asheville B.S. in Engineering (EAC); 9 undergrad robotics courses. 6 labs, CRIM, 2 competition teams.
score_notes.computing_resources: No page documenting undergraduate GPU or HPC cluster access was retrieved this session.
score_notes.industry_preparation: 548 new co-op rotations and 30 career fairs in 2025-26 with 70% of undergraduates completing an internship, plus a required industry-sponsored capstone — but no salary or employer data is published [NCSU-S30][NCSU-S3].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: CSC Honors requires a completed CSC 498/499 with a written report and permits 5XX graduate coursework, but no undergraduate publication or PhD-placement evidence was found [NCSU-S14][NCSU-S15].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: ABM double-counts up to 12 graduate credits into an AI-capable MS (CSC 520 AI I is a core option) finishing within 12-18 months, gated at a 3.500 GPA with no published funding discount [NCSU-S19][NCSU-S32].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: Hack_NCState drew a 24-hour, free, cross-disciplinary field into Talley's State Ballroom in February 2026 and HackPack ran a CTF in April 2026 [NCSU-S22a][NCSU-S23].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: Major grade rules are permissive (C/C- minimums, 2.0 major-GPA floor), but CODA forces first-year competition for capacity-limited CS seats judged on chemistry, physics and calculus grades [NCSU-S1][NCSU-S4].
score_notes.student_agency: CSC 299/490/499 proposals, three concentrations and three elective tracks give real choice, yet graduate courses are restricted to Honors/ABM students and AI students are barred from the Robotics Track [NCSU-S13][NCSU-S15].
score_notes.community_within_scale: CSC Honors, ABM, robotics teams and HackPack provide sub-communities inside a College of Engineering of more than 12,500 students; the living-learning village roster was not retrievable [NCSU-S27][NCSU-S33].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: Four separate technical organizations have dated 2025-26 activity: Hack_NCState (Feb 14-15, 2026), HackPack CTF (Apr 17-18, 2026), Aerial Robotics Club (2025-26 NC Space Grant award) and RoboPack [NCSU-S22a][NCSU-S23][NCSU-S25b][NCSU-S25c].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: No student-organization directory or event calendar was fetched this session.
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: Official FSL data updated Summer 2026 shows 52 chapters and 3,800+ members at "more than 15%" of undergraduates, with Greek Village housing only 767 residents, so roughly 85% are unaffiliated and Greek life does not control housing [NCSU-S34].
score_notes.campus_engagement: No evidence was gathered on weekend/evening campus life, traditions, or residential versus commuter patterns.
score_notes.recreation_facilities: 430,000 sq ft across the Wellness and Recreation Center and Carmichael Gym with 11 indoor courts, an Olympic weightlifting room, the Casey Aquatic Center, a Climbing Center and an indoor track, included automatically in student fees [NCSU-S37][NCSU-S38].
score_notes.daily_life: Home-metro location with RDU and RTP nearby, 24-hour libraries Sunday-Thursday, and free staffed makerspaces — offset by a daily main-campus/Centennial-Campus split for CS students [NCSU-S24e][NCSU-S3][NCSU-S37].

admissions.overall_admit_rate_note: Fall 2024: 44,043 applied / 18,201 admitted / 5,837 enrolled. NC State has not posted a 2025-26 CDS, so this is the most recent official cycle. Waitlist: 9,704 offered a place, 4,194 accepted it, 261 admitted from it.
admissions.admit_rate_note: IN-STATE vs OUT-OF-STATE (Fall 2024, CDS): North Carolina residents 21,636 applied / 10,570 admitted = 48.9%. Out-of-state 19,487 applied / 6,963 admitted = 35.7%. International 2,920 applied / 668 admitted = 22.9%. The in-state advantage is roughly 13 percentage points, and it is policy-driven: UNC System Policy 700.1.3 caps nonresidents at 18 percent of NC State's fall first-time undergraduate class, with a State operating budget reduction if the cap is exceeded for two consecutive fiscal years.
admissions.major_admit_context: For engineering, NC State's intended major is explicitly non-competitive at the admission stage: 'All first-year students are admitted to the Engineering First Year Program (EFY). Students who know which engineering major they plan to pursue may indicate it on the admissions application as their intended major ... Please note that indication of an intended major on the admissions application has no effect whatsoever on admissions decisions.' Students must complete English composition, calculus, chemistry, physics and introductory engineering and computer courses before joining an academic department [NCSU-S6]. What is weighted heavily is the academic record: 'a student's high school academic record, including grade point average (weighted and unweighted) and class rank, receives significant emphasis in engineering admissions decisions', with the typical admitted first-year at an unweighted GPA of 3.8-4.0 [NCSU-S6]. Studio-based majors are the exception — College of Design, Fashion and Textile Design and Music Technology applicants must apply by November 1 with a 10-piece portfolio and an additional essay [NCSU-S2]. The CDS also flags a math floor: 'The most competitive applicants will have taken math through precalculus as a minimum in high school, particularly for STEM and business' [NCSU-S1].
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: NC State offers no Early Decision plan (CDS C21 = No).
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 confirms a non-binding Early Action plan closing November 1 with notification January 30, but NC State publishes no EA application or admit counts. NC State does say 'We don't necessarily give priority to early action applicants in the review process, but first-year early action applicants receive priority consideration for scholarships and financial aid' [NCSU-S2].
admissions.sat_mid50_note: Fall 2024 CDS C9: composite 25th 1290 / 50th 1360 / 75th 1440, from 1,422 enrolled submitters.
admissions.act_mid50_note: ACT composite 25th 25 / 50th 29 / 75th 32, from 2,365 enrolled submitters (41.34%) — NC State is one of the few schools in this set where ACT submission exceeds SAT submission.
admissions.pct_submitting_sat_note: 24.86% of enrolled first-years submitted SAT scores; 41.34% submitted ACT scores.
admissions.gpa_note: CDS C12 average high school GPA 3.83, reported for 98% of enrolled first-years; CDS C11 shows 20.02% with a 4.0 GPA and CDS C10 shows 40% in the top tenth of their class. The College of Engineering states the typical admitted first-year has an unweighted GPA of 3.8-4.0.
admissions.test_policy_note: Conditional test-optional with a GPA floor. CDS C8 states verbatim: 'We are test optional for applicants with a weighted GPA of 2.8 or above. International students for whom English is not their first language will be required to submit an English proficiency test.' The 2024-25 CDS labels these policies 'for use in admission for Fall 2026', with a latest receipt date of February 1, so Fall 2027 applicability is inferred from the standing UNC System-aligned rule. Applicants below a 2.8 weighted GPA must submit a score.
admissions.c7_note: CDS C7 also marks geographical residence and state residency 'Considered', consistent with the 18 percent nonresident cap.

interview.mechanism: No admissions interview is offered or considered; CDS C7 marks Interview 'Not Considered'. Portfolio review substitutes for studio-based majors (10-piece portfolio plus an additional essay, due November 1).

first_frc_scholarship.note: No FIRST/FRC-specific scholarship appears on NC State admissions, College of Engineering or student-services scholarship pages. NC State routes merit awards through the PackASSIST scholarship portal, which admitted students access after admission, with a February 15 priority consideration deadline; applying Early Action by November 1 gives priority consideration for scholarships. An FRC applicant should search PackASSIST after admission rather than expect a named FIRST award.

why_us_ammunition: NC State's College of Engineering states its robotics ambition directly: it 'aims to be a national leader in robotics innovation, focusing on AI-enabled, hands-on and collaborative robotics' [NCSU-S8].

Robotics at NC State is framed as bringing together 'control, AI, human interaction and systems integration from fundamentals to application' — language an FRC applicant can mirror when describing subsystem integration work [NCSU-S11].

The Engineering First Year Program means every engineering student shares a common first year before joining a department, so an applicant can honestly describe exploring across robotics-adjacent departments without gambling on a capped major [NCSU-S6].

For a North Carolina resident, the in-state admit rate was 48.9% versus 35.7% out-of-state, and NC residents who apply Early Action by November 1 and confirm residency by November 10 now receive decisions by the end of December — a genuine strategic advantage worth planning around [NCSU-S1][NCSU-S3].
Applying Early Action by November 1 is the only route to the University Honors Program application and gives priority consideration for scholarships and financial aid [NCSU-S2][NCSU-S3].

why_us_ammunition: Co-op is the structural differentiator and is quantifiable: engineering undergraduates typically complete two co-ops on a four-year plan or three on a five-year plan, each usually six months, with terms running January-June or July-December — an applicant can map a concrete AI/robotics co-op sequence [NEU-S4][NEU-S8].

"Almost all students participate in co-op" in the College of Engineering, and every Northeastern undergraduate must complete some form of experiential learning (co-op, research, or service learning) — so an essay can commit to a specific pathway rather than a vague interest [NEU-S4].

The Institute for Experiential Robotics organizes research into five thrusts — human-robot teaming, embodied AI, systems/design/control, ethics-policy-economics, and secure/privacy-preserving robotics — with application areas including manufacturing and extreme environments (space, polar, marine) [NEU-S5][NEU-S9].

IER explicitly recruits undergraduates: its director states "the institute also always provides experiential learning opportunities for our undergraduates. We have a track record of recruiting qualified students in our institute, so they will get involved in our research," with lab space occupying most of the first floor of the EXP research complex [NEU-S6].

Named faculty fits are easy to cite: Taskin Padir (experiential robotics, human-robot teaming at the extremes, embodied AI; RIVeR Lab), Hanumant Singh (SLAM/mapping for aerial, marine and ground vehicles in extreme environments), and Peter Whitney (human-safe, medical and soft robotics) [NEU-S5].
Because Northeastern's CDS shows ED at 43.05% versus 5.21% overall and marks level of interest as Considered, applying ED I is the single largest lever available in this file [NEU-S1].

score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: The Fall 2024 CSE 5539 section covered transformers, LLMs, parameter-efficient fine-tuning and emergent properties, and the university offers "Unlocking Generative AI" open to all majors [OSU-S18] [OSU-S24].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: The 126-hour BS CSE leaves 17 hours of open CSE technical electives at 3000+, which is exactly the room needed to stack 5000-level AI courses [OSU-S7] [OSU-S5].
score_notes.course_availability: CSE 3521, 5522 and 5243 require enrollment in the CSE/CIS/ECE/Data Analytics major, and the department states first preference for CSE courses above 2221 goes to majors, with non-majors taking leftover seats [OSU-S15] [OSU-S16] [OSU-S13].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: STEP offers every second-year student a faculty mentor plus up to $2,000 regardless of GPA, layered over up to 300 Undergraduate Research Scholar Awards per year with monthly rounds and a $6,000 ten-week library fellowship [OSU-S31] [OSU-S32] [OSU-S34] [OSU-S38].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: STEP mandates weekly small-group meetings with a faculty mentor through autumn semester, and major status confers an assigned faculty advisor [OSU-S31] [OSU-S12].
score_notes.project_based_learning: The BS CSE requires both a junior project course (CSE 3901/3902/3903) and a capstone (CSE 5911-5915, with 5914 Knowledge-Based Systems recommended for AI), on top of nine-plus OHI/O events per year [OSU-S7] [OSU-S3] [OSU-S44].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: Robotics and Autonomous Systems (RAS); 11 undergrad robotics courses. 14 labs, CAR, 1 competition team.
score_notes.computing_resources: The Ohio Supercomputer Center is "always free for Ohio classroom usage" and offers H100 (96 GB), A100 (80/40 GB) and V100 GPUs, but students need a class code or a faculty PI to be added to a project [OSU-S39] [OSU-S40] [OSU-S41].
score_notes.industry_preparation: Official figures give average starting salaries of $113,161 (CA/WA) and $76,429 (elsewhere), with named employers from Google and Microsoft to Columbus-based Nationwide and Root [OSU-S65].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: The combined BS/MS is clean and the BS CSE objectives name graduate study, but no PhD placement, co-authorship or graduate-destination data was published [OSU-S48] [OSU-S4] [OSU-S65].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: Open to both CSE and CIS majors, 3.5 CPHR and 90 hours at application, up to 9 double-counted credits shortening the combined degree by a full semester, with no GRE mentioned [OSU-S48] [OSU-S63] [OSU-S64].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: OHI/O ran HackOHI/O, MakeOHI/O, ShowOHI/O, Hack AI, BuckeyeCTF, Game I/O and more within the 2025-26 window, and the AI Club met weekly and hosted OpenAI in November 2025 [OSU-S44] [OSU-S57] [OSU-S59].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: Pressure is structural: the CSE/CIS pre-major has been closed to internal switchers since Autumn 2023, closes at capacity, and the major GPA cutoff is reset annually with "not possible to make exceptions" [OSU-S12] [OSU-S13].
score_notes.student_agency: STEP lets a sophomore design and budget their own funded Signature Project across six categories, and 17 free CSE technical-elective hours let a student build a de facto AI major [OSU-S31] [OSU-S32] [OSU-S7].
score_notes.community_within_scale: A two-year on-campus residency requirement plus seventeen theme-based Scholars living-learning programs and a 1,700-student ASC honors community counterbalance a 46,627-undergraduate campus [OSU-S73] [OSU-S45] [OSU-S76] [OSU-S56].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: Active AI Club (weekly, Baker Systems 198, hosted OpenAI Nov 2025), OSU DEV (200+ members, founded 2022), Underwater Robotics (RoboSub 2026), Buckeye AutoDrive (50+ members), plus a Tech Hub directory of a dozen more [OSU-S57] [OSU-S60] [OSU-S61] [OSU-S29] [OSU-S43].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: Ohio State's student-activities office lists more than 1,400 student organizations [OSU-S78].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: With a rush cohort of roughly 1,900 students against ~46,600 undergraduates, the great majority are unaffiliated — though the official participation percentage is NOT PUBLISHED [OSU-S79] [OSU-S56].
score_notes.campus_engagement: The university's own Student Life Survey found 85.6% of undergraduates involved in at least one of thirteen involvement types [OSU-S77].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: Official Student Life material puts the RPAC at "more than 600,000 square feet" with five pools including an Olympic-size competition pool and 10-meter diving pool, covered by a ~$135 per-semester recreation fee [OSU-S86] [OSU-S87] [OSU-S85].
score_notes.daily_life: A major metro with unlimited free COTA bus access on the Ohio State app and a nonstop Breeze flight to RDU of about 1h 25m [OSU-S93] [OSU-S94] [OSU-S95].

admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2025 (Columbus campus): 81,392 applicants, 40,047 admitted, 8,248 enrolled = 49.2% [OSU-S1]. In-state 11,395/25,273 = 45.1%; out-of-state 19,914/42,898 = 46.4%; international 8,738/13,221 = 66.1% [OSU-S1] (INFERRED - division of CDS C1 counts). Note the pattern: OSU's in-state and out-of-state admit rates are nearly identical, but yield differs sharply - 5,609 of 8,248 enrollees are Ohio residents [OSU-S1]. Waitlist: 5,358 offered, 2,278 accepted a place, 2,049 admitted [OSU-S1] - the only school in this batch where the waitlist is a live path.
admissions.major_admit_context: Ohio State admits first-year students as PRE-majors, not majors: 'Students new to OSU are not directly admitted to major status. Instead, they are admitted as pre-majors' [OSU-S8]. To be a pre-CSE student you must be 'directly admitted to the College of Engineering,' where 'Entry into the college is competitive and several factors are considered including ACT/SAT scores, strong college prep curriculum, class rank and GPA'; the alternative CIS option lives in Arts and Sciences with no additional departmental requirements after college admission [OSU-S8]. Both majors a robotics applicant would want are Limited Space Programs reached through the admission-to-major application, and eligibility is restricted by pre-major: 'Computer Science - CSE and CIS pre-majors may apply' and 'Mechanical Engineering - MECH and AERO pre-majors may apply' (Aerospace likewise) [OSU-S6]. By contrast, Chemical, Civil, Electrical and Computer, Environmental, Industrial and Systems, Materials, Welding, Engineering Physics and FABE are 'Space Available Programs' that accept any engineering student in good standing (2.0 GPA or above) without an application [OSU-S6]. The admission-to-major floor is a 2.0 cumulative OSU GPA plus major-specific course criteria (for CS: Calculus I and CSE 2221 with a C or better plus pre-major enrollment, and for the CSE option also Calculus II and Fundamentals of Engineering; for ME: Calculus II, Fundamentals of Engineering, Physics I and enrollment in the aerospace or mechanical pre-major), but admission is capacity-competitive, students rank up to three majors, and 'Admitted students will be offered a place in one major' [OSU-S6]. There are hard limits on second chances - two attempts only, and accepting an offer bars reapplying in the next cycle [OSU-S6]. Front-end choice matters too: applicants wanting Aerospace, Biomedical, CSE, CIS or Mechanical 'must choose one of these programs during their initial application to Ohio State,' admitted students may change into engineering programs only through May 15, and 'After May 15, students will not be permitted to switch into Aerospace Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Computer and Information Science, or Mechanical Engineering programs' [OSU-S7]. Applying Early Action is effectively mandatory for engineering: EA is required for 'Majors in the College of Engineering' as well as merit scholarships and honors [OSU-S3]. No per-major admit rate is published by OSU.
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: Ohio State offers no Early Decision plan (CDS C21 = No) [OSU-S1].
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: The 2025-2026 CDS records a non-restrictive EA plan (closing 11/1, notify 1/31) without publishing EA applicant/admit counts [OSU-S1]. The 60.4% EA rate circulating from the 2023-24 CDS was not re-verified in this session.
admissions.test_detail_note: Fall 2025 enrolled: SAT submitted by 25% (2,099), ACT by 42% (3,474) - the only school in this batch where ACT submission exceeds SAT. SAT composite 25th/50th/75th = 1300/1380/1440; ACT 27/30/32 [OSU-S1].
admissions.gpa_note_detail: OSU leaves CDS C11/C12 blank, so no institution-reported GPA distribution or average is available [OSU-S1]. Class rank instead: 73% top tenth, 96% top quarter, 99% top half, with 27% submitting rank [OSU-S1].
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: REQUIRED - this is a change from prior cycles and the biggest surprise in this batch. CDS C8 states SAT/ACT are 'Required to be considered for admission' for Fall 2027 [OSU-S1], the admissions site confirms 'Yes, standardized test scores from ACT or SAT are required for first-year applicants to the Columbus campus,' superscoring is used, and the last usable test dates for Early Action are October 3 (SAT) / October 17 (ACT) [OSU-S3]; the university announced the reinstatement publicly [OSU-S5]. CDS C8E gives a latest test date of 1/15 and notes scores are used for advising/placement [OSU-S1].
admissions.c7_note: C7 grid visually confirmed from the CDS page image (the PDF text layer omits the checkbox values). Test scores are Very Important here - the only school in this batch to rate them that highly - consistent with the reinstated requirement. Volunteer work and work experience are both Important, unusually high. Alumni relation and religious affiliation Not Considered; geographical residence and state residency Considered [OSU-S1].

admissions.supplemental_essays_note: Confirms the expectation that OSU has no conventional supplemental essay set for first-year admission [OSU-S4]. Separately, the later admission-to-major application (taken as a current student) does require essays of about 250 words / maximum 1500 characters each, with the major-specific Essay 1 required only for Aerospace, Biomedical, Computer Science (CSE or CIS) and Mechanical Engineering [OSU-S6] - useful to know, but not part of the freshman application.
why_us_ammunition: The Center for Automotive Research is OSU's flagship mobility lab and reports '137 Students Gaining Hands on Research Experience' and '131 Collaborating Faculty' [OSU-S9] - a rare, citable undergraduate-research scale number.

CAR's technical focus - 'Electrification, connectivity, automation, and multi-modal transportation systems' - plus advanced-mobility programming and industry tours in central Ohio gives a specific autonomy/robotics angle [OSU-S10].

OSU's engineering structure is worth addressing head-on: Space Available versus Limited Space programs [OSU-S6] means you can argue why you want a capacity-controlled major (CS or ME) and show you know the 2.0-plus-coursework gate and the three-choice ranking.

The pre-major model means your first-year plan is part of the pitch: Calculus, CSE 2221 or Fundamentals of Engineering, and Physics sequences are the actual admission-to-major currency [OSU-S6] - referencing them signals fit.

Ohio State reinstated the SAT/ACT requirement for first-year applicants [OSU-S3][OSU-S5] and rates test scores Very Important [OSU-S1], so a strong score is itself a why-us-fit argument: this is the one school in the batch where testing carries maximum weight.

robotics_curriculum_detail.score_basis: A real, college-level Robotics and Autonomous Systems (RAS) undergraduate minor with a published 12-credit course list: required ECE/ME 5463 Introduction to Real Time Robotics Systems plus approved electives covering controls (ECE 3551, ME 5372), perception (CSE 5524 Computer Vision, ECE 5200 DSP), planning/autonomy (ECE 5553 Autonomy in Vehicles), industrial robotics (ISE 5520, ISE 5525) and human-centered automation (ISE 5740); undergraduate research credit (4998/4999) counts toward the minor. Rubric 4, not 5: no dedicated robotics degree, and the robotics course stack sits at the 5000 level shared with graduate students rather than forming an 8-course dedicated undergraduate sequence with a robotics capstone. [OSU-R1][OSU-R2][OSU-R3][OSU-R4]

degree_type: No AI or CS degree; AI is assembled inside the Engineering degree's Computing concentration [OLIN-S7]
program_archetype: D (undergraduate-centered) — project-based engineering college, not an AI program

best_fit_reason: A project-from-day-one curriculum, a 9:1 ratio with no graduate students, funded self-designed projects, and a year-long sponsored capstone with sponsors like Amazon Robotics, Blue Origin and Microsoft Research [OLIN-S1][OLIN-S35][OLIN-S21][OLIN-S43]. biggest_concern: The AI curriculum is four courses deep with unverified rotation and no graduate-level backstop, and cross-registration cannot include MIT [OLIN-S6][OLIN-S15][OLIN-S28]

score_notes.cs_foundations: E:Computing requires ENGR2510 Software Design, ENGR3525 Software Systems, and one of ENGR3515 Data Structures & Algorithms / ENGR3520 Foundations of CS — solid but only 16 concentration credits total and no required systems course [OLIN-S7].
score_notes.math_foundations: Linear algebra and multivariable calculus are built into required ENGX2000 QEA I/2, plus a 2-credit probability and statistics requirement and MTH2110 Discrete Math [OLIN-S6][OLIN-S7].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: Only four AI-relevant courses were verified in the catalog and schedules — ENGR3537 Machine Learning, ENGR3590 Computational Robotics, the Fall 2026 Generative AI course, and IDX2131 Data Science; no intro-AI, deep-learning, or NLP course exists [OLIN-S6][OLIN-S10].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: There is no second-level AI course after ENGR3537 Machine Learning; depth must come from ENGR3599 Special Topics or a cross-registered course [OLIN-S6][OLIN-S28].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: A dedicated generative-AI course (AHSE2199/ENGR3299, Fall 2026) covering both tool use and societal implications is verified as scheduled, but there is no LLM-systems or AI-agents course [OLIN-S10].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: Students may "choose or create an area of concentration," propose credit-bearing Passionate Pursuits with college funding, and a student-led ENGR3599 section has actually run [OLIN-S1][OLIN-S21][OLIN-S18].
score_notes.course_availability: ENGR3537 Machine Learning was verified offered only in Fall 2024, and with ~45 total faculty a single departure can remove a topic entirely [OLIN-S15][OLIN-S4].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: Summer research is a full-time paid residential position working directly with a faculty member, supported by a Summer Research Educational Program on publishing and conferences — but no funded-program application data or undergraduate publication record is published [OLIN-S25][OLIN-S24].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: 9:1 ratio with 378 students, no graduate students, no departments, and faculty evaluated on "expectations to develop students" rather than research output [OLIN-S35][OLIN-S4].
score_notes.project_based_learning: Projects start in semester one ("every student works on interdisciplinary projects") and culminate in SCOPE — a full September-to-May sponsored capstone in teams of 4–6 with sponsor-owned IP [OLIN-S1][OLIN-S20].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: Engineering: Robotics (E:Robo) concentration (EAC); 6 undergrad robotics courses. 3 labs, 3 competition teams.
score_notes.computing_resources: No GPU, cluster, or computing-resource inventory was found on any Olin page.
score_notes.industry_preparation: SCOPE sponsors in the last three cycles include Amazon Robotics, Blue Origin, Microsoft Research, Moderna, Pfizer, Boston Scientific and New Balance, and sponsors "have hired many students" [OLIN-S40][OLIN-S43][OLIN-S20].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: Olin's own page names Cornell, Stanford, Texas A&M and Colorado School of Mines as destinations and a 2013 Science* interview reported ~41% attending grad school, but the transcript would lack deep learning, NLP and intro AI [OLIN-S48][OLIN-S50][OLIN-S6].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: Olin awards only bachelor's degrees; the sole 4+1 in the catalog is for Wellesley students who spend a fifth year at Olin [OLIN-S1][OLIN-S6].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: A student's first-semester tally was "0 tests, 6 major group projects, 18 individual smaller projects and labs, 2 hackathons," and multiple accounts say "Oliners are always working on something. There are no slackers" [OLIN-S19][OLIN-S9].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: Classes are not curved, the first semester is Pass/No Record, and a current student states "there is very little competition… people are often helping each other" [OLIN-S52][OLIN-S22].
score_notes.student_agency: Passionate Pursuits let students propose a semester project with a faculty sponsor and college funding for transcript-noted non-degree credit, and the Candidates' Weekend design challenge is itself student-designed [OLIN-S21][OLIN-S13].
score_notes.community_within_scale: All 378 students live on campus in two halls with intentionally matched first-year roommates and hallmates — cohesive, but students themselves say the size "can feel limiting at times" [OLIN-S53][OLIN-S56][OLIN-S35][OLIN-S57].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: Documented design teams (SailBot, Baja, Human Powered Vehicle) come from a 2013 source and no current AI/CS club activity was verified; a ~378-student body limits simultaneous teams [OLIN-S27][OLIN-S35].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: Rather than a club directory, Olin funds individual pursuits — documented Passionate Pursuits include earning a pilot's license, improvised jazz, scuba diving and food writing — plus staff/faculty-led co-curriculars [OLIN-S61][OLIN-S62][OLIN-S45][OLIN-S8].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: There is no Greek life (83% of students in a Niche poll say so) and social life extends to Babson/Wellesley parties and club sports, but 79% of the same poll picked "some decent frat/house parties, weekends only" and students call the campus "somewhat isolated" [OLIN-S58][OLIN-S59][OLIN-S57].
score_notes.campus_engagement: A 100% four-year on-campus residency requirement means the campus does not empty; traditions like Glory Ball are student-named [OLIN-S53][OLIN-S58].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: Babson's Len Green Complex — 5,000 sq ft strength floor, 5,000 sq ft cardio area, 25-yard pool, indoor track, three courts, 6 a.m.–11 p.m. weekdays — is walking distance and described in an official Olin video as the most-used space after classes; Olin's own halls have only small exercise rooms [OLIN-S63][OLIN-S65][OLIN-S59].
score_notes.daily_life: Campus is adjacent to Babson and a car is not necessary on campus, but commuter rail and the T are "a few minutes drive" away and Needham is affluent-suburban rather than a college town [OLIN-S66].

admissions.overall_admit_rate_note: Fall 2023 (the most recent Common Data Set Olin has posted publicly): 928 applied / 201 admitted / 98 enrolled.
admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2023 residency detail from the CDS: 161 in-state applicants with 23 admitted; 599 out-of-state applicants with 157 admitted; 168 international applicants with 21 admitted. Olin is a private college, so residency carries no policy weight.
admissions.major_admit_context: Olin has no major-level admission gate at all — there are only three degrees (Engineering, Electrical & Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering) and robotics is pursued as the E:Robo concentration, where 'students work and study in a multi-disciplinary concentration focusing on software, sensing, mechanics, controls and integration aspects of robotics' [OLIN-S9]. The selectivity structure is completely different from a normal college: Olin runs a two-step process, inviting roughly 275-300 applicants to a mandatory on-campus Candidates' Weekend, and states 'Participation in CW is required to continue to be considered for admission to Olin' [OLIN-S3][OLIN-S2]. That makes the interview — rated Very Important in CDS C7, along with demonstrated interest — the decisive gate rather than any major choice [OLIN-S1]. There is also one deadline and no early plans: 'We don't have any early deadlines. There's one deadline for all applications' [OLIN-S7].
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: Olin offers no Early Decision — 'We don't have any early deadlines. There's one deadline for all applications.' CDS sections C21/C22 are blank.
admissions.sat_mid50_note: Fall 2023 CDS C9 (enrolled students): composite 25th 1500 / 50th 1530 / 75th 1560; EBRW 720/750/770; Math 760/780/790. For admitted (not enrolled) students, Olin's Class of 2028 profile reports SAT 1483-1528 and ACT 34-35, with 59% of admitted students submitting scores.
admissions.act_mid50_note: Fall 2023 CDS C9: ACT composite 25th 34 / 50th 35 / 75th 35, from 22 enrolled submitters (22%).
admissions.pct_submitting_sat_note: 46% of enrolled first-years (45 students) submitted SAT scores in Fall 2023; 22% submitted ACT. Olin's Class of 2028 profile reports 59% of admitted students submitted scores.
admissions.gpa_note: Fall 2023 CDS C12 average high school GPA 3.9 reported for 100% of enrolled first-years, and CDS C11 shows 43.0% with a 4.0 GPA. Olin's Class of 2028 profile lists an unweighted GPA range of 3.81-4.00.
admissions.test_policy_note: Olin states: 'We are extending the temporary suspension of our testing requirement through the 2026-27 application cycle' — i.e. explicitly covering Fall 2027 entry. The older Fall 2023 CDS answers C8 'No' to making use of SAT/ACT scores while noting all applicants may submit scores with no minimums. SAT code 2824, ACT code 1883.

Olin invites roughly 275-300 applicants and states 'Participation in CW is required to continue to be considered for admission to Olin.' Students living outside the continental United States 'will have a virtual interview.'

first_frc_scholarship.note: Olin publishes no FIRST/FRC or robotics-specific scholarship. Instead every admitted student receives the merit-based Olin Tuition Scholarship, which is $10,000 per year for incoming students for up to eight semesters. Olin's 2023-24 annual report states that the scholarship covered 50% of tuition through the class of 2029 but that 'starting with the class of 2030, we have made the decision to reduce the merit scholarship from 50% of Olin's annual tuition to $10,000 per year' — a Fall 2027 applicant falls in the $10,000/year regime. Olin also lists a four-year changemaker grant of $7,000-$17,000/year awarded through the two-step holistic admission process with no separate application.

robotics_curriculum_detail.score_basis: BS Engineering with a formal Engineering: Robotics (E:Robo) concentration backed by a published course list [OLIN-R1]. Undergrad robotics courses span perception/planning (ENGR3390 Fundamentals of Robotics: sensors, vision, navigation, localization, manipulation, mobility, control/planning [OLIN-R2]), computation (ENGR3590 Computational Introduction to Robotics), controls (ENGR3370), and systems integration (ENGR3392, industrial robot arm + vision, autonomous UGVs, intelligent assembly [OLIN-R3]), plus directed research/special topics in robotics. Year-long industry-sponsored SCOPE capstone (ENGR4190) regularly runs robotics projects [OLIN-R4][OLIN-R5][OLIN-R6]. Falls short of 5: fewer than 8 distinct robotics courses and no dedicated robotics degree (Olin awards only ECE, ME, and Engineering degrees).
robotics_curriculum_detail.minor_or_concentration: Engineering: Robotics (E:Robo) concentration within the BS in Engineering [OLIN-R1]
robotics_curriculum_detail.capstone: SCOPE (ENGR4190), year-long industry-sponsored senior capstone; robotics is a named focus area with sponsors including Amazon Robotics, Blue Origin, New Balance, GE Healthcare [OLIN-R4][OLIN-R5][OLIN-R6]

robotics_access_detail.score_basis: No robotics institute or center, and fewer than 10 documented robotics labs, so the rubric caps this at 3. Within that band Olin is at the top: three named robotics research settings (Olin Robot Lab, faculty lead David Barrett, with 15 named undergraduate researchers working on long-duration autonomous biomimetic undersea robots [OLIN-R7]; the student-run Olin Robotics Lab, self-described as a fully undergraduate research lab covering air/ground/surface/submersible autonomy [OLIN-R8]; and HIRO, the Human Interactions Robotics Laboratory [OLIN-R9]). Because Olin enrolls only undergraduates, all published lab rosters are undergraduates; access is by emailing a professor, available from the first semester [OLIN-R10]. Extensive fabrication access and multiple robotics-adjacent teams [OLIN-R11][OLIN-R12].

score_notes.cs_foundations: CIS 1200/1210/3200 + CIS 1600 + CIS 2450 are required, but theory of computation is not a required course in the 37-CU ARIN plan [PENN-S1].
score_notes.math_foundations: Requires ESE 2030 (AI-oriented linear algebra), ESE 3010 probability, ESE 4020 statistics and an optimization course, though the plan lists only MATH 1400/1410 for calculus [PENN-S1].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: 12 required AI CUs spanning six mandated categories (intro AI, ML, signals & systems, optimization & control, vision & language, AI project) plus ~30 electives [PENN-S1][PENN-S6].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: Undergraduates can reach CIS 6200 Advanced Topics in ML, CIS 6250 Theory of ML, ESE 6450 Deep Generative Models and ESE 6500 Learning in Robotics inside the major's own elective list [PENN-S1].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: ESE 3600 TinyML, ESE 5140 Graph Neural Networks, CIS 4270/5270 Trustworthy ML and ESE 6450 are listed, but no course fetched is titled for LLMs or AI agents [PENN-S1].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: Only 1 free-elective CU of 37, though 3 technical electives and 6 AI electives can be steered across CIS/ESE/MEAM/NETS [PENN-S1].
score_notes.course_availability: Course lists are published, but no class-search/schedule page was fetched to confirm which 6000-level AI electives actually ran in 2025-26 or their undergraduate seat limits.
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: PURM pays $5,000 to students in their 2nd or 4th semester, and SURE explicitly hosts undergraduates in GRASP, PRECISE and PRiML [PENN-S8][PENN-S12].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: GRASP publishes a named "best contact" faculty member for each of ~17 research groups, and Rachleff pairs rising sophomores with standing-faculty mentors [PENN-S27][PENN-S9].
score_notes.project_based_learning: A required AI Project CU appears in second-year spring and a two-semester senior design/thesis sequence is mandatory [PENN-S1].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: Dynamics, Controls and Robotics Concentration; 13 undergrad robotics courses. 12 labs, GRASP Laboratory, 3 competition teams.
score_notes.computing_resources: No fetched page documents undergraduate GPU/cluster access.
score_notes.industry_preparation: Penn Engineering's Class of 2025 median starting salary was $122,500, the highest of Penn's four undergraduate schools [PENN-S22].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: CIS 4100/4110 senior thesis, graduate-course access and funded early research exist, but no ARIN-specific PhD-placement data is published yet [PENN-S1][PENN-S8].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: Accelerated Master's (4+1) allows 3 double-counted CUs into an MSE such as CIS/MSE or GRASP's ROBO MSE, with junior-year application; no published admit rate [PENN-S3][PENN-S27].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: A student-run hackathon founded in 2009 drew 500+ participants over 48 hours in September 2025 [PENN-S23].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: No current multi-source student evidence on competitiveness was collected; the brief forbids inferring it.
score_notes.student_agency: Elective lists reach across six departments and law/philosophy/psychology, but only one free-elective CU exists in the 37-CU plan [PENN-S1].
score_notes.community_within_scale: SEAS is 1,782 undergraduates inside a 10,610-student university, and all students spend four semesters in a College House [PENN-S18][PENN-S20].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: PennApps XXVI is verified active, but individual AI/robotics team activity was not verified in this session [PENN-S23].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: No student-activities directory or current activity calendar was fetched.
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: ~25% Greek participation across 48 chapters (2012/2019 sources, STALE) and a mandatory two-year College House requirement that keeps first- and second-year housing out of Greek control [PENN-S21][PENN-S20].
score_notes.campus_engagement: Four-semester residency plus meal-plan requirement supports engagement, but only ~950 upperclass housing spaces exist, so most juniors/seniors live off campus [PENN-S20][PENN-S34].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: Pottruck is included in the General Fee, open to 11:30 p.m. weekdays, with an 8,000+ sq ft weight room, 40-ft climbing wall, three courts and Sheerr Pool [PENN-S19][PENN-S19a][PENN-S19c].
score_notes.daily_life: Contiguous University City campus with required two-year College House residency, though upperclass housing is randomized and limited [PENN-S20][PENN-S34].

why_us_ammunition: The GRASP Lab is large enough to name precisely: "16 faculty members, 90+ PhD and 130+ Robotics Master's graduate students and over 50 undergraduate students," spanning CIS, MEAM and ESE — and it explicitly includes undergraduates [PENN-S5].

Undergraduate participation is stated policy, not aspiration: "Undergraduate students take introductory courses in robotics, pursue independent studies, and conduct research in robotics, computer vision and machine learning," and GRASP maintains a dedicated undergraduate-research page [PENN-S5][PENN-S8].

Named subgroups make the Penn Engineering essay concrete: DAIR Lab, Daniilidis Group, Lifelong Machine Learning, Sung Robotics (soft/compliant robots) at GRASP@Levine; Kod*Lab, Kumar Robotics, ModLab and ScalAR at GRASP@PERCH in the Pennovation Center, plus the Rehabilitation Robotics Lab at Penn Medicine [PENN-S5].
Undergraduates genuinely present research: an ENG'26/C'26 GRASP member won 'Best Undergraduate Presenter' at the NDIA conference for reinforcement-learning work on autonomous drone racing [PENN-S6].

Founded in 1979 and interdisciplinary by design — GRASP's director frames it as faculty from ESE, CIS, MEAM "and even beyond Engineering, like the Medical School... all put together in one place" — which answers 'why Penn rather than a pure tech school' [PENN-S9].

Because Penn requires SAT/ACT for Fall 2027 and does not consider demonstrated interest, the leverage points are test scores plus a major-specific SEAS essay, not campus visits [PENN-S1][PENN-S3][PENN-S4].

name: Pennsylvania State University, University Park
degree_name: BS in Artificial Intelligence Engineering (Engineering/EECS); BS in Artificial Intelligence Methods and Applications (IST); BS in Computer Science (Engineering)
degree_type: Two dedicated AI bachelor's degrees in two different colleges, plus a CS BS
program_archetype: A (dedicated AI) + B (deep CS+AI) + E (large AI ecosystem)
major_access_full: GATED — entrance-to-major after 29-55 graded Penn State credits for all routes; CS is under administrative enrollment controls with a 3.20 GPA threshold, AIE 2.60, AIMA 2.00 [PSU-S5] [PSU-S2] [PSU-S3]
recommended_major_route: BS Artificial Intelligence Engineering (same EECS faculty as CS, required optimization/AI-systems/responsible-AI/capstone courses, materially lower published ETM threshold)
alternative_route: BS Computer Science (systems spine + ABET); BS AIMA in IST as a third, lowest-gated route with a domain focus area
primary_structural_risk: Two-to-three semesters in pre-major status with a 3.20 CS threshold that must be earned in calculus/physics and excludes AP and transfer credit from the 29-55 credit window [PSU-S5]
notable_ai_institute: Institute for Computational and Data Sciences (ICDS, Roar Collab); Center for Socially Responsible AI (CSRAI); Nittany AI Alliance [PSU-S10] [PSU-S19] [PSU-S20]
notable_undergraduate_research_program: Erickson Discovery Grant (43 awarded for summer 2024; fewer planned for 2026); Millennium Scholars Program; Nittany AI Challenge [PSU-S17] [PSU-S18] [PSU-S27] [PSU-S20]
fourplusone_available: Not found for University Park CS or AIE into an MS in CSE/AI (NOT PUBLISHED); the CS+MS CS IUG is Abington/Harrisburg only; a UP Integrated BS CS + M.I.A. International Affairs exists [PSU-S37] [PSU-S38] [PSU-S5]
fourplusone_name: Integrated Undergraduate-Graduate (IUG) plans under GCAC-210 (up to 40% of master's credits double-counted, max 15) [PSU-S35]
housing_guarantee: Yes for first-year students — and required; not guaranteed after year one [PSU-S64] [PSU-S66]
greek_participation: "Over 15%" per the official FSL page; 17% in spring 2024 per the 2024 FSL Program Review (history: 12% in 2011 → 19% in 2016 → 11% → 17%); only ~600 members live in chapter space [PSU-S47] [PSU-S48]
sports_influence: High enough that the IM Building and Natatorium close on home football Saturdays [PSU-S51]; broader cultural dominance UNVERIFIED
recreation_center: Distributed system — IM Building (166,500 sq ft, new 12,718 sq ft Gym 2, 16-lane climbing wall), White Building (81,200 sq ft, Esports Center), McCoy Natatorium, Tennis Center, Hepper Fitness Center, Stone Valley [PSU-S51] [PSU-S53] [PSU-S55]
best_fit_reason: A two-year-old dedicated AI engineering degree in the same school as CS that requires optimization, AI systems and tooling, responsible AI and a capstone — reachable through a published 2.60 ETM threshold rather than CS's 3.20 — backed by cluster access open to all Penn Staters with free GPU credits. On robotics: a dedicated BS in Electro-Mechanical Engineering Technology (EMET) (ABET engineering technology), with 10 undergrad robotics courses and 3 labs (ARL).
biggest_concern: The AI degree omits computer systems, software engineering and robotics; the accelerated master's path at University Park is undocumented; and travel from RDU always requires a connection into a three-destination airport
evidence_confidence: High for curriculum, ETM structure, cost, recreation, engagement and travel; medium for research access and faculty mentorship; low for accelerated graduate paths, AIE outcomes (no graduates yet), and graduate-school placement

score_notes.cs_foundations: AIE requires CMPSC 131/132, CMPSC 360 and A-I 305 but no computer-systems or software-engineering course; the CS BS route adds CMPSC 315/316/320/461/465/483W [PSU-S2] [PSU-S5].
score_notes.math_foundations: AIE requires MATH 140/141, MATH 225 Mathematical Foundations for Machine Learning, STAT 401, and AIE 355 Optimization for Machine Learning — a named optimization course, which is rare [PSU-S2].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: AIE requires knowledge representation (A-I 375), problem solving (A-I 370), ML (CMPSC 448/445), neural networks (EE 456), AI systems (A-I 410) and responsible AI (A-I 341W); CV and NLP are electives [PSU-S2] [PSU-S5].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: Depth comes from 27 technical-elective credits with ≥15 at the 400 level, but no 500-level AI course was found listed as an ordinary undergraduate elective [PSU-S2].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: A-I 410 AI Systems and Tools and A-I 341W Responsible AI are required and current in spirit, but no named generative-AI, LLM or AI-agents course appears in any plan of study [PSU-S2] [PSU-S3] [PSU-S5].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: AIE's 27-credit technical-elective block and AIMA's 9-credit application focus area (options from national security to psychology to agriculture) give real room to shape the degree [PSU-S2] [PSU-S3].
score_notes.course_availability: CMPSC 442 and CMPSC 448 have live instructor course sites, but AIE is only in its second year and per-course seat data is NOT PUBLISHED [PSU-S8] [PSU-S9] [PSU-S1].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: The Erickson Discovery Grant is open to all undergraduates with a faculty mentor, but only 43 were awarded for summer 2024 and Penn State said the 2026 cycle would have fewer [PSU-S17] [PSU-S18].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: The AIE program contacts are named faculty who also teach the undergraduate ML course, and Millennium Scholars requires faculty-mentored research — but no undergraduate co-authorship evidence was found [PSU-S1] [PSU-S8] [PSU-S26].
score_notes.project_based_learning: The Learning Factory has run 3,000+ sponsored capstones for 750+ sponsors, and both AIE (AIE 489W) and CS (CMPSC 483W) require a capstone [PSU-S16] [PSU-S2] [PSU-S5].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: BS in Electro-Mechanical Engineering Technology (EMET) (ETAC); 10 undergrad robotics courses. 3 labs, ARL.
score_notes.computing_resources: Roar Collab access is stated to be available to all Penn Staters, undergraduates are an eligible account category with a PI sponsor, and free READ Credits work on GPU hardware [PSU-S10] [PSU-S12] [PSU-S13].
score_notes.industry_preparation: 2024-25 self-reported average starting salary was $92,503 for CMPSC and $96,650 for CMPEN, with co-op pay averaging $26.55/hour across 107 CMPSC respondents [PSU-S42].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: Schreyer requires an honors thesis and Millennium reports >50% of alumni entering graduate education, but no major-level PhD-placement data is published [PSU-S23] [PSU-S27].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: The Integrated BS+MS in Computer Science is offered at Abington/Harrisburg, not University Park; the only UP CS integrated plan found pairs CS with an M.I.A. in International Affairs [PSU-S37] [PSU-S38] [PSU-S5].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: HackPSU ran in Spring 2026 and is scheduled for Oct 24, 2026, alongside a Feb 2026 sprint hackathon and 50+ engineering organizations [PSU-S29] [PSU-S30] [PSU-S31] [PSU-S32].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: Pressure is front-loaded and structural: CS entrance-to-major requires a 3.20 cumulative GPA earned in calculus and physics within 29-55 graded Penn State credits, excluding AP credit [PSU-S5].
score_notes.student_agency: AIMA lets a research project (A-I 494) substitute for the two-semester capstone, and AIE's 27-credit elective block plus Schreyer honors-options let students reshape courses [PSU-S3] [PSU-S2] [PSU-S23].
score_notes.community_within_scale: Schreyer (~2,000, 2% of students) and Millennium (125 scholars, cohort housing for two years) are strong but small islands within 42,822 University Park undergraduates [PSU-S25] [PSU-S27] [PSU-S22].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: ACM, Association of Women in Computing, Coder's Guild, Competitive Cyber Security Organization, Autonomous Robotics Competition Club and HackPSU are all currently listed or dated within 12 months [PSU-S33] [PSU-S29].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: The University lists more than 1,000 student organizations, and over 400 of them participate in THON alone [PSU-S32] [PSU-S46].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: Official figures put affiliation at 15-17%, only ~600 members live in chapter space, and THON draws 16,500 volunteers across 400+ organizations [PSU-S47] [PSU-S48] [PSU-S45].
score_notes.campus_engagement: THON 2026 raised a record $18,841,726.53 with 16,500 student volunteers — the largest student-run philanthropy in the world [PSU-S45] [PSU-S46].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: Fee-included access to five facilities (IM 166,500 sq ft, White 81,200, Natatorium, Tennis Center, Hepper) including a new 12,718 sq ft Gym 2 with eight Olympic platforms and a 16-lane climbing wall [PSU-S51] [PSU-S53] [PSU-S55].
score_notes.daily_life: SCE has only three nonstop destinations on two airlines with no RDU service, and first-year students may not have cars [PSU-S56] [PSU-S57] [PSU-S58].

admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2025 (University Park): 106,547 applicants, 58,952 admitted, 9,148 enrolled = 55.3% [PSU-S1]. In-state 12,096/21,321 = 56.7%; out-of-state 38,846/72,861 = 53.3%; international 8,010/12,365 = 64.8% [PSU-S1] (INFERRED - division of CDS C1 counts). Residency barely moves the university-level rate, and 68% of applications are from out of state - Penn State is structurally the most out-of-state-friendly public in this batch.
admissions.major_admit_context: Penn State admits to the university and campus first, then to the major through Entrance to Major (ETM), so the competitive gate is entirely internal. Both target majors carry the same explicit control: the Undergraduate Bulletin states for Computer Science, B.S. at University Park that 'This program currently has administrative enrollment controls. Administrative Enrollment Controls are initiated when limitations of space, faculty, or other resources in a major prevent accommodating all students who request them,' and for first-year students entering Summer 2026 / Fall 2026 / Spring 2027 requires enrollment in the College of Engineering or the Division of Undergraduate Studies, 29-55 graded Penn State credits, C or better in CMPSC 121 or 131, CMPSC 122 or 132, MATH 140, MATH 141 and PHYS 211, and 'a minimum cumulative grade-point average (GPA) of 3.20' [PSU-S7]. Mechanical Engineering, B.S. at University Park carries the identical structure and the same 3.20 minimum with CHEM 110, EDSGN 100, MATH 140, MATH 141 and PHYS 211 [PSU-S8]. Aerospace Engineering also sits at 3.20 while, for contrast, Architectural Engineering is 2.60 [PSU-S9]. The mechanics: you become eligible after 29 graded Penn State credits, must request the change before exceeding 55 graded credits, must meet the published minimum GPA at the time you apply, must be scheduled for or have completed the ETM courses with a C or better, and then request the major in LionPATH [PSU-S9]. Note the same 3.20 threshold applies at University Park while satellite-campus versions of both majors sit at 2.60 - with the caveat that 'In the event that the major is under enrollment control, a higher minimum cumulative grade-point average is likely to be needed' [PSU-S7][PSU-S8]. One admissions-strategy wrinkle: applicants naming University Park and fall entry are asked whether they would accept summer start, and Penn State states plainly that 'Saying yes to this question will increase your chances of admission to University Park because summer admission is slightly less competitive than fall admission,' with summer then mandatory [PSU-S6]. Practical consequence for a robotics applicant: getting into Penn State is comparatively easy, but you must produce a 3.20 college GPA in a calculus/physics/programming sequence during your first year to actually enter CS or ME - plan for that, and consider the summer-start option and the 2+2 campus plan as levers.
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: Penn State offers no Early Decision plan (CDS C21 = No) [PSU-S1].
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 records an EA closing date of 11/01 with notification 12/24 but publishes no EA applicant/admit counts [PSU-S1].
admissions.test_detail_note: Fall 2025 enrolled: SAT submitted by 28.60% (2,616), ACT by 4.98% (456). SAT composite 25th/50th/75th = 1280/1340/1410; ACT 28/30/32 [PSU-S1].
admissions.gpa_note: Penn State reports only 12% of enrolled first-year students with a 4.0 GPA and an average high school GPA of 3.67 (CDS C11/C12) - by far the lowest GPA profile in this batch, reflecting unweighted reporting [PSU-S1]. Class rank: 37% top tenth, 74% top quarter [PSU-S1].
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: TEST-OPTIONAL. CDS C7 rates test scores as Considered [PSU-S1] and the admissions site states 'For first-year applicants, Penn State is test-optional, so submitting scores is not required for your application,' with applicants choosing whether scores are considered, self-reporting via MyPennState, Penn State using 'a student's highest combined score from one single test date' and NOT superscoring, and not accepting the optional Enhanced ACT Science section. Exception: the Accelerated Premedical-Medical Program requires scores by its October 13 deadline [PSU-S5].
admissions.c7_note: Penn State's review is the most narrowly academic in this batch: GPA Very Important, rigor Important, test scores and talent/ability Considered, and essays, recommendations, extracurriculars, character, volunteer work, work experience and demonstrated interest all Not Considered [PSU-S1]. Geographical residence and state residency are Considered. Implication: a strong robotics resume will not move the Penn State admission decision - it matters for scholarships (including the College of Engineering FIRST award) rather than for admission.

decision_dates.ea_deadline: CONFLICTING: the first-year deadlines page states 'our Early Action Deadline is November 1' [PSU-S3], while a Penn State news release states 'the University has moved its deadline for Early Action from Nov. 1 to Nov. 15' [PSU-S4]. The news release contains COVID-era context (test-optional 'for the first time', canceled test dates), so it may not describe the Fall 2027 cycle. Treat November 1 as the safe date and re-verify in fall 2026.
decision_dates.ea_notify: By December 24 ('Students applying for Early Action are assured a decision from the University by Dec. 24') [PSU-S4]; CDS C22 notification 12/24 [PSU-S1]
decision_dates.rd_deadline: No closing date - 'After November 1, Penn State reviews applications on a rolling basis'; the application closes July 28 [PSU-S3]; CDS C14 records no closing date [PSU-S1]
decision_dates.deposit_deadline: May 1 ('Students will still have until May 1 to accept offers') [PSU-S4]
decision_dates.restrictions: Early Action is non-binding and is the priority date for scholarships and campus placement; no Early Decision. Applicants select a first-choice and alternate campus, and University Park fall applicants may opt into a mandatory summer start to improve odds [PSU-S6].

admissions.supplemental_essays_note: No required essay was found: CDS C7 marks the application essay as Not Considered [PSU-S1], and neither the how-to-apply page nor the steps-to-apply page lists an essay or personal statement requirement or word limit [PSU-S5][PSU-S6]. The commonly cited '500-word Penn State personal statement' could NOT be verified from a Penn State source on 2026-08-16 - if the live application offers an optional personal statement, treat it as optional and low-leverage given the CDS weighting. Application mechanics that DO matter: apply via MyPennState or Common App, and complete the STARS self-reported academic record in MyPennState (Penn State 'does not accept the high school record that is available in the Common App') [PSU-S6].
why_us_ammunition: The Applied Research Laboratory at Penn State, 'established at Penn State in 1945 at the request' of the US Navy, is a US Navy University Affiliated Research Center that 'partners with industry on many of our programs' and runs mentorship and outreach programs 'from high school through graduate school' - the strongest institutional research hook, though the About page does not itemize robotics labs [PSU-S12].

Penn State's scale is a legitimate argument: 106,547 first-year applications and more than 275 academic programs across campuses, with the 2+2 plan letting students start at one campus and finish at University Park [PSU-S1][PSU-S6].

There is an institutional FIRST pipeline: the College of Engineering FIRST Scholarship pays $2,500/year up to $10,000 for FRC/FTC alumni admitted to engineering who maintain a 3.0 college GPA [PSU-S10] - name it, and apply through the Recently Admitted Students scholarship application.

Entrance-to-Major transparency is usable in an essay about preparation: CS and ME both require a 3.20 GPA with a defined calculus/physics/programming sequence [PSU-S7][PSU-S8][PSU-S9], so describing how FRC build-season discipline maps to that first-year workload is concrete.

Because Penn State's review ignores essays, activities and demonstrated interest [PSU-S1], the highest-value 'why us' work here is not the application - it is the post-admission scholarship applications and the ETM plan; budget effort accordingly.

robotics_curriculum_detail.score_basis: University Park offers 5-7 undergraduate robotics courses including required controls (ME 455 Automatic Control Systems, ME 450 Modeling of Dynamic Systems) and robotics/mechatronics (ME 456 Introduction to Robotics, ME 454 Mechatronics — a required ME course with weekly two-hour labs, ME 445 Microcomputer Interfacing, EE 483 Introduction to Automation and Robotics Systems), plus a genuine capstone in the Learning Factory (ME 440W). Rubric 4 rather than 5: no robotics degree and no robotics minor at University Park — the Mechatronics minor is offered at Penn State Harrisburg (Capital College), not UP. Perception/planning is the weak axis: ME 459 Machine Learning in Mechanical Engineering is the closest documented offering. [PSU-R1][PSU-R2][PSU-R3][PSU-R4][PSU-R5]
