admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2025 (West Lafayette): 87,220 applicants, 37,881 admitted, 9,656 enrolled = 43.4% [PU-S1]. In-state 8,559/12,040 = 71.1%; out-of-state 25,650/58,853 = 43.6%; international 3,672/16,327 = 22.5% [PU-S1] (INFERRED - division of CDS C1 counts). Purdue is unusual in this batch: the out-of-state rate (43.6%) is close to the headline rate, so a North Carolina applicant is not structurally penalized at the university level - the selectivity sits inside the major.
admissions.major_admit_context: Purdue admits engineering applicants into First-Year Engineering (FYE), not into a degree program: 'The first year of all Engineering programs at Purdue is common, and incoming students are admitted to First-Year Engineering (FYE) rather than to one of the 16 Engineering degree programs,' and after completing FYE requirements students move through the 'Transition to Major' (T2M) process [PU-S5]. T2M outcomes are good but not guaranteed: 'Over the past five years 93% to 95% of students who have met minimum requirements for transition-to-major have received their first choice,' while 'Admission to Engineering degree programs may be competitive, especially for programs that are at or above enrollment capacity,' judged on GPA, the Engineering Admissions Index (EAI) and other factors [PU-S5]. Two programs are named as capacity-limited: Aeronautical and Astronautical Engineering (AAE) and Mechanical Engineering (ME) - 'Students with a cumulative GPA of 2.99 or below, and who request majors with capacity limitations (currently AAE and ME), will be advised by FYE Advisors' [PU-S5]. So for a robotics applicant targeting ME, first choice is usually granted but a sub-3.0 first year puts it at risk. Computer Science sits outside engineering and is the harder door from inside: CS change-of-degree-objective (CODO) approvals 'will be made on a SPACE AVAILABLE BASIS and will be determined through an academic review of all applicants,' with the highest consideration going to students earning an A- in CS 18000, a B or better in an approved calculus course, and a minimum 3.00 cumulative GPA; students on academic probation are ineligible, only the first or second attempt at a required course counts, and decisions are made at the end of each semester [PU-S6]. Purdue also tells applicants directly that 'Changing majors or locations is never guaranteed' and lets them list a primary major plus an optional alternate [PU-S3]. Practical consequence: name CS on the application if CS is the goal - do not plan to CODO in - and expect ME to be reachable through FYE with a solid first-year GPA.

why_us_ammunition: First-Year Engineering plus Transition to Major is a genuine differentiator to write about: you spend a common first year and then choose among 16 degree programs, with 93-95% of qualified students getting their first choice [PU-S5] - frame it as wanting exposure before committing.

Aeronautics and Astronautics facilities are concrete and quotable: Purdue describes its UAS Research and Test Facility as the 'World's largest Motion Capture facility for UAS research' and claims world leadership in laminar-turbulent transition in hypersonic flows and in Earth remote sensing via reflected satellite transmissions [PU-S8] - strong for drone/autonomy interests.

The Robotics Accelerator exists specifically to pool robotics work across campus - 'Be it for medical, agricultural, search and rescue, assistive robotics, or any other application' - which supports a cross-college robotics narrative [PU-S9].

Purdue publishes a robotics/cyber-physical-systems course landscape spanning AAE, CS and CNIT (e.g. CS 49000 Introduction to Robotics, CNIT 56200 Assistive Technology and Robotics, CNIT 56300 Software Design and Development for Robotics) [PU-S10] - naming courses shows real research.

Purdue counts demonstrated interest (level of applicant's interest = Considered) and weights the essay Very Important [PU-S1], so a specific, Purdue-only 'opportunities' answer in the 250-word question is unusually high-leverage here.

admissions.admit_rate_note_note: RIT's CDS does not publish an in-state vs out-of-state admit split.
admissions.major_admit_context: RIT reviews by program, and it says so in the context of applying early: Early Decision I lets an applicant 'Stand out in a small pool of applicants and benefit from higher acceptance rates, especially for competitive majors', and applications received after a deadline 'will be reviewed, but on a space-available basis for each program' [RIT-S2]. The numbers bear this out — ED I admitted 1,028 of 1,405 applicants (73.2%), only marginally above the 71.0% overall rate, so the ED advantage at RIT is program-level rather than institution-level [RIT-S1]. Program-specific requirements also exist: an art portfolio is required for bachelor's programs in the School of Art, School of Design and School of Film and Animation, and RIT recommends STEM applicants include the optional ACT Science section if submitting ACT scores [RIT-S3][RIT-S7]. For a robotics applicant the most consequential program-level fact is financial: the RIT/FIRST Scholarship is worth $14,000 per year but 'is not stackable. It cannot be combined with other RIT merit-based scholarships', while base first-year merit scholarships already range from $14,000 to $27,000 annually [RIT-S5].
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: Fall 2025 ED (both rounds combined as reported in CDS C21): 1,405 applications, 1,028 admits.
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 confirms a non-restrictive Early Action plan closing November 1 with notification January 31, but RIT does not report EA application or admit counts.
admissions.sat_mid50_note: Fall 2025 CDS C9: composite 25th 1310 / 50th 1380 / 75th 1440, from 1,206 enrolled submitters.
admissions.pct_submitting_sat_note: 41.0% of enrolled first-years submitted SAT scores; 8.0% submitted ACT scores.
admissions.gpa_note: CDS C12 average high school GPA 3.90, reported for 98.6% of enrolled first-years; CDS C10 shows 40% in the top tenth of their class. RIT expects 'a strong performance in a college preparatory program', generally 4 years of English, 3-4 years of mathematics, 2-3 years of science and 3 years of social studies and/or history.
admissions.test_policy_note: CDS C8 marks SAT/ACT 'Not Required for Admission, but Consider if Submitted (Test-Optional)' with a latest-receipt date of February 1, and RIT's Academic Profile states 'RIT is test-optional. You may choose to apply SAT/ACT test-optional, or choose to have scores considered with your application.' Neither is stamped specifically to Fall 2027, so applicability is inferred from a standing, program-wide policy.

interview.mechanism: No required or evaluative admissions interview is published; CDS C7 rates Interview only 'Considered'. RIT's published interview-adjacent touchpoints are campus visits and counselor meetings, and program-specific portfolio review substitutes for interviews in art/design/film programs.

first_frc_scholarship.name: RIT/FIRST Scholarship
first_frc_scholarship.amount: $14,000 per year ($7,000 per semester) of full-time enrollment in required coursework
first_frc_scholarship.renewable: Yes — renewable; up to 20 awarded each year
first_frc_scholarship.stackable_with_merit: No — RIT states: 'This scholarship is not stackable. It cannot be combined with other RIT merit-based scholarships.' Since base first-year merit awards run $14,000-$27,000 annually, students receiving the highest-valued scholarship they qualify for should note that the FIRST award may not add to a larger merit offer.
first_frc_scholarship.application_mechanism: Separate scholarship application at rit.edu/first-scholarship (hosted on RIT's join.rit.edu portal), submitted before the undergraduate admission application deadline for the selected term. The form collects FIRST team name and number and program (FIRST Robotics Competition or FIRST Tech Challenge), high school and CEEB code, and intended major; the term dropdown includes Fall 2027. Only first-year students are eligible ('Only first year students are eligible for consideration').
first_frc_scholarship.deadline: Must apply for admission to RIT by January 15 to be considered; the scholarship application must be submitted prior to the admission application deadline for the selected term

why_us_ammunition: The RIT/FIRST Scholarship is a named, $14,000-per-year renewable award created specifically for high school FIRST participants, with up to 20 given each year and its own application at rit.edu/first-scholarship — the most directly FRC-targeted award in this set alongside WPI's [RIT-S5][RIT-S6].
The FIRST scholarship application asks for team name, team number and program (FRC or FTC), so an applicant's competition record is formally part of RIT's evaluation record [RIT-S6].

RIT frames Early Decision I as a way to 'benefit from higher acceptance rates, especially for competitive majors' and to 'Get a full review of your scholarship and financial aid eligibility before committing' — useful for explaining a genuine first-choice commitment [RIT-S2].

Base first-year merit scholarships range from $14,000 to $27,000 annually ($56,000 to $108,000 over the degree) and require no separate application, which supports an affordability-driven Why-RIT argument [RIT-S5].
RIT recommends STEM applicants include the optional ACT Science section — a small but concrete signal of how technically the institution reads applications [RIT-S7].

admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2025 residency detail from the CDS: in-state 1,341 applicants with 967 admitted (72.1%); out-of-state 3,614 applicants with 3,075 admitted (85.1%); international 1,036 applicants with 805 admitted (77.7%). Rose-Hulman is private, so Indiana residency confers no advantage — in fact the in-state admit rate is the lowest of the three groups.
admissions.major_admit_context: Rose-Hulman has no separate major-level admission gate and no published capacity caps; admission is to the institute with an intended major. What matters instead is preparation: 'Incoming students are expected to complete the following high school courses, at a minimum, before enrolling: Four years of math (through trigonometry/precalculus), Four years of English, Three years of lab science (one year EACH of biology, chemistry, and physics)' [RHIT-S3]. That physics-and-chemistry-and-biology requirement is stricter than most peers in this set. Rose-Hulman recently restructured its computing offering, launching 'a unified computer science major with new AI, cybersecurity and data science specializations' [RHIT-S7]. Applying by the November 1 Early Action date is the real lever: 'To be considered for admission to Rose-Hulman and the new Provost Scholarship, students must apply by the November 1 non-binding early action date', and Rose-Hulman tells students to 'Apply by Nov. 1 for Early Action (non-binding) for maximum consideration for scholarships' [RHIT-S4][RHIT-S8].
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: Rose-Hulman offers no Early Decision plan — applicants 'can choose to apply Early Action (non-binding) or Regular Decision', and CDS C21 indicates no ED plan.
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 confirms a non-restrictive Early Action plan (closing November 1, notification December 15) but publishes no EA application or admit counts.
admissions.sat_mid50_note: Fall 2025 CDS C9: composite 25th 1270 / 50th 1380 / 75th 1450 (mean 1357), from 173 enrolled submitters.
admissions.pct_submitting_sat_note: 35.7% of enrolled first-years submitted SAT scores; 16.5% submitted ACT scores.
admissions.gpa_note: CDS C12 average high school GPA 3.91, reported for 97.9% of enrolled first-years; CDS C11 shows 59.5% with a 4.0 GPA and CDS C10 shows 59.2% in the top tenth of their class.
admissions.test_policy_note: CDS C8 answers 'Yes (Test-Optional Policy in effect)' and marks SAT/ACT 'Not Required for Admission, but Consider if Submitted (Test-Optional)' explicitly for the Fall 2027 cycle; latest receipt date February 1. Rose-Hulman's site adds: 'Rose-Hulman does not require standardized test scores for admission. However, if you would like to have your scores considered, you can self-report them on the application ... We continue to embrace a holistic admission process.' ACT code 1232, SAT code 1668.

interview.mechanism: Video/interview submissions are optional and explicitly no-penalty. robotics_curriculum_detail.score_basis: ANCHOR CORRECTED: Rose-Hulman does have a Multidisciplinary Minor in Robotics with a published course list [ROSE-R1]. All students in the minor take CSSE 120 Introduction to Software Development, ME/CSSE 435 Robotics Engineering, and ECE 425 Introduction to Mobile Robotics, then add major-specific courses (ME 230/430 Mechatronic Systems, ECE 320 Linear Control Systems, ME 306 Control Systems, ME 445 Robot Dynamics and Control, CSSE 463 Image Recognition) plus robotics electives (CSSE 461 Computer Vision, ECE 497 Advanced Mobile Robotics, Robotics Studio, Swarm Intelligence, BE 520 Brain Machine Interfaces, BE 543 Neuroprosthetics) [ROSE-R1][ROSE-R2]. That yields 5-7 undergraduate robotics courses including controls and perception, plus a three-term multidisciplinary senior design option in robotics - a 4. Not a 5 because there is no robotics degree and the required distinct robotics-titled course count stays below 8.

admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2025: 14,356 applicants, 9,655 admitted, 1,394 enrolled = 67.3% [RPI-S1]. New York residents 2,917/4,319 = 67.5%; out-of-state 6,125/8,947 = 68.5%; international 613/1,090 = 56.2% [RPI-S1] (INFERRED - division of CDS C1 counts). Residency is irrelevant here, and RPI is by far the least selective school in this batch on paper - the constraint is cost and yield (1,394 enrolled from 9,655 admits), which is why merit and FIRST scholarships matter more than admissibility.
admissions.major_admit_context: RPI admits to a school rather than to a capacity-controlled major: applicants select a program (for example a School of Engineering major or Undeclared Engineering), and the application requires no program-specific essay except for five named programs - Accelerated Physician-Scientist (B.S./M.D.), Architecture, Electronic Arts, Games and Simulation Arts and Sciences, and Music [RPI-S4]. RPI publishes NO major-level or school-level admit rates, and none appear in the CDS [RPI-S1][RPI-S4]; there is likewise no published GPA gate, capacity limit, or restricted change-of-major process for Computer Science or Mechanical Engineering on the pages fetched on 2026-08-16 [RPI-S4]. For a robotics applicant the notable structural feature is curricular rather than competitive: RPI now offers a B.S. in Robotics Engineering 'Jointly administered by the Departments of Electrical, Computer, and Systems Engineering and Mechanical, Aerospace, and Nuclear Engineering,' combining 'mechanical design, electronics, computing, and artificial intelligence' with coursework in sensing, actuation, control and intelligent decision-making [RPI-S5]. Practical consequence: you can apply directly into robotics rather than assembling it from a mechanical or CS degree, and there is no internal admission tournament to survive after arrival - the trade-off is a 67% admit rate that makes RPI a likely-admit whose real question is net price.
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: CDS 2025-2026: 317 Early Decision applications, 219 admitted = 69.1% (INFERRED - division of CDS C21 counts) [RPI-S1]. The ED rate is essentially identical to the overall rate, so ED at RPI buys certainty and demonstrated commitment (which the CDS marks as Considered), not a statistical edge - and it forfeits the ability to compare aid offers.
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 records Early Action closing 12/1 with notification 1/29 but publishes no EA applicant/admit counts [RPI-S1].
admissions.test_detail_note: Fall 2025 enrolled: SAT submitted by 53% (733 students), ACT by 13% (180). SAT composite 25th/50th/75th = 1380/1450/1500; ACT 31/33/34 [RPI-S1]. Scores of admitted students are high relative to the admit rate - a strong score is the main merit-aid lever.
admissions.gpa_note: 43% of enrolled first-year students reported a 4.0 GPA; average high school GPA 3.93 with 96% submitting (CDS C11/C12) [RPI-S1]. Class rank: 63% top tenth, 90% top quarter [RPI-S1].
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: TEST-OPTIONAL, explicitly for this applicant's cycle: 'Any student who applies to attend Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute as an undergraduate in the fall of 2027 will be able to choose whether or not to submit SAT or ACT scores,' and 'RPI will remain test-optional through the Fall 2030 application cycle' [RPI-S3]. Mechanics: answer the Common App question 'Would you like RPI to consider your ACT/SAT scores as a part of your application file?'; if you say yes, the file is incomplete until scores arrive (official or self-reported); changes require emailing adm_updates@rpi.edu; Regular Decision applicants may use tests taken before January 31; 'not submitting test scores does not lower your chances of admission' and 'RPI does not use test scores to determine student eligibility for merit aid.' Exception: Physician-Scientist (B.S./M.D.) applicants must submit official scores [RPI-S3][RPI-S4].
admissions.c7_note: RPI is one of two schools in this batch that count level of applicant's interest (Considered) [RPI-S1] - campus visits, portal engagement, the optional GLIMPSE video and an ED application all register. Alumni relation Considered; interview, geographical residence, state residency and religious affiliation Not Considered [RPI-S1].

admissions.supplemental_essays_note: CONFLICTING with the expectation of two RPI short essays: the official apply page fetched on 2026-08-16 states the general personal statement satisfies the essay requirement for all programs except the five named ones [RPI-S4]. If the live Common App member section adds 'why RPI' questions for 2026-27, treat them as new.
why_us_ammunition: RPI's B.S. in Robotics Engineering is jointly administered by ECSE and MANE and 'provides a rigorous, interdisciplinary education that combines mechanical design, electronics, computing, and artificial intelligence' - a single degree instead of a stitched-together path [RPI-S5].

The program's own rationale cites growing demand and 'increasing K-12 engagement in robotics' - i.e. FIRST-style pipelines are explicitly part of why the degree exists, which makes your FRC record on-thesis rather than incidental [RPI-S5].

Curriculum is explicit about sensing, actuation, control and intelligent decision-making 'within unified robotic systems,' with named strands in Electrical, Computer, Mechanical Engineering and AI/Machine Learning [RPI-S5] - reference specific strands rather than 'robotics' generally.

RPI counts demonstrated interest and alumni relation in review [RPI-S1] and offers the optional GLIMPSE video [RPI-S4], so a visit, a video and (if RPI is a clear first choice) an ED I application are the levers that actually move this file.

The FIRST scholarship pathway is the largest in this batch - up to ten four-year awards with a minimum $12,500/year and $50,000 total - but it is applied for in 11th grade [RPI-S6], so this is the school where FIRST participation can be converted into money earliest.

why_us_ammunition: Swarthmore is one of very few liberal arts colleges with an ABET-accredited engineering degree: "The Swarthmore College Engineering Program's bachelor of science in engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission (EAC) of ABET" [SWAT-S4].

The engineering-plus-liberal-arts model is stated institutionally — "Swarthmore College is a liberal arts college, and all our students, including the engineering majors, get a liberal arts education" — which is the honest framing for an applicant who wants robotics plus breadth [SWAT-S6].

Research access is unusually high for the college's size: engineering students are encouraged to tour the research labs in Singer Hall and talk with faculty, and "between a quarter and third of all students join in faculty research, many finding their names on a published paper" [SWAT-S5].

Depth beyond Swarthmore's own catalog is built in: "If you decide to take more specialized courses you can take courses at the University of Pennsylvania's School of Engineering and Applied Science" — a direct answer to the 'small college, narrow robotics offerings' objection [SWAT-S5].

Because the second supplement asks about "a topic that has fascinated you recently," a specific robotics or AI rabbit hole (a control problem, a paper, a build failure) fits the prompt exactly as written [SWAT-S2].

admissions.admit_rate_note: CDS 2024-25 (Fall 2024) C1: 54,905 first-year applicants (27,374 M + 27,531 W), 31,472 admitted (15,617 + 15,855), 12,498 enrolled = 57.32% [TAMU-S1]. TAMU does not publish a resident/non-resident split in its CDS residency table. The in-state tilt is structural rather than numerically disclosed: C7 marks STATE RESIDENCY and GEOGRAPHICAL RESIDENCE as 'Important' [TAMU-S1], Texas top-10% applicants receive decisions first (from September, 'typically within three weeks of completing their admission file') while holistic-review applicants wait until October or later [TAMU-S2]. A North Carolina applicant is in the holistic pool by definition and should discount the 57% headline (INFERRED — no official OOS rate published).
admissions.major_admit_context: Texas A&M engineering does NOT admit to a major. Every engineering admit enters as a GENERAL ENGINEERING student and competes later through Entry to a Major (ETAM): 'we don't ask you to decide on a major during the first year' [TAMU-S3]. ETAM 'uses a priority method that places students in their highest preferred major possible based on their academic performance, their ETAM application content and the program's capacity' [TAMU-S4]. Mechanics for the Class of 2030 (Fall 2026 entrants, one year ahead of this applicant but the same published structure): students must rank at least THREE majors and may rank up to FIVE; they get THREE attempts, starting with the second semester and ending no later than the fourth semester in the college; eligibility requires at least two semesters of A&M coursework with a minimum 2.0 cumulative AND 2.0 term GPA plus the required course sequence with C or better; for a Fall 2026 entrant the first application window is March 2027 with decisions in July 2027 [TAMU-S4]. THE CRITICAL POINT FOR A ROBOTICS APPLICANT: Multidisciplinary Engineering Technology - Mechatronics (MXET, awarded as a BS in MXET, with an alternative STEM Educator track) [TAMU-S5] and Computer Science & Engineering (CSCE) are BOTH allocated out of that same capacity-constrained ETAM pool. So at TAMU the robotics-relevant selectivity is deferred by a year and converted into a first-year GPA competition against a cohort of several thousand general engineering students — the opposite of UT Austin's direct-admit model. Additional capacity risk on the admissions side: 'Students selected from the waitlist may be asked to select a new major due to capacity limitations,' and engineering pathway offers (which may route an applicant to Blinn TEAM, Galveston or McAllen rather than College Station) begin in January [TAMU-S2]. TAMU publishes no ETAM placement rates by major on the pages reviewed, so the probability of landing MXET or CSCE specifically is officially unquantified.
admissions.gpa_note: TAMU does NOT report average high school GPA or a GPA distribution — CDS 2024-25 C11 and C12 are blank/zero [TAMU-S1]. It reports class rank instead, and the rank data is the real signal: 66.57% of enrolled first-years were in the top tenth of their high school class, 91.40% in the top quarter, 99.01% in the top half, with 73.39% of the class submitting rank [TAMU-S1]. Test detail from C9: 71.00% submitted SAT (n=8,888) and 19.00% submitted ACT (n=2,328); SAT composite 25/50/75 = 1160/1270/1390, EBRW 580/630/690, Math 570/640/710; ACT composite 25/28/31 [TAMU-S1]. Because GPA is unpublished, the odds engine should band TAMU on the SAT range plus the top-decile rank concentration.
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: TEST-OPTIONAL — this CORRECTS the brief. The official freshman page states verbatim: 'Texas A&M University is test optional and will not require ACT or SAT scores for freshman applicants. We encourage students who have test scores to send them. The submission of test scores will not create any unfair advantage or disadvantage for those students who provide them.' Scores must come from the testing agency, the highest total from a single test date is used (no cross-date superscore), scores expire after five years, and the optional essay/writing portion is not required [TAMU-S2]. CDS C7 correspondingly marks standardized test scores only 'Considered' [TAMU-S1]. Practical read for a strong-testing FRC applicant: submitting helps for SCHOLARSHIPS (College of Engineering awards are judged partly on 'merit (GPA and test scores)' [TAMU-S7]) more than it helps for admission. (INFERRED for Fall 2027 — the page reflects the currently open cycle; TAMU has not posted a Fall 2027-specific testing statement.)
admissions.c7_factors_note: CDS 2024-25 C7 [TAMU-S1]. Also marked: geographical residence = important, state residency = important, alumni relation = not_considered, religious affiliation = not_considered. TAMU is the ONLY school in this batch that marks 'Level of applicant's interest' as Considered rather than Not Considered — combined with five 'Very Important' factors (rigor, class rank, GPA, extracurriculars, talent/ability), it has the most demanding C7 profile in the batch. An FRC applicant's competition record maps directly onto the two Very-Important nonacademic factors.

interview.mechanism: No admissions interview (CDS marks Interview 'Not Considered' [TAMU-S1]). TAMU accepts letters of recommendation but 'will consider the first two letters received as part of your admission file' [TAMU-S2]. Because demonstrated interest is 'Considered', campus visits / New Student Conference engagement are the only interest signals available.

first_frc_scholarship.note: NOT VERIFIABLE in this session. No FIRST/FRC-specific award appears on the College of Engineering undergraduate scholarship page or the freshman admissions page reviewed, and the FIRST provider list is behind the portal login [TAMU-S8]. What IS documented and actionable: incoming freshmen apply for College of Engineering scholarships through ApplyTexas or the Common App between Aug 1 and Dec 1; awards are judged on 'merit (GPA and test scores), extracurricular activities, donor specifications, and/or financial need'; a FAFSA is used for the need component; recipients are selected competitively; and 'late or incomplete applications will not be considered' [TAMU-S7]. (The 2.75 minimum cumulative GPR on that page applies to currently enrolled students, not incoming freshmen.)

decision_dates.restrictions: NO Early Decision and NO Early Action for fall entry — this CORRECTS the brief. The published Fall timeline is: Aug 1 application opens (College Station, Galveston, McAllen); Sept 1 acknowledgement emails begin; September decisions begin for Texas top-10% applicants; October decisions begin for holistic-review applicants; DEC 1 application deadline (College Station); Dec 15 deadline for additional required and optional documents; January engineering pathway offers begin; Feb 15 missing-document appeal deadline; February waitlist offers; March final decisions; Apr 1 decision-appeal deadline; MAY 1 deadline to accept and confirm [TAMU-S2]. The Oct 15 date in the brief is the SPRING-term deadline, not a fall EA. TAMU also warns 'Applying early does not guarantee an early decision' and that decisions are made on an ongoing basis. The only genuine early-timing incentive is the Aug 1-Dec 1 College of Engineering scholarship window [TAMU-S7]. Dates are the currently published cycle carried forward (INFERRED — Fall 2027 dates not separately posted; TAMU states 'Dates are subject to change').

Required short answer: 'Describe a life event which you feel has prepared you to be successful in college.'
Required short answer: 'In a few words, what are some of your life goals and objectives?'
Required short answer: 'In a few words, why have you chosen your academic major(s)?' — for a general-engineering applicant this is where the MXET/CSCE ETAM intention should be named explicitly.
Required short answer: 'We know you have a lot of options. In a few words, why did you choose to apply to Texas A&M?' — the why-us slot; 100 words means one specific fact, not a list.
Required short answer: 'Briefly describe any educational plans you have beyond earning your bachelor's degree.'
Optional short answer (TAMU also invites a resume upload for accomplishments that do not fit the application).

why_us_ammunition: MXET — Multidisciplinary Engineering Technology, Mechatronics track, awarded as a BS in MXET; a second STEM Educator track adds secondary-education teacher certification in engineering, math and physical science. Naming MXET (rather than 'robotics') shows the applicant understands A&M's actual degree map [TAMU-S5].

Texas A&M-RELLIS — a dedicated 'Innovation and Technology Campus' hosting Texas A&M System state agencies and 'unique Texas A&M University System facilities', with a RELLIS Academic Alliance; it is the System's autonomy and proving-ground asset [TAMU-S6].

ETAM itself is usable ammunition if framed correctly: the applicant can state the intended ranked list (e.g., MXET, CSCE, MEEN) and the 2.0-cumulative/2.0-term eligibility and three-attempt structure, demonstrating they have read the placement rules rather than assuming a major is guaranteed [TAMU-S4].

College of Engineering scholarships for incoming freshmen are applied for through the same ApplyTexas/Common App submission between Aug 1 and Dec 1, judged on merit, activities and need — an FRC record plus a submitted SAT feeds this directly [TAMU-S7].

TAMU's C7 flags extracurricular activities AND talent/ability as VERY IMPORTANT — one of only two schools in this batch to do so — so a multi-season FRC leadership record is worth more here than at Berkeley or UW [TAMU-S1].

name: University of California, Berkeley
degree_name: BS Electrical Engineering & Computer Sciences (EECS) or BA Computer Science (CDSS)
degree_type: CS degree via EECS (BS) or CS (BA)
program_archetype: B (deep CS + AI) with strong E (large AI ecosystem) and C (robotics) characteristics
major_access_full: MIXED. Direct-admit into EECS (College of Engineering) for first-years. CS BA (CDSS) admits directly into the major; declaration for Fall 2023+ frosh requires only CS 61A/61B/70 with 2.0 GPA (down from 3.30).
recommended_major_route: Apply directly to EECS (College of Engineering) as a first-year for direct-admit into the major.
alternative_route: Apply to CS (BA) in CDSS for more flexibility to combine with other fields.
primary_structural_risk: Scale + teaching capacity — CS 189 ran 857/875 seats in Spring 2026; CS 287 Advanced Robotics requires instructor consent for undergrads; URAP is unpaid.
notable_ai_institute: BAIR (Berkeley AI Research) — 78 affiliated faculty including Pieter Abbeel, Sergey Levine, Trevor Darrell, Ken Goldberg, Anca Dragan, Stuart Russell
notable_undergraduate_research_program: URAP (Undergraduate Research Apprentice Program) — apprenticeships across all schools; new project listings each semester; unpaid, 1 unit per 3 hrs/week up to 4 units/term
fourplusone_name: 5th Year MS in EECS — competitive (typical admit ≈3.88 GPA + 6-12 months of undergrad research); ≥10 units of 200-level EE/CS

sports_influence: Moderate-to-high — NCAA Division I Power-conference, but campus culture is academically dominated
recreation_center: Recreational Sports Facility (RSF) — 100,000+ sq ft with Olympic pool, climbing wall, 7 basketball courts

admissions.admit_rate_note: CDS 2025-26 (Fall 2025): 126,864 first-year applicants, 14,524 admitted, 6,687 enrolled = 11.45% [BERK-S1]. Berkeley's own student-profile page reports 126,843 / 14,502 / 11% for the same cycle [BERK-S2] and OPA Quick Facts reports 126,842 / 14,451 / 6,740 SIRs [BERK-S12] — CONFLICTING at the margin (126,842 vs 126,843 vs 126,864 applicants; 14,451 vs 14,502 vs 14,524 admits) because the three offices freeze counts on different dates; the CDS figure is the citation of record. The NEXT cycle is materially tighter: for Fall 2026 UC reports 133,154 applicants / 13,967 admits = 10.5% [BERK-S3], the lowest rate in the UC system. Berkeley does not publish an in-state vs out-of-state admit split in the CDS ('State applicant data not yet available' [BERK-S1]); UC systemwide policy caps nonresident undergraduate enrollment, so a North Carolina applicant should plan against an effective OOS rate meaningfully below the published ~10-11% headline (INFERRED — no official Berkeley OOS rate is published; do not quote a number).
admissions.major_admit_context: Berkeley admits BY COLLEGE AND BY MAJOR, and EECS is the single hardest undergraduate admit on campus. Berkeley does not publish a major-level admit rate — no official Berkeley or UC page discloses an EECS or Mechanical Engineering first-year admit rate, and every '4-5% EECS' / '10% CoE-ME' figure in circulation traces to admissions-consulting blogs, which are excluded under the source-priority rule. What IS officially documented is the one-way door: for students admitted Fall 2026 and later, changing INTO EECS requires a minimum 3.7 GPA across two of the first four courses drawn from EECS 16A/16B, CS 61A/61B/61C and CS 70, the request must be filed before the start of the 4th term, and it must be the student's first change of major; the parallel ECE path requires a 3.5 overall plus 3.5 technical GPA [BERK-S4]. The EECS department states plainly: 'Because of our competitive admissions process, it is rare for students already admitted to UC Berkeley to change their field of study to EECS,' and since Fall 2017 the College of Engineering has stopped accepting change-of-COLLEGE applications into EECS entirely [BERK-S5]. STRATEGIC CONSEQUENCE: applying to CoE Mechanical Engineering as a robotics back door into EECS is not a viable plan at Berkeley — ME is a legitimate robotics home (and the correct application target if ME is genuinely wanted), but the EECS internal-transfer path should be treated as effectively closed, not as a hedge. Berkeley's separate 'L&S Computer Science' route no longer exists as an open declaration path either; CS is now a capped major.
admissions.gpa_note: CDS 2025-26 C12: average high school GPA 3.90, with 100% of enrolled first-years reporting GPA. C11 distribution: 39.8% at 4.0, 50.1% between 3.75-3.99, 8.1% 3.50-3.74, 1.4% 3.25-3.49 — i.e. ~90% of the enrolled class sits at 3.75+ [BERK-S1]. Berkeley's admissions office separately publishes admitted-student mid-50% ranges of 3.90-4.00 unweighted and 4.36-4.72 weighted [BERK-S2]. Practical read: an unweighted GPA below ~3.85 puts an applicant in the bottom decile of the admitted pool with no test score available to offset it.
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: TEST-FREE (test-blind). Berkeley's CDS 2025-26 C8A, which is filled in for students applying for FALL 2027, marks 'SAT or ACT', 'ACT Only' and 'SAT Only' all as 'Not considered for admission, even if submitted' [BERK-S1]. UC systemwide confirms: 'UC does not consider SAT or ACT test scores when making admissions decisions or awarding scholarships' [BERK-S8]. CONFLICTING internal marking: the same CDS marks C7 'Standardized test scores' as 'Considered', with an adjacent note reading 'We do take into account SAT II Subject Test scores, but we do not take into account regular SAT or ACT scores' [BERK-S1] — a stale artifact (College Board retired SAT Subject Tests in 2021). Treat Berkeley as fully test-free for Fall 2027; a strong SAT is worth zero admissions value here and should be spent on test-required schools instead.

first_frc_scholarship.note: NOT VERIFIABLE in this session. No FIRST/FRC-specific award appears on any UC Berkeley scholarship page reviewed. Additionally, UC does not consider test scores 'or award scholarships' on them [BERK-S8], and Berkeley offers very little non-need merit aid to nonresidents — treat Berkeley as a full-cost OOS assumption.

decision_dates.restrictions: NO Early Decision and NO Early Action anywhere in the UC system. One single UC application is filed once, in the Oct 1 - Nov 30 filing window (application opens Aug 1), and the same application can select up to nine UC campuses at no extra essay cost [BERK-S6]. There is no binding commitment and no application-timing advantage: submitting Oct 2 and submitting Nov 29 are treated identically. rd_notify and deposit_deadline are recorded as null because Berkeley has not published Fall 2027 notification or SIR dates; historically Berkeley releases first-year decisions in late March with a May 1 SIR deadline (INFERRED — prior-cycle pattern, not on any fetched Fall-2027 page).

supplemental_essays.prompt: UC Personal Insight Questions — applicants answer FOUR of eight PIQs. All eight are weighted equally, there is no 'main' essay, and there is no Common App personal essay (UC does not use the Common App). 2026-27 cycle prompts: (1) Describe an example of your leadership experience... (2) Every person has a creative side... describe how you express your creative side. (3) What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? (4) Describe how you have taken advantage of a significant educational opportunity or worked to overcome an educational barrier. (5) Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome it. (6) Think about an academic subject that inspires you. Describe how you have furthered this interest inside and/or outside of the classroom. (7) What have you done to make your school or your community a better place? (8) Beyond what has already been shared, what do you believe makes you a strong candidate for admission to the University of California?

There is NO Berkeley-specific 'why us' supplement. Berkeley receives only the four PIQs plus the activities/awards sections. For a robotics applicant this means PIQ #6 (academic subject that inspires you) and PIQ #3 (greatest talent or skill) are the ONLY places FRC/robotics depth can be argued, and PIQ #6 must carry the technical narrative.

why_us_ammunition: BAIR — Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Research lab, the umbrella for the campus's AI/robotics faculty and the intellectual home of much of modern deep reinforcement learning [BERK-S9].
AUTOLAB — Berkeley's automation-sciences lab (robot grasping, manipulation, cloud robotics, surgical automation), one of the highest-output academic manipulation groups in the world [BERK-S10].
RAIL — Robotic AI & Learning Lab in EECS, focused on robot learning and deep RL for real-world control [BERK-S11].

EECS scale: Berkeley admits ~14.5K first-years out of ~127K applicants and runs the CS 61A/61B/61C sequence at a scale no peer matches — the same sequence that gates the 3.7-GPA EECS change-of-major criterion, so citing it shows the applicant understands Berkeley's actual course architecture [BERK-S1][BERK-S4].

Because Berkeley has no why-us essay, this ammunition belongs in PIQ #6 — name ONE lab and ONE concrete mechanism (e.g., an AUTOLAB manipulation problem the applicant's FRC gripper work maps onto), not a list.

score_notes.cs_foundations: The 35-hour core requires CS 173, 225, 233, 341, 357, 361, 374, and 421 — including a required system-programming and a required numerical-methods course [UI-S5].
score_notes.math_foundations: CS 361 Probability & Statistics for Computer Science and CS 357 Numerical Methods I are both required, plus MATH 257 Linear Algebra with Computational Applications [UI-S5].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: The Intelligence and Big Data focus area holds CS 440, 441, 442, 443, 444, 446, 447, and 448, all of which appeared in the Spring 2026 schedule [UI-S5][UI-S2].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: Six technical electives must all be 400-level with three in one focus area, and 500-level courses (CS 510-546) are permitted substitutions [UI-S5].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: Named undergraduate courses exist for reinforcement learning (CS 443) and trustworthy ML (CS 442), and CS 588 Autonomous Vehicle System Engineering ran in Spring 2026, but no named LLM/agents course was verified [UI-S5][UI-S2].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: Eight focus areas, 18 hours of 400-level electives, and CS+X blends across five colleges — offset by a 128-hour engineering degree structure [UI-S5][UI-S6].
score_notes.course_availability: The Spring 2026 live schedule confirmed actual sections of CS 440, 441, 442, 443, 444, 446, 447, 448, 498, 499, 543, 568, and 588 [UI-S2].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: Six named programs (ISUR, Clare Boothe Luce funding 8 scholars/year, C3SR AI, UR2PhD, DaRin Butz, URSA) plus a research open house each fall and spring, with URSA explicitly for first- and second-years [UI-S9][UI-S14].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: ISUR requires the student to secure a faculty placement before applying, so the model is cold-email-then-formalize, softened by URSA mentor pairing and semesterly open houses [UI-S11][UI-S9].
score_notes.project_based_learning: CS 222 Software Design Lab is core, at least one technical elective must be a team-project course, and CS 448/588 are lab-based [UI-S5][UI-S2].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: No robotics degree or minor; 3 undergrad robotics courses. 4 labs, Center for Autonomy, 2 competition teams.
score_notes.computing_resources: NCSA Delta is the largest x86 GPU resource in the NSF portfolio (including 8 eight-way H200 nodes), but the page documents allocation-based access and no undergraduate or classroom program [UI-S24].
score_notes.industry_preparation: 2024-25 CS outcomes: 372 graduates, 96% secured a first destination, median salary $133,000, median signing bonus $15,500 [UI-S25].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: UR2PhD runs for zero-hour CS 397 credit each fall and spring, CS 499 Senior Thesis is scheduled, and ISUR is a two-semester ≥10 hr/week apprenticeship [UI-S9][UI-S2][UI-S10].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: MCS admission is guaranteed with CS 374 + one of CS 340/341/ECE 391 and a 3.4 CS GPA, though double-counting and funding are not published [UI-S1].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: 9,814 Grainger undergraduates, six named research programs, and a ~1,000-student student-run hackathon in Feb 2026 with $75K+ in prizes [UI-S28][UI-S9][UI-S27].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: Structural internal competition is documented — BS CS is closed to on-campus transfer and the alternative routes publish 3.67 and 3.50 GPA thresholds with portfolios [UI-S3].
score_notes.student_agency: Strong curricular choice (8 focus areas, 500-level substitutions) but almost no ability to switch into BS CS after enrolling [UI-S5][UI-S3][UI-S4].
score_notes.community_within_scale: Against 38,572 undergraduates, the verified small-group structures are course labs, the ISUR ENG 199 seminar, and URSA mentor pairs [UI-S28][UI-S10][UI-S14].

admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2025: 83,045 applicants, 30,384 admitted, 9,207 enrolled = 36.6% [UIUC-S1], the same figure UIUC publishes as its 'Total Admit Rate' [UIUC-S3]. In-state 14,509/29,419 = 49.3%; out-of-state 9,495/32,702 = 29.0%; international 6,380/20,924 = 30.5% [UIUC-S1] (INFERRED - division of CDS C1 counts). A North Carolina applicant faces the 29.0% non-resident rate. Waitlist: 6,826 offered, 4,317 accepted a place, 1 admitted [UIUC-S1] - the waitlist is effectively not a path.
admissions.major_admit_context: UIUC is the most transparent school in this batch about major-level selectivity, and the numbers are stark: against a 36.6% total admit rate, the first-choice-major admit rate is 30.2%, the Grainger College of Engineering rate is 21.2%, and Computer Science alone is 7.4%, with CS+X programs at 17.4% [UIUC-S3]. For comparison, the Division of Exploratory Studies admits 53.4% and Gies Business 20.9% [UIUC-S3]. Applicants name a first-choice and optional second-choice major, and the second choice is a real hedge: a separate essay is required for it [UIUC-S4]. The mobility rules make first-choice selection close to irreversible for computing: Grainger states that students admitted as Engineering Undeclared may declare other engineering majors, but 'Computer Science, Computer Science + Bioengineering, and Computer Science + Physics are not available majors for declaration'; transfer students admitted to a major outside Grainger 'are not eligible to change their major into a major within the Grainger College of Engineering nor Chemical Engineering,' and transfers admitted inside Grainger may only add the ILEE dual degree [UIUC-S7]. Internal moves run through an Inter-Departmental Transfer / Intercollegiate Transfer process handled with an advisor [UIUC-S7]. Practical consequence: a robotics-oriented applicant should pick the engineering major they actually want (e.g. Mechanical Engineering or Electrical/Computer Engineering at 21.2% college-level odds) rather than treating CS at 7.4% as a gateway, and should use the second-choice slot deliberately. One curriculum gate to note: all Grainger Engineering and CS+X majors require 3.5 years of math including trigonometry [UIUC-S6].
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: UIUC offers no Early Decision plan (CDS C21 = No) [UIUC-S1].
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 records a non-restrictive Early Action plan (closing 11/1, notify 1/30) but publishes no EA applicant/admit counts [UIUC-S1].
admissions.test_detail_note: Fall 2025 enrolled: SAT submitted by 42.59% (3,921), ACT by 14.07% (1,295). SAT composite 25th/50th/75th = 1390/1442/1520; ACT 31/32.3/34 [UIUC-S1].
admissions.gpa_note_detail: UIUC leaves CDS C11 (GPA distribution) and C12 (average GPA) blank, so no institution-reported GPA figure is available [UIUC-S1]. Class rank context instead: 61.6% top tenth, 88.8% top quarter, with only 21.7% of enrollees submitting rank [UIUC-S1].
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: TEST-OPTIONAL. CDS C8 for Fall 2027 states scores are 'Not required for admission, but considered if submitted' [UIUC-S1]. The admissions FAQ is emphatic: 'ACT/SAT scores are optional for all first-year applicants,' 'ACT/SAT scores are not required to apply to any major,' review is holistic with or without scores, and test scores are not required for merit scholarships or honors [UIUC-S5]. Two traps: the test-optional election cannot be changed after submission, and if you do not report scores with the application UIUC 'will not accept them later for any enrollment purposes, including course placement or proficiency' [UIUC-S5].

admissions.overall_admit_rate_note: Fall 2025: 76,247 applied / 12,751 admitted / 5,084 enrolled full-time plus 7 part-time. Waitlist: 7,355 offered a place, 5,258 accepted it, 2,099 admitted from it.
admissions.admit_rate_note: IN-STATE vs OUT-OF-STATE: UNC's 2025-26 CDS reports its residency breakdown for Fall 2024 — North Carolina residents 17,846 applied / 6,605 admitted = 37.0%; out-of-state 48,645 applied / 4,685 admitted = 9.6%; international 9,756 applied / 1,461 admitted = 15.0%. UNC's own litigation-disclosure page reports the same pattern: 'The overall acceptance rate was 16.8 percent - 43.1 percent for North Carolina applicants and 8.2 percent for out-of-state applicants.' The driver is statutory-style policy: UNC System Policy 700.1.3 caps nonresidents at 18 percent of the fall first-time undergraduate class at UNC-Chapel Hill, with a State operating budget reduction if exceeded for two consecutive fiscal years — a penalty UNC has actually incurred.
admissions.major_admit_context: The dominant admission constraint at UNC-Chapel Hill is residency, not major. UNC System Policy 700.1.3 states 'The cap shall be 18 percent for Appalachian State University, North Carolina State University at Raleigh, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, University of North Carolina at Charlotte, and University of North Carolina Wilmington', calculated as a percentage of the prior year's first-time undergraduate cohort, and any institution exceeding it for two consecutive fiscal years 'shall have its State operating budget reduced' [UNC-S6]. Because UNC receives roughly 2.7 times more nonresident than resident applications while only 18 percent of seats may go to nonresidents, the out-of-state admit rate collapses to single digits — 9.6% versus 37.0% in-state [UNC-S1]. Consistent with this, CDS C7 rates state residency 'Very Important' — the only school in this set to do so [UNC-S1]. Major selection is comparatively unconstrained: UNC has no undergraduate engineering college, robotics exists as research (the Computational Robotics Research Group in Computer Science) and as coursework such as COMP 581 Introduction to Robotics inside an Applied Sciences and Engineering minor, and data science degrees now sit in the new School of Data and Information Sciences launched July 1, 2026 [UNC-S10][UNC-S11][UNC-S9].
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: UNC-Chapel Hill offers no Early Decision plan (CDS C21 = No).
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 confirms a non-binding, non-restrictive Early Action plan closing October 15 with notification January 31, but UNC publishes no EA application or admit counts.
admissions.pct_submitting_sat_note: 28% of enrolled first-years (1,102 students) submitted SAT scores; 41% (1,945) submitted ACT scores.
admissions.gpa_note: CDS C12 reports an average high school GPA of 4.47 for 89.9% of enrolled first-years — note this is a weighted scale, unlike most schools in this set which report ~3.9 unweighted. CDS C7 rates Academic GPA only 'Important' while rigor of secondary school record is 'Very Important'. Application fee $85.
admissions.test_policy_note: Conditionally required, with a hard score floor — this is the strictest test policy in this set. UNC's CDS marks the Fall 2027 entrance-exam check in the 'Required for some' column, and UNC's first-year application page states: 'For students applying for the 2026-2027 academic year and beyond, students with a weighted GPA of 2.8 or above (on a 4.0 scale) are not required to submit a test score. Students with a weighted GPA below 2.8 (on a 4.0 scale) are required to submit either an ACT score of 17 or higher or an SAT score of 930 or higher.' The CDS adds: 'If applicants have scores that they choose to share with us, they will be considered as one fact among many in our holistic application review.' Latest receipt date January 31.
admissions.c7_note: UNC also marks state residency 'Very Important' and alumni/ae relation 'Considered'. Essays, recommendations, extracurriculars, talent/ability and character are all 'Very Important' — the most writing-and-activity-weighted C7 profile of the nine schools.

robotics_curriculum_detail.score_basis: UNC has no engineering school and no mechanical engineering department, so all robotics teaching sits in Computer Science. Undergraduate-accessible robotics courses are COMP 581 Introduction to Robotics (hands-on; build and program mobile robots; kinematics, actuation, sensing, configuration spaces, control, motion planning; honors version available), COMP 545 Programming Intelligent Physical Systems (embedded control for robots, drones, and autonomous vehicles; feedback controller design), COMP 577 Introduction to Computer Vision (undergraduate-focused perception), and COMP 560 Artificial Intelligence (explicitly includes robotics applications) [UNC-R1]. The deeper robotics courses - COMP 781 Robotics and COMP 782 Motion Planning in Physical and Virtual Worlds - are 700-level graduate courses, and the fetched catalog does not state that undergraduates may enroll [UNC-R1]. There is no robotics degree, minor, or concentration, and no robotics capstone; independent study (COMP 496) is the project route [UNC-R6]. Three to four undergraduate robotics courses = 3.

The CS department's facilities page documents an 800 sq ft dedicated robotics research space inside the Graphics, Imaging, and Robotics Laboratories in Sitterson Hall - Rethink Robotics Baxter with two 7-DOF arms, Aldebaran Nao humanoid, Pioneer P3-DX mobile robot, iRobot Roomba platforms for multi-robot coordination, custom minimally invasive surgical robot prototypes, open mobile-robot space, and ceiling-mounted tracking cameras [UNC-R2]. Named groups: the Computational Robotics Research Group (Prof. Ron Alterovitz - steerable needles, tentacle-like surgical robots, home-assistance robots, motion planning under uncertainty; NSF/NIH funded) [UNC-R3]; the IDEAL Lab, a full-stack robot-learning lab working on humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation, dexterous multi-fingered manipulation, foundation models, and robot hardware [UNC-R4]; and the Interactive Robotics and Novel Technologies Lab (Prof. Daniel Szafir), where a student leads a Boston Dynamics Spot guide-companion project for visually impaired users [UNC-R5]. Undergraduate entry is by contacting PIs for COMP 496/COMP 991 independent study and research [UNC-R6]; lab pages do not publish undergraduate rosters or a formal application program [UNC-R3][UNC-R4]. Student side is one club, Ram Robotics within R.A.M. Engineering, explicitly created because UNC lacks an engineering school [UNC-R7].

admissions.admit_rate_note: CDS 2025-26 (Fall 2025) C1: 90,690 first-year applicants (45,923 M + 44,735 W + 32 unknown), 20,154 admitted (8,704 + 11,449 + 1), 9,900 enrolled = 22.22% [UTA-S1]. UT Austin does not publish a resident/non-resident admit split in the CDS. The structural OOS problem is stated in the CDS itself: under C6 'Other (explain)', UT notes admission is selective for all applicants EXCEPT Texas high school graduates who are automatically admissible under Texas Education Code 51.803 (the top-percentage rule, currently top 6% for UT Austin) [UTA-S1]. Automatic admits consume the great majority of Texas seats before holistic review begins, and state law effectively caps non-resident enrollment near 10% of the entering class — so a North Carolina applicant is competing for a small residual pool at a rate well below the 22% headline (INFERRED — UT publishes no OOS-specific rate; do not quote a number).
admissions.major_admit_context: UT Austin is a DIRECT-ADMIT-TO-MAJOR school: applicants are admitted to a specific major in a specific college, and being denied the first-choice major means being denied or redirected, not held in a general pool. Computer Science sits in the College of Natural Sciences (CNS); Mechanical Engineering sits in the Cockrell School of Engineering. UT DOES NOT PUBLISH major-level admit rates — no official UT page discloses a CS or ME first-year admit rate, and the CDS reports only university totals [UTA-S1]. Two officially documented gates matter more than any rumored rate: (1) COCKRELL CALCULUS READINESS — every Cockrell (engineering, incl. ME) admit must demonstrate calculus readiness via SAT Math >=620, ACT Math >=26, AP Calculus AB or BC score >=3, IB HL Math >=4, or transferred Calculus I credit with a B+ or better [UTA-S5]; a North Carolina FRC applicant should treat SAT Math 620 as a hard floor, not a target. (2) TEXAS ROBOTICS HONORS PROGRAM — this is the one place UT lets a robotics applicant be admitted to robotics FROM HIGH SCHOOL. Applicants apply to one of six eligible majors (Aerospace Engineering, Electrical & Computer Engineering, Computational Engineering, Computer Science, X+CS, or MECHANICAL ENGINEERING), check the 'interested in the robotics program' box, and write one extra ~500-word short answer. Admitted Robotics Honors students get the Robotics Living-Learning Community at Jester West, a GUARANTEED Freshman Research Initiative robotics stream, and a RESERVED seat in the 15-hour Minor in Robotics (gateway RBT 350) [UTA-S4]. Because ME is an eligible feeder major, ME + Robotics Honors is a genuinely coherent robotics application at UT — unlike Berkeley, where the ME-to-EECS path is closed. Also note UT's holistic review changed in 2024: standardized scores 'will not change the admissions decision for automatic admits' but ARE used 'to match applicants to their choice of majors' [UTA-S6] — i.e. at UT, test scores are explicitly a MAJOR-ALLOCATION instrument, which raises the stakes of the SAT for a CS or ME first choice.
admissions.profile_suppression_note: UT Austin LEAVES C9, C10, C11 AND C12 ENTIRELY BLANK in its CDS 2025-26 — no SAT/ACT percentiles, no percent submitting, no class-rank distribution, and no average high school GPA are reported [UTA-S1]. This is a deliberate institutional practice, not a data gap on our side: UT does not publish an admitted- or enrolled-student test or GPA profile through the CDS. Consequence for the dashboard's odds engine: UT Austin CANNOT be classified by the SAT-percentile heuristic and must fall back to admit-rate banding plus the Cockrell SAT Math >=620 readiness floor [UTA-S5]. Any 'UT Austin average SAT' figure found elsewhere is an aggregator estimate and is excluded.
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: TEST REQUIRED. The current freshman application page instructs applicants to 'Send at least one official SAT or ACT score' [UTA-S2], and UT announced in March 2024 that it would 'return to requiring standardized testing scores beginning with applications for the Fall 2025 semester' after suspending the requirement in spring 2020 [UTA-S6]. The Classic Learning Test (CLT) is accepted as an optional additional score, and up to two recommendation letters are accepted [UTA-S2]. For Fall 2027 this is the strongest test-required signal in the batch, and it compounds with the calculus-readiness threshold: for an ME or CS first choice, the SAT is doing double duty (admission + major matching).
admissions.c7_factors_note: UT Austin marks EVERY evaluated factor merely 'Considered' — there is not a single 'Very Important' or 'Important' anywhere in its C7 grid; only interview, alumni relation, religious affiliation and level of applicant's interest are 'Not Considered' [UTA-S1]. Geographical residence and state residency are also only 'Considered'. Interpretation: UT's C7 is uninformative by design (a legally-constrained holistic-review posture under Texas Education Code 51.803), so the C7 heatmap should show UT as a flat row and the odds engine should NOT read this as 'nothing matters' — read the published mechanics (auto-admit percentage rule, required tests, major matching, calculus readiness) instead.

interview.mechanism: No admissions interview; CDS marks Interview 'Not Considered' [UTA-S1]. The Texas Robotics Honors Program adds a written short answer rather than an interview, and runs informational sessions (not evaluative) on Sept 17 and Oct 29, 2026 [UTA-S4].
interview.dates_window: Texas Robotics info sessions: 2026-09-17 and 2026-10-29 (informational only)

first_frc_scholarship.note: NOT VERIFIABLE in this session. No FIRST/FRC-specific award appears on any UT Austin admissions, Cockrell, CNS or Texas Robotics page reviewed; the FIRST provider list is behind the portal login [UTA-S9]. UT Austin's competitive-scholarship consideration is generally tied to applying by the Oct 15 Early Action date [UTA-S2] — that timing, not a robotics-specific award, is the actionable lever.

decision_dates.restrictions: NON-BINDING Early Action (introduced for Fall 2025), not a true restrictive EA and definitely not ED: the Oct 15 EA deadline buys a GUARANTEED decision by Jan 15 with no commitment to enroll, and supplemental materials are due Oct 22. Regular deadline Dec 1 (supplements Dec 10), all decisions by Feb 15, 2027; Honors decisions Mar 1, 2027. Application opens Aug 1; fee $75. Waitlisted (non-auto-admit) applicants may hear from Mar 1 onward [UTA-S2][UTA-S6]. There are no ED-elsewhere prohibitions. Deposit deadline is not published on the fetched pages (null rather than assumed).

supplemental_essays.prompt: Required essay — topic of the applicant's choice; the Common App personal essay satisfies this requirement (500-650 words).

Required short answer 1 — 'Why are you interested in the major you indicated as your first-choice major?' (max 40 lines, roughly 250-300 words). THIS IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE ESSAY IN THIS BATCH: UT admits by major and explicitly uses the application to match applicants to majors, so this answer must justify ME (or CS) specifically, not 'engineering'.
Required short answer 2 — describe the activity or accomplishment the applicant is most proud of (max 40 lines, roughly 250-300 words).
Optional short answer — circumstances that have affected academic performance.

Texas Robotics Honors Program additional short answer (only for applicants who check the robotics-program interest box while applying to one of the six eligible majors, including Mechanical Engineering).

why_us_ammunition: Texas Robotics — 'world-class education and ... innovative research emphasizing long-term autonomy and human-robot interaction while leveraging UT Austin's breadth' — the named organizing unit to cite [UTA-S7].

Texas Robotics Honors Program: Robotics Living-Learning Community at Jester West + guaranteed Freshman Research Initiative robotics stream + reserved seat in the 15-hour Minor in Robotics (RBT 350). A first-year applicant can point to a research placement that is guaranteed on paper, which very few programs offer [UTA-S4].

Named Texas Robotics labs available to undergraduates include the Autonomous Mobile Robotics Laboratory (AMRL — autonomy in real-world unstructured environments), the Center for Autonomy (formal methods + control + learning for verified autonomy), the Advanced Robotic Technologies for Surgery (ARTS) lab, and the Augmenting Human Mechanics (SAHM) lab for wearable assistive robotics [UTA-S7].
UT Computer Science AI Lab / LARG (Learning Agents Research Group) — reinforcement learning and multiagent robot learning, the classic RoboCup lineage [UTA-S8].

Cockrell's calculus-readiness requirement is itself usable ammunition: naming it, and showing an AP Calculus BC score or SAT Math above 620, signals the applicant has read UT's actual engineering requirements [UTA-S5].

admissions.admit_rate_note: CDS 2024-25 (Fall 2024) C1: 31,789 first-year applicants, 20,704 admitted, 4,196 enrolled = 65.13% [UTD-S1]. UTD DOES publish a residency breakdown, and it is the most OOS-friendly picture in this batch: in-state 24,462 applied / 16,907 admitted = 69.1%; OUT-OF-STATE 3,844 applied / 2,415 admitted = 62.8%; international 3,483 / 1,382 = 39.7% [UTD-S1]. The resident/non-resident gap is only ~6 points (versus an 18x gap at UW for CS), and out-of-state applicants make up a small enough pool (3,844) that a North Carolina FRC applicant with strong stats is a genuinely likely admit. Yield is low (4,196 enrolled from 20,704 admits), which is exactly why merit money is used aggressively — see first_frc_scholarship.
admissions.major_admit_context: UT Dallas admits DIRECTLY TO THE INTENDED MAJOR, and its holistic-review criteria explicitly include 'Preparation for and ability to be successful in the intended major' [UTD-S2]. Critically, UTD publishes its capacity-overflow rule in writing: 'Students not admitted into their first choice of major due to capacity constraints or major-specific requirements may be offered admission to a different major as outlined in their acceptance letter' [UTD-S2] — so the downside case at UTD is an alternate-major offer, not a denial, which materially softens the risk of naming a competitive first choice (CS or Mechanical Engineering). UTD publishes no per-major admit rates. Texas residents in the top 10% with the Distinguished Level of Achievement receive automatic admission [UTD-S2]; that does not help a North Carolina applicant but it also does not crowd OOS applicants out the way UT Austin's top-6% rule does, as the residency data above shows. Change of major after enrolling is handled centrally through the Office of Undergraduate Education [UTD-S7]. Class-rank context from the CDS: 39.95% of enrolled first-years were in the top tenth and 69.93% in the top quarter, with 56.67% submitting rank [UTD-S1] — a less rank-compressed class than TAMU's 66.57% top-tenth.
admissions.gpa_note: UTD does NOT report average high school GPA or a GPA distribution — CDS 2024-25 C11/C12 are blank/zero [UTD-S1]. It reports class rank: 39.95% top tenth, 69.93% top quarter, 94.49% top half, 56.67% submitting rank [UTD-S1]. Test detail from C9: 78% submitted SAT (n=3,290), 13% submitted ACT (n=566); SAT composite 25/50/75 = 1170/1280/1390, EBRW 580/630/690, Math 580/650/720; ACT composite 24/28/32 [UTD-S1]. Note the SAT Math distribution: 31.61% of enrolled scored 700-800 in Math [UTD-S1] — the class is math-heavy relative to its overall selectivity, consistent with UTD's engineering/CS concentration.
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: TEST-OPTIONAL, with a documented scholarship asterisk. CDS 2024-25 C8A, completed for FALL 2026 applicants, marks 'SAT or ACT' as 'Not required for admission, but considered if submitted' [UTD-S1], and the application lists 'SAT I or ACT scores, if available' among OPTIONAL supplements [UTD-S2]. BUT the Academic Excellence Scholarship page states that eligibility review includes 'Official high school transcripts. SAT/ACT scores' and that 'Official test scores submitted before the December 1st deadline will be used for AES consideration'; applicants who intend to apply without scores must affirmatively answer 'Yes' to 'I request my application to be reviewed without SAT/ACT scores' on ApplyTexas or the Common App and then supply supplemental materials instead [UTD-S6]. PRACTICAL READ: test-optional for admission, effectively test-advantaged for money. A strong-testing applicant should submit by Dec 1. Separately, Texas state mandate: enrolling students who have not demonstrated college readiness through prior test scores or coursework must take the TSIA2 [UTD-S1]. (INFERRED for Fall 2027 — C8A on the fetched CDS covers the Fall 2026 cycle.)
admissions.c7_factors_note: CDS 2024-25 C7 [UTD-S1]. Also marked NOT CONSIDERED: first generation, alumni relation, geographical residence, STATE RESIDENCY, religious affiliation. UTD is the only school in this batch that marks state residency as Not Considered in C7 — which corroborates the near-parity in the published in-state vs out-of-state admit rates and makes UTD the most residency-neutral of the four public Texas/Florida options here. Note also that UTD is the only school in the batch to mark RECOMMENDATIONS as 'Important', so the (nominally optional) letters are worth submitting.

interview.mechanism: No admissions interview for general admission (CDS marks Interview 'Not Considered' [UTD-S1]). One exception at the scholarship level: Eugene McDermott Scholars Program finalists 'are invited to interview each spring, with approximately 20 Scholars selected annually' [UTD-S5].
interview.dates_window: Eugene McDermott Scholars finalist interviews: spring (scholarship only, not admission)

first_frc_scholarship.application_mechanism: automatic (for the general merit programs below — no separate scholarship application)
first_frc_scholarship.note: No FIRST/FRC-specific award verified at UTD (FIRST provider list is behind the portal login [UTD-S9]). However UTD has the most actionable merit architecture in this batch, all keyed to the SAME Dec 1 priority date: (1) ACADEMIC EXCELLENCE SCHOLARSHIP (AES) — 'Students who complete the application process by the December 1 priority deadline are automatically reviewed... No additional information or scholarship submission is required'; 'The AES Program awards eight funded semesters'; awards are based on grades and achievement trends, curriculum rigor (AP/IB/dual credit), community involvement, leadership, extracurricular distinction, work experience and national recognition; applicants are encouraged (not required) to add an essay, resume and up to three recommendation letters; 'Award criteria and amounts vary with each incoming class' and 'previous years should not set expectations' [UTD-S5][UTD-S6]. (2) AES recipients at ANY award level 'qualify for in-state tuition and fee charges, regardless of their resident status' — for a North Carolina applicant this is the single most valuable published fact about UTD, because it converts non-resident tuition to resident tuition on top of the scholarship [UTD-S6]. (3) Also available: Comet Scholars (merit + significant financial need), Eugene McDermott Scholars (~20/year, finalist interview), National Merit Scholars Program (requires listing UTD first-choice with NMSC by their deadline), Terry Scholars, and a Top 10% Scholarship [UTD-S5]. Exact dollar amounts are NOT published ('amounts vary with each incoming class'), so no figure is asserted here.

decision_dates.restrictions: NO Early Decision and NO Early Action — rolling review instead. Applications (ApplyTexas or Common App) open Aug 1; DEC 1 is the PRIORITY deadline, which triggers early review for BOTH admission and scholarships (including automatic AES consideration); MAY 1 is the regular deadline; later applications are still reviewed but with no guarantee. Application fee $75 [UTD-S3][UTD-S6]. Because Dec 1 controls the money and there is no binding commitment, Dec 1 should be treated as the operative deadline. UTD does not publish fixed notification or deposit dates for rolling decisions (recorded null rather than assumed). Dates are the currently published cycle carried forward (INFERRED — Fall 2027 dates not separately posted).

supplemental_essays.prompt: No required supplemental essay. UTD lists writing as an OPTIONAL supplement: 'an application essay response through Common App', letter(s) of recommendation (maximum three), and a resume [UTD-S4]. However, applicants who choose to be reviewed WITHOUT SAT/ACT scores must supply the selected supplemental materials [UTD-S6], and the AES page 'encourages' the essay/resume/letters for scholarship review — so for a scholarship-seeking applicant the essay is functionally required.
Optional short-answer / supplemental responses and resume upload (used for AES scholarship review and for test-optional applicants).

why_us_ammunition: Erik Jonsson School of Engineering & Computer Science organizes research around five named priority thrusts including advanced manufacturing and energy science, with dedicated Research Centers and Research Institutes plus an explicit First Year Program in the undergraduate structure [UTD-S8].

Dallas-Fort Worth industry adjacency is written into the Jonsson School's own research framing — 'working closely with international academic institutions and the Dallas-Fort Worth area's diverse industry climate' — which is the honest version of the internship/co-op argument [UTD-S8].

The AES in-state-tuition conversion ('Students receiving any level of AES award qualify for in-state tuition and fee charges, regardless of their resident status') is the strongest affordability fact in this batch for a North Carolina applicant and should drive the Dec 1 submission decision [UTD-S6].
UTD's published alternate-major rule means naming a competitive first choice is low-risk: an over-capacity CS application can convert to an offer in another major rather than a denial [UTD-S2].

CAUTION on the Laboratory for Autonomous Robotics and Systems (LARS): both LARS URLs previously in circulation are dead — ecs.utdallas.edu/research/researchlabs/LARS/ is blocked to crawlers and labs.utdallas.edu/syse-lars/ returns 'This site has been archived or suspended.' Do NOT cite LARS as an active lab without confirming with the Jonsson School; use the documented research thrusts/centers page instead [UTD-S8].

admissions.admit_rate_note: CDS 2025-26 (Fall 2025) C1: 72,933 first-year applicants (33,584 M + 39,263 W + 86 unknown), 30,446 admitted (13,032 + 17,369 + 45), 7,129 enrolled = 41.75% admit rate [UW-S1]. UW publishes an explicit residency split (3-year averages): overall Washington residents 47% vs non-residents 39% [UW-S2]. For a North Carolina applicant the 39% non-resident figure is the correct headline — but see major_admit_context, because the university-level number is nearly irrelevant to a CS applicant.
admissions.major_admit_context: UW is the single most extreme major-gating case in this dataset, and the gap is officially published. UW admits first-years through named pathways, and the Allen School's Direct to Major (DTM) pathway for Computer Science / Computer Engineering admits 30% of Washington residents but only 2% of non-residents (3-year averages) [UW-S2]. Direct to College (DTC) Engineering — which covers Mechanical Engineering and the other CoE majors — admits 43% of residents and 37% of non-residents [UW-S2]. So for a North Carolina applicant the same application yields roughly a 2% shot at CS and a ~37% shot at Engineering: an 18x difference. DTM is not a separate application (no extra essay, no computing prerequisites, no coding experience required — the applicant simply lists CS or CE as first-choice major, and UW Admissions reviews it) [UW-S5], which is precisely why it is so oversubscribed. DTC, by contrast, 'guarantees incoming first-year students access to an engineering major' once admitted to the college [UW-S6]. STRATEGIC CONSEQUENCE: for an out-of-state robotics applicant, UW should be treated as an ENGINEERING (DTC) application, not a CS application; listing CS first-choice as a non-resident converts a target-band school into a sub-3% lottery. Note UW's CDS also marks 'Selective admission to some programs' under C6, and marks STATE RESIDENCY as VERY IMPORTANT in C7 [UW-S1] — the only school in this batch to do so.
admissions.gpa_note: CDS 2025-26: average high school GPA 3.84, with 99.87% of enrolled first-years reporting a GPA; distribution 18.12% at 4.0, 58.07% at 3.75-3.99, 18.08% at 3.50-3.74. Class rank is not reported [UW-S1]. UW separately publishes the middle 50% admitted GPA for autumn 2025 as 3.75-3.98 [UW-S2]. SAT detail from C9: composite 25/50/75 = 1320/1440/1502; EBRW 650/710/740; Math 650/730/780; ACT composite 30/32/34; only 19.12% (n=1,364) submitted SAT and 4.89% (n=349) submitted ACT [UW-S1] — the submitting cohort is small and self-selected, so these ranges overstate the typical admit.
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: TEST-OPTIONAL. UW's published deadline table for the current cycle still lists a Dec 31 test-score deadline for applicants who choose to submit [UW-S3], and CDS 2025-26 C7 marks 'Standardized test scores' as NOT CONSIDERED [UW-S1] — a stronger statement than 'optional'. Practical read for Fall 2027: submitting scores is unlikely to help and cannot be relied on to offset GPA (INFERRED for Fall 2027 — UW has not posted a cycle-specific Fall 2027 testing statement; the CDS C7 marking is for the Fall 2025 entering class).
admissions.c7_factors_note: CDS 2025-26 C7 [UW-S1]. Additional markings: STATE RESIDENCY = VERY IMPORTANT (unique in this batch); geographical residence = not_considered; alumni relation = not_considered; religious affiliation = not_considered. C6 'Selective admission to some programs' is checked, which is the CDS acknowledgement of the DTM/DTC gating described above.

interview.mechanism: No admissions interview. CDS C7 marks Interview as Not Considered and recommendations as Not Considered [UW-S1]; there is 'no separate application for Allen School DTM applicants and no additional materials are required' [UW-S5].

first_frc_scholarship.note: NOT VERIFIABLE in this session. No FIRST/FRC-specific award appears on any UW admissions or Allen School page reviewed, and the FIRST scholarship provider list is behind the FIRST portal login [UW-S9]. UW offers essentially no large non-resident merit aid; assume full non-resident cost.

decision_dates.restrictions: NO Early Decision and NO Early Action. One application, one deadline: the UW application opens Aug 15 (Sept 1 per the Allen School's own timeline table) and closes Nov 15; optional test scores must arrive by Dec 31; all first-year decisions — including Allen School DTM decisions, released simultaneously with the university decision — are released Mar 1-15; enrollment is confirmed by May 1 [UW-S3][UW-S5]. Dates above are the currently published cycle carried to Fall 2027 (INFERRED — UW's deadline structure has been stable Nov 15 / Mar 1-15 / May 1 for years, but Fall 2027 dates are not yet separately posted).

supplemental_essays.prompt: Common App personal essay (any of the seven Common App prompts; UW states no prompt preference). This is the ONLY required writing. Response must be at least 250 words and no more than 650 words — the application will reject anything under 250.
OPTIONAL — Common App 'Challenges and Circumstances': explain any unique challenges or circumstances that affected the applicant's educational experience.

OPTIONAL — Common App 'Additional Information': any additional details or qualifications not reflected elsewhere (UW suggests unusual academic progression, course availability issues, or academic work not visible elsewhere).

why_us_ammunition: Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering — but frame it around the DTM/DTC reality: as a non-resident, argue engineering-first with CS coursework, not CS-first [UW-S2][UW-S5].
UW Robotics (robotics.cs.washington.edu) — the campus-wide robotics research umbrella spanning CSE and ME [UW-S7].

Personal Robotics Lab (founded 2006 by Prof. Siddhartha Srinivasa) — assistive manipulation and human-robot interaction; platforms include ADA, an assistive dexterous arm built on a Kinova JACO plus eye-in-hand vision mounted on a powered wheelchair for robot-assisted feeding [UW-S8].

MuSHR (Multi-agent System for non-Holonomic Racing) — an open-source low-cost autonomous racecar platform with 30+ cars in the fleet (Jetson Nano, YDLIDAR, Intel RealSense RGBD, IMU), explicitly designed so 'anyone from high school students to Ph.D. researchers' can do robotics research. This is the single strongest hook for an FRC applicant: it is a documented high-school-to-research on-ramp with hardware an FRC student already understands [UW-S8].
Seattle industry adjacency (Boeing, Microsoft, Amazon) supports the co-op/internship half of a robotics narrative — cite it as access to deployment-scale engineering, not as a name-drop.

Only one flagship competition team was verified (Husky Robotics, 100-120 members, University Rover Challenge finalist, ~8% acceptance rate with 500 applicants for 40 spots) [UW-R8][UW-R9][UW-R14], so the 2+-team requirement for a '5' is not met.
robotics_access_detail.institute_or_center: No university-wide robotics institute verified; Paul G. Allen School robotics group (6 labs + 3,000 sq ft shared robotics lab in CSE2) functions as the hub [UW-R1][UW-R3]
