name: Virginia Tech (Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University)
degree_name: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
degree_type: B.S. in CS with no AI concentration; AI assembled from electives
program_archetype: B (deep CS + AI); partially E (large AI ecosystem, but center is DC-headquartered)
major_access_full: GATED — all engineering first-years enter General Engineering; CS is a restricted major requiring internal change of major
recommended_major_route: Apply to the College of Engineering (General Engineering), then change of major to Computer Science at the earliest review; list CS first among up to three choices
alternative_route: Data-Centric Computing or Secure Computing (same CS department), or Computer Engineering in ECE (which teaches ECE 4424 ML and ECE 4704 Robotics)
primary_structural_risk: CS entry rules are published inconsistently — 2.0 minimum with a 3.0 "guarantee" (College of Engineering page) vs. a flat 3.0 minimum (CS department page), with no published seat count or admit rate
notable_ai_institute: Sanghani Center for Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics (CS dept.; headquartered in the greater Washington, D.C. metro, faculty also in Blacksburg)
notable_undergraduate_research_program: First-Year Fralin Undergraduate Research Fellowship ($1,000, first-years with no prior research experience, faculty-project matching); FURF (15 × $1,350); Fralin SURF
fourplusone_name: Accelerated Undergraduate/Graduate Program
housing_guarantee: First year required and guaranteed (contract due June 1; guarantee suspendable if capacity is exhausted); not guaranteed after year one except for the Corps of Cadets
greek_participation: 18-19% of undergraduates, 5,769 students, 61 chapters, four councils (Spring 2026)
sports_influence: Prominent (Lane Stadium football) — PARTIALLY VERIFIED, no attendance or participation data fetched
recreation_center: McComas Hall (180,000 sq ft) + War Memorial Hall (reopened Sept 6, 2024) + Rec Sports Field House + Venture Out Center, all fee-included
best_fit_reason: A required, AI-capable capstone plus a mandatory Career Bridge Experience, a first-year research fellowship designed for beginners, and genuine 4000/5000-level AI depth including reinforcement learning, deep learning, and NLP. On robotics: Robotics and Mechatronics (RMBT/RBMT) major, plus 11 undergrad robotics courses and 10 labs.
biggest_concern: No AI course in year one, no named AI pathway, NLP graduate-only, no LLM/agents course, robotics only via ECE/ME electives — at out-of-state cost
evidence_confidence: medium (curriculum, entry structure, cost, Greek, housing, and recreation are strongly sourced; outcomes, GPU/computing resources, club variety, and AI student organizations are not)

score_notes.cs_foundations: 123-hour degree requires CS 2505+2506 organization, CS 3114 algorithms, CS 3214 systems, CS 3304 languages, plus a theory elective — a complete classical spine [VT-S2].
score_notes.math_foundations: Requires MATH 2114 linear algebra, MATH 2204 multivariable, MATH 2534 discrete, MATH 3134/3124, plus a statistics elective; no required optimization course [VT-S2].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: Undergraduate courses exist for intro AI (CS 4804), ML (CS 4824), deep learning for vision (CS 4644), creative/generative AI (CS 4644 Creative AI), plus ECE 4424/4524 and CMDA 3654/4654 [VT-S5][VT-S2].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: Real depth exists but sits at the 5000 level — CS 5804 Deep Learning, CS 5824 ML, CS 5844 Reinforcement Learning, CS 5874 Advanced Computer Vision, CS 5894 AI/ML research projects [VT-S5].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: CS 4644 Creative AI is a named generative-AI undergraduate course, but no LLM or AI-agents course appears in the catalog and NLP is graduate-only [VT-S5].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: 7 hours of free electives plus 6 hours of CS 3/4/5XXX and a 3-hour technical elective — better than NC State's 3 free hours, but AI must come out of those slots [VT-S2].
score_notes.course_availability: Course existence* is documented, but the catalog returned three conflicting titles for CS 4644 and inconsistent titles for CS 4604/5644, so live-timetable verification is required [VT-S5][VT-S2].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: First-Year FURF explicitly targets first-years with no research experience, pays $1,000, and matches students to faculty projects (apply Sept 11–Nov 1) [VT-S18]; but CS 4994 research credit requires a 3.0 in-major GPA [VT-S2].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: Structured funding and matching exist [VT-S17][VT-S18], but independent study needs a 2.5/2.5 GPA and research credit a 3.0 in-major GPA, and no lab page listing undergraduate members was verified [VT-S2].
score_notes.project_based_learning: A CS 4XXX capstone is required with 11 named options including Creative Computing Studio and Data-Centric Computing, and ENGE 3900 Career Bridge Experience is a graduation requirement [VT-S2].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: Robotics and Mechatronics (RMBT/RBMT) major (EAC); 11 undergrad robotics courses. 10 labs, Autonomy and Robotics at Virginia, 2 competition teams.
score_notes.computing_resources: No undergraduate GPU/HPC access policy page was fetched this session.
score_notes.industry_preparation: ENGE 3900 makes a documented professional experience mandatory and CS 1944/4944 seminars scaffold it [VT-S2]; institutional outcomes data could not be retrieved [VT-S35].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: 5000-level AI courses are reachable by instructor permission or via the accelerated program [VT-S2], but no verified undergraduate co-authorship or PhD-placement evidence beyond one named Sanghani undergraduate [VT-S7].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: The Accelerated Undergraduate/Graduate Program exists and unlocks 5000-level AI courses at a 3.0 GPA within two semesters of graduating, but double-counted credits, admit rate, and funding are not published [VT-S2].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: VTHacks 12 drew over 850 participants from 50+ universities and VTHacks 13 advertised $30,000 in prizes, free and open to all skill levels [VT-S13]; 450+ students work in Ware Lab design teams [VT-S29].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: The College states "most engineering majors accept students below the GPA guarantees" with only Aerospace and Mechanical unable to do so [VT-S3], but GPA gates recur at 2.5 and 3.0 for independent study, research credit, and graduate courses [VT-S2].
score_notes.student_agency: Independent study (CS 2974/4974) and research (CS 4994) exist but are GPA-gated, and only 6 credits combined count toward the degree [VT-S2].
score_notes.community_within_scale: Mandatory guaranteed first-year on-campus housing [VT-S25], Living-Learning Programs, and a 1,200-1,400-cadet Corps living on the Upper Quad all four years [VT-S30][VT-S32].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: Ware Lab hosts 450+ students in undergraduate design teams and VTHacks is large and current [VT-S29][VT-S13], but no dated AI/ML-specific student organization was verified.
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: No student-organization directory or participation evidence was fetched; only recreation programming (100+ weekly group-exercise classes, intramurals, outdoor trips) is documented [VT-S23][VT-S20b].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: Greek life is 18-19% across 61 chapters [VT-S14][VT-S15], leaving ~80% of undergraduates outside it on a campus with mandatory first-year residency and a 1,400-person Corps [VT-S25][VT-S32].
score_notes.campus_engagement: A required residential first year with a required dining plan [VT-S25] plus 300,000+ annual McComas visits [VT-S24] indicate a full-time residential campus.
score_notes.recreation_facilities: Access is included in the comprehensive fee [VT-S21]; 180,000 sq ft McComas plus War Memorial Hall reopened September 6, 2024 roughly doubling rec space, two 25-yard pools, nine acres of turf, golf and disc golf [VT-S23][VT-S22][VT-S20].
score_notes.daily_life: Blacksburg is a cohesive but isolated small college town, car-dependent and a multi-hour drive from the Research Triangle with no verified convenient air or rail link [VT-S20].

admissions.cds_year_note: NO CDS AVAILABLE. Virginia Tech's Common Data Set page (https://aie.vt.edu/analytics-and-ai/common-data-set.html) renders its file links via JavaScript and every underlying file path tested on 2026-08-16 returned HTTP 404, including the indexed 2025-2026 workbook path and older archived paths; the Internet Archive was unavailable for a fallback. Every CDS-derived field below is therefore null with an explanatory note, and the substitute figures come from Virginia Tech's own admissions and news pages [VT-S1].
admissions.admit_rate_note: (INFERRED - 31,460 offers / 57,700 applicants = 54.5%) from Virginia Tech's fall 2025 census release: 'The 2025 first-year class of 7,088 students came from a record 57,700 applicants' and 'The university extended offers to 31,460 of those applicants' [VT-S7]. Residency split of the admit pool is not published; for enrollment, 4,345 of 7,088 first-year students are Virginians [VT-S7]. In-state vs out-of-state admit rates are n.a. because the CDS is unavailable [VT-S1]. Enrolled first-year average GPA 4.06 [VT-S7].
admissions.major_admit_context: Virginia Tech does not admit first-year students into an engineering major at all: 'When a student applies to Virginia Tech to begin as a first year student, they are applying to the College of Engineering's General Engineering program through the Office of Undergraduate Admissions,' and 'While students can indicate that Computer Science is their intended program, if admitted to the College of Engineering, all freshmen students still have to apply and be admitted to their preferred College of Engineering major after completing the general engineering requirements' [VT-S10]. Neither the College of Engineering nor the CS department has any role in freshman admission [VT-S10]. General Engineering coursework is built around 'the required change of major courses for a restricted engineering degree, which include two semesters of calculus, one semester of English, and two semesters of foundations of engineering' [VT-S11]. The restricted list is broad and includes both target majors: Aerospace and Ocean, Biological Systems, Biomedical, Chemical, Civil, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Construction Engineering and Management, Electrical, Industrial and Systems, Materials Science, Mechanical and Mining Engineering (plus restricted minors in Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, Cybersecurity and Human-Computer Interaction) [VT-S8]. Entry requirements: ENGE 1215 and 1216 (or ENGE 1414), MATH 1225, MATH 1226, ENGL 1105, at least 12 GPA hours, a 2.0 overall VT GPA minimum, with a 3.0 'guarantee' for engineering students and 3.5 for non-engineering students - and the crucial nuance: 'Most engineering majors accept students below the GPA guarantees. In previous application reviews, Aerospace Engineering and Mechanical Engineering were the only programs not able to admit students below the GPA guarantees' [VT-S9]. So MECHANICAL ENGINEERING is effectively the tight door at VT (3.0 in practice), while Computer Science, though formally restricted, has historically admitted students below the guarantee [VT-S9]. Students may rank up to three engineering majors, order is set by application sequence, and change-of-major cycles open in May, August and November - three chances per year [VT-S14][VT-S10]. Two 2026 curricular changes matter for robotics applicants: 'Students can no longer declare Robotics and Mechatronics within Mechanical Engineering as of January 2026' and 'Students can no longer declare Data Centric Computing or Secure Computing within Computer Science as of January 2026,' with affected students moved to the base major [VT-S14]. Practical consequence: apply to VT knowing you enter General Engineering; plan for a 3.0-plus first-year GPA if ME is the goal; and note that the named Robotics and Mechatronics option inside ME is being retired.
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: Virginia Tech's published plans are Early Action and Regular Decision, both non-binding - 'Early Action is a non-binding decision plan' and Regular Decision is 'another non-binding option' [VT-S3]. No ED plan; no plan-level admit rates are published and the CDS is unavailable [VT-S1].
admissions.sat_mid50_note: n.a. - CDS C9 unavailable; no test-score mid-50% range appears on the admissions pages fetched on 2026-08-16 [VT-S1][VT-S4].
admissions.gpa_note: Enrolled first-year students entered with 'an average GPA of 4.06' (fall 2025 census) [VT-S7]. No CDS GPA distribution is available [VT-S1].
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: TEST-OPTIONAL, and locked in far ahead: 'Virginia Tech remain test-optional for first-year applicants entering through Fall 2028' [VT-S4]. Applicants choose whether scores are reviewed; the choice can be changed only before the deadline of the relevant plan (Early Action November 1, Regular Decision January 15); if you indicate test-optional, 'those scores will be ignored by the admissions committee'; scholarships and financial aid are unaffected; scores earned after the last testing window for a plan are not considered; transfer applicants are always reviewed without scores [VT-S4][VT-S5].
admissions.c7_note: All C7 factor ratings are n.a. for Virginia Tech: the Common Data Set files are unreachable as of 2026-08-16 [VT-S1]. What VT does publish about review priorities: the Ut Prosim Profile short answers are 'required for all degree-seeking applicants' [VT-S6], and the test-optional FAQ frames score submission as a personal choice that does not disadvantage applicants [VT-S4]. Do not infer factor weights from third-party sources.

Ut Prosim Profile: 'Have you had an experience when you or someone you know were not being included? Did you reach out to anyone for assistance, direction, or resources? Were you able to affect change and/or influence others? Did this experience change your perspective and if so, how?' (framed by Virginia Tech's Principles of Community)

Ut Prosim Profile: 'Share a time when you were most proud of yourself either as a role model or when you displayed your leadership.' (What specific skills did you contribute? How did others rely on you? What did you learn about yourself?)
Ut Prosim Profile: 'Describe a goal that you have set and the steps you will take to achieve it.' (Why this goal? What is your timeline? Who supports your progress?)

admissions.supplemental_essays_note: The Ut Prosim Profile page (labeled '2025-2026 Short Answer Questions') lists FOUR questions at 120 words each - not three - and states 'The Ut Prosim Profile is required for all degree-seeking applicants' and that responses 'are final and cannot be updated' once submitted [VT-S6]. Re-check the 2026-2027 question set when it posts.
why_us_ammunition: Autonomy and Robotics at Virginia Tech is the umbrella research effort: 'Researchers at Virginia Tech are addressing a wide variety of interdisciplinary challenges in autonomy and robotics' with activities spanning 'water, land, air, and space' and work ranging 'from advances in fundamental theory to novel applications for science, security, and commerce' - including an NSF CAREER award to Dylan Losey to build assistive AI [VT-S12].

The Virginia Tech Transportation Institute is 'one of eight premier research institutes created by Virginia Tech to answer national challenges' and has 'affected public policy on national and international levels' in transportation - the natural home for autonomous-vehicle interests [VT-S13].

Named robotics/autonomy concentrations exist inside Electrical and Computer Engineering ('Controls, Robotics, and Autonomy'), addable after ECE 2804 with a C minimum regardless of GPA [VT-S14] - a real alternative route to robotics if ME is the tight door.

The General Engineering entry model is worth engaging honestly in the Ut Prosim answers: two semesters of foundations of engineering plus calculus before choosing a restricted major [VT-S11], and 'students can change their major once per semester, for a total of three change of major opportunities each academic year' [VT-S10].

Ut Prosim ('That I May Serve') is the explicit evaluative frame - service, inclusion, leadership and goal-setting in 120 words each [VT-S6] - so FIRST outreach, mentoring rookie teams and community demos are exactly the evidence VT asks for.

robotics_credential.notes: Closed to new declarations: "Students can no longer declare Robotics and Mechatronics within Mechanical Engineering as of January 2026. Students already in Robotics and Mechatronics who can graduate by May 2027, nothing changes. Students who cannot graduate by May 2027 will be moved to the Mechanical Engineering Major." (https://eng.vt.edu/undergraduate/resources-support/change-of-major/faqs.html). name: Worcester Polytechnic Institute (WPI)
degree_name: BS in Artificial Intelligence (also BS Computer Science, BS Data Science, BS Robotics Engineering) [WPI-S1][WPI-S9][WPI-S69][WPI-S48]
degree_type: Dedicated standalone AI bachelor's degree with 11 concentrations [WPI-S1]
program_archetype: A (dedicated AI) + C (AI + robotics) — plus an unusually strong project-based character
major_access_full: DIRECT (INFERRED — no published gate) [WPI-S1][WPI-S8]
recommended_major_route: BS Artificial Intelligence, Advanced AI Methods and Technologies concentration [WPI-S1]
alternative_route: BS Computer Science or BS Data Science, both reaching the same 4000-level AI/ML courses [WPI-S9][WPI-S69]
primary_structural_risk: AI major is new (first tracking sheet AY2026-27, Class of 2030) — course rotation and MQP advising capacity unproven [WPI-S4]
notable_ai_institute: Department of Artificial Intelligence [WPI-S3]; PracticePoint (medical cyber-physical systems, surgical robotics, clinical data analytics) [WPI-S73]
notable_undergraduate_research_program: EREE — Early Research Experience in E-Term, $4,500/10 weeks, open to first- and second-years [WPI-S26]
fourplusone_name: WPI BS/MS program; BS/MS in Artificial Intelligence [WPI-S38][WPI-S6]
housing_guarantee: Required and guaranteed for first AND second years (Class of 2030 onward); not guaranteed for juniors/seniors [WPI-S51][WPI-S52]
greek_participation: 26% of men, 25% of women (CDS 2024-25); CONFLICTING third-party figure of 45% of women [WPI-S21][WPI-S37]
sports_influence: Minor (NCAA Division III) [WPI-S35]
recreation_center: Sports & Recreation Center — Mon–Fri 6 a.m.–11 p.m., Sat 8 a.m.–11 p.m., Sun 10 a.m.–11 p.m., with pool [WPI-S33]
best_fit_reason: Genuine undergraduate access to generative-AI, RL, NLP and computer-vision coursework combined with two mandatory faculty-advised team projects and a grading system that rewards academic risk-taking [WPI-S4][WPI-S5][WPI-S12][WPI-S15]. On robotics: a dedicated BS in Robotics Engineering (ABET engineering), with 13 undergrad robotics courses and 15 labs.
biggest_concern: The AI major is one cohort old and the graduate AI courses' rotation and undergraduate-permission rules are unverified [WPI-S4][WPI-S7]
evidence_confidence: Medium-high — curriculum, cost, grading, housing and projects are from official primary sources; course frequency, outcomes data, nonacademic clubs, GPU resources and safety data are unverified

score_notes.cs_foundations: Intro programming, object-oriented design (CS 2102/2103/2119) and CS 2223 Algorithms are required, but computer systems is not required in the AI major and no theory-of-computation course appears in the tracking sheet [WPI-S4].
score_notes.math_foundations: 5/3 units required — MA 1021, MA 1022, MA 2611, MA 2612 and MA 2071/2072 linear algebra — but no multivariable calculus course is named in the AI sheet [WPI-S4].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: Named courses span RL (DS/CS 551), generative AI (DS/CS 552), NLP (DS/CS 554), CV (CS/RBE 549), motion planning (RBE 550), HRI (RBE 526) and edge AI (ECE/CS/DS 556), all permitted toward the BS [WPI-S4][WPI-S5].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: AI Core is 8/3 units with at least two of three units required at 4000-level or above, plus a 6/3-unit concentration and a required 9-credit MQP [WPI-S4][WPI-S12].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: Dedicated courses exist for Generative Artificial Intelligence (DS/CS 552), Responsible AI (DS 555), ML Development & Operations (DS 553) and On-Device Deep Learning (556) [WPI-S5][WPI-S70].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: The 15-unit degree carries 6/3 HUA and a 6/3 concentration, leaving few free electives — though eleven concentrations and normal double-majoring provide steerability [WPI-S4][WPI-S1][WPI-S78].
score_notes.course_availability: Catalog eligibility is explicit, but no term class schedule was reachable and the AI major's first tracking sheet is only AY2026-27, so rotation of DS 552/554/551 is unverified [WPI-S4][WPI-S7].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: EREE pays $4,500 over 10 weeks and is aimed at first- and second-year students with a faculty-matching committee, and the CUR submission states 100% of full-time faculty involve undergraduates in research [WPI-S26][WPI-S14].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: The required 9-credit MQP gives every senior a faculty-advised research project, and A&S research pages name individual undergraduate fellows with their advisors (e.g., a CS+RBE double major with Prof. Whitehill) [WPI-S12][WPI-S27].
score_notes.project_based_learning: Two required 9-credit projects (IQP junior year, MQP senior year), 70% of courses include project activities, 90% complete an off-campus project, 918 off-campus IQPs in 2019-20 [WPI-S11][WPI-S14][WPI-S12].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: BS in Robotics Engineering (EAC); 13 undergrad robotics courses. 15 labs, Robotics Engineering Department, 4 competition teams.
score_notes.computing_resources: No public GPU inventory or undergraduate cluster-access policy was found; PracticePoint provides physical labs rather than compute [WPI-S73][WPI-S74].
score_notes.industry_preparation: Corporate-sponsored MQPs with sponsors including MITRE, Pfizer, Barclays, DraftKings and BNP Paribas, plus PracticePoint members GE Healthcare and Boston Scientific [WPI-S25][WPI-S73].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: Required faculty-advised MQP plus open graduate AI courses are strong ingredients, but no published grad-school destination list or undergraduate publication record was found [WPI-S12][WPI-S44].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: BS/MS in AI exists with up to 12 credits or 40% of the MS double-counted at grade B or higher and a 20% alumni tuition incentive [WPI-S6][WPI-S38].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: Students across five independent threads describe 35–45 hour academic weeks in a collaborative atmosphere, with 91% first-to-second-year retention [WPI-S63][WPI-S59][WPI-S11].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: The registrar awards only A, B, C or NR, and NR does not appear on transcripts or grade reports — removing the mechanical basis for grade competition [WPI-S15][WPI-S11].
score_notes.student_agency: Eleven AI concentrations including "Design Your Own"-style breadth options, HECCMA cross-registration, and student-initiated events like the club-run PLAnt competition with 26 robots [WPI-S1][WPI-S67][WPI-S47].
score_notes.community_within_scale: 93% of first-years live on campus, first- and second-year residency is now required for the Class of 2030, and IQP project centers place 24–28 students abroad with two resident faculty [WPI-S21][WPI-S51][WPI-S12].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: 15 robotics/technology clubs demonstrated at the 2025-09-09 Robotics Clubs Showcase, and the Robotics Club ran its own 26-robot combat event on 2025-09-26 [WPI-S46][WPI-S47].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: No student-organization directory was retrieved in this session; only technical clubs were verified [WPI-S46][WPI-S47].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: Greek participation is high for a tech school (26% of men, 25% of women per CDS) and students report thin Worcester nightlife outside Greek/house parties, though a strong LGBTQ community is also described [WPI-S21][WPI-S59][WPI-S60].
score_notes.campus_engagement: Required first- and second-year residency plus Innovation Studio hours to midnight weeknights and 1 a.m. weekends indicate an evening-active campus [WPI-S51][WPI-S31].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: Sports & Recreation Center opens at 6 a.m. weekdays and closes at 11 p.m. daily, with a pool and posted membership terms [WPI-S33][WPI-S34].
score_notes.daily_life: Campus is 1.5 miles from Union Station with MBTA commuter rail to Boston (~$11.50 each way per students) and free SNAP evening shuttles, but Boston is an hour away and Worcester nightlife is reported as limited [WPI-S55][WPI-S57][WPI-S60].

admissions.overall_admit_rate_note: Fall 2025: 12,355 applied / 7,647 admitted / 1,300 enrolled (CDS C1). Fall 2024 was 60.2% (12,559 / 7,555).
admissions.admit_rate_note_note: WPI's CDS does not publish an in-state vs out-of-state admit split.
admissions.major_admit_context: WPI admits to the university, not to a capped major: applicants indicate an intended major on the Common Application and there is no separate, more selective admission gate for Robotics Engineering. The practical 'direct-admit' benefit is financial rather than academic — WPI states that students who indicate Robotics Engineering as their intended major are automatically considered for Robotics Engineering Scholars awards of typically $10,000-$25,000 per year renewable for four years [WPI-S9]. WPI's Robotics Engineering department describes its BS program as 'first-of-its-kind in the nation and the most comprehensive in the world' [WPI-S10]. Selectivity is instead concentrated in the application plan: Early Decision I admitted 310 of 397 applicants (78.1%) for Fall 2025 versus 69.3% Early Action and 61.9% overall, and ED admits receive a minimum $25,000 scholarship plus a free summer course [WPI-S1][WPI-S3].
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: Fall 2025 ED: 397 applications, 310 admits (CDS C21). Fall 2024: 279 apps / 211 admits.
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: Fall 2025 EA: 8,882 applications, 6,151 admits, 858 enrolled (CDS C22). EA is non-restrictive.
admissions.sat_mid50_note: WPI leaves CDS section C9 blank/'not reported' in both 2024-25 and 2025-26 — no score percentiles are published, consistent with its 2021-2024 test-blind period.
admissions.gpa_note: CDS C12 average high school GPA 3.9, reported for 88% of enrolled first-years; CDS C10 shows 51% in the top tenth of their class. WPI's admissions site states an average GPA of 3.92 and average class rank in the top 9%.
admissions.test_policy_note: CDS C8 marks SAT/ACT 'Not Required for Admission, but Consider if Submitted (Test-Optional)' explicitly for the Fall 2027 cycle. WPI was test-blind 2021-2024 and returned to test-optional beginning with the Class of 2030 (Fall 2026 entry) per a November 2024 faculty Committee on Academic Policy motion; WPI describes it as a 'no-harm' practice and asks on the Common Application whether scores should be considered.

interview.mechanism: No evaluative admissions interview; CDS C7 marks Interview 'Not Considered'. WPI will, however, 'consider Initialview or Vericant interviews if submitted' from international applicants as a supplement to English-proficiency evidence.

first_frc_scholarship.name: WPI Design Innovation Scholarship; WPI FIRST Community Scholarship; FIRST Digital Animation Award (WPI also offers VEX/REC Foundation Aerial Drone awards)
first_frc_scholarship.amount: Design Innovation Scholarship: one full-tuition four-year award (~$220,000) plus three $40,000 awards ($10,000/year). FIRST Community Scholarship: one full-tuition four-year award (~$220,000). FIRST Digital Animation Award: $1,000 scholarship to any student on a submitting team. Full-tuition awards increase as tuition increases.
first_frc_scholarship.application_mechanism: Complete the WPI admissions application by the February 1 Regular Decision deadline, then submit the separate scholarship application form with a signed adult mentor/coach nomination and a video of five minutes or less. Eligibility is limited to FRC, FTC and FIRST Global participants (FLL excluded), one nominee per team per scholarship, final year of high school, active member of the current season's team.
first_frc_scholarship.deadline: For the 2026-27 cycle the applications opened December 15, 2025 and closed February 23, 2026 (11:59 PM EST), with mentor nominations due March 2, 2026, initial offers at the end of March and final notifications April 15, 2026. WPI states applications reopen in Fall 2026 for the next cycle.

why_us_ammunition: WPI's Robotics Engineering department calls its program 'first-of-its-kind in the nation and the most comprehensive in the world', and it offers a dedicated Robotics Engineering BS [WPI-S10].
The Major Qualifying Project (MQP) is a capstone in which robotics students complete professional-level design work in their major — a concrete hook for project-based applicants [WPI-S11].

PracticePoint, WPI's medical-device and robotics prototyping/validation facility, opened in January 2020 with a $5 million MassTech matching grant and gives undergraduates access to industry-grade healthcare-robotics infrastructure [WPI-S12].

WPI states it 'is proud to have been the inaugural university to offer a FIRST scholarship starting in 1996' — a directly citable link between an FRC applicant's background and WPI's institutional history [WPI-S9].
Intended Robotics Engineering majors are automatically considered for Robotics Engineering Scholars awards, typically $10,000-$25,000 per year renewable for four years [WPI-S9].
